children.translated_text: When men were devoted solely to <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) and were truthful,

children.text: tadā na vyavahāro 'bhūn na dveṣo nāpi matsaraḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: then there was no legal dispute, no hatred, and no jealousy. || 1 ||
When <s>Dharma</s> declined among men, legal procedure (<s>vyavahāra</s>) came into practice,

children.text: draṣṭā ca vyavahārāṇāṃ rājā daṇḍadharaḥ kṛtaḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: and the king, bearing the rod of punishment, was appointed as the arbiter of disputes. || 2 ||

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś cātra dvau vidhī samprakīrtitau |
children.translated_text: Documents and witnesses — these two modes of proof are proclaimed here,
for the purpose of resolving doubtful matters between two disputing parties. || 3 ||
A lawsuit is known to be of two kinds: with a reply and without a reply;
that which has a reply is superior, where the wager is preceded by a written document. || 4 ||

children.text: vivāde sottarapaṇe dvayor yas tatra hīyate |
children.translated_text: In a dispute with a counter-wager, whichever of the two parties is defeated therein,

children.text: sa paṇaṃ svakṛtaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ ca parājaye || 5 ||
children.translated_text: that one shall be made to pay the wager he himself made, and a fine upon defeat. || 5 ||
The essence of legal proceedings is declared to be the plaint (<s>pratijñā</s>);

children.text: taddhānau hīyate vādī taraṃs tām uttaro bhavet || 6 ||
children.translated_text: if that is lost, the plaintiff fails; one who overcomes it becomes the successful respondent. || 6 ||

children.text: kulāni śreṇayaś caiva gaṇāś cādhikṛto nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Families, guilds, corporations, and the appointed king —
these are the authorities for legal proceedings, each subsequent one being superior to the preceding. || 7 ||

children.text: sa catuṣpāc catuḥsthānaś catuḥsādhana eva ca |
children.translated_text: It (<s>vyavahāra</s>) has four feet, four seats, four means of accomplishment,
four benefits, four extensions, and four actions — so it is declared. || 8 ||
It has eight limbs, eighteen titles, and a hundred branches;

children.text: triyonir dvyabhiyogaś ca dvidvāro dvigatis tathā || 9 ||
children.translated_text: it has three sources, two kinds of accusations, two doors, and two outcomes. || 9 ||

children.text: dharmaś ca vyavahāraś ca caritraṃ rājaśāsanam |

children.translated_text: these are the four feet of legal procedure, each subsequent one overriding the preceding. || 10 ||

children.text: tatra satye sthito dharmo vyavahāras tu sākṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: Of these, <s>Dharma</s> is established in truth, <s>vyavahāra</s> rests on witnesses,
<s>caritra</s> (custom) on written records, and <s>śāsana</s> (edict) on royal command. || 11 ||
It is called 'having four means' because it is to be accomplished through <s>sāma</s> (conciliation) and the other expedients;

children.text: caturṇām āśramāṇāṃ ca rakṣaṇāt sa caturhitaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: it is 'four-benefiting' because it protects the four <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life). || 12 ||

children.text: kartṝn atho sākṣiṇaś ca sabhyān rājānam eva ca |
children.translated_text: It extends to the litigants, witnesses, assessors, and the king,

children.text: vyāpnoti pādaśo yasmāc caturvyāpī tataḥ smṛtaḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: pervading each quarter by quarter — therefore it is called 'four-pervading.' || 13 ||
because it produces these four, it is declared to be 'four-acting.' || 14 ||
The king, his officers, the assessors, the law book, the accountant and scribe,

children.text: hiraṇyam agnir udakam aṣṭāṅgaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: gold, fire, and water — it is said to have these eight limbs. || 15 ||

children.text: ṛṇādānaṃ hy upanidhiḥ sambhūya-utthānam eva ca |

children.translated_text: resumption of a gift, and breach of service after an agreement; || 16 ||
Non-payment of wages, sale by a non-owner,
non-delivery after sale, and rescission after purchase; || 17 ||
Breach of a compact, disputes concerning boundaries,
the relations between man and woman, partition of inheritance, and violence; || 18 ||
Verbal assault and physical assault are likewise declared,
gambling and miscellaneous — thus it is said to have eighteen titles. || 19 ||

children.text: eṣām eva prabhedo 'nyaḥ śatam aṣṭa.uttaraṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: A further subdivision of these, numbering one hundred and eight, is recognized;
because of the diversity of human activities, it is said to have a hundred branches. || 20 ||

children.text: kāmāt krodhāc ca lobhāc ca tribhyo yasmāt pravartate |
children.translated_text: Since it arises from these three — desire, anger, and greed —

children.text: triyoniḥ kīrtyate tena trayam etad vivādakṛt || 21 ||
children.translated_text: it is called 'three-sourced'; these three are the causes of disputes. || 21 ||
The two kinds of accusation should be known: based on suspicion and based on fact;
suspicion arises from association with the wicked, fact from seeing stolen goods and the like. || 22 ||
Because it involves two sides, it is said to have two doors;
of these two, the plaint is the first side, and the reply is the counter-side. || 23 ||
Because it follows either truth or fraud, it is said to have two courses;
truth is that which accords with the real facts, and fraud is that which is stated through carelessness or deceit. || 24 ||

children.text: tatra śiṣṭaṃ chalaṃ rājā marṣayed dharmasādhanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of these, the king who upholds <s>Dharma</s> should overlook learned fraud,

children.text: bhūtam eva prapadyeta dharmamūlā yataḥ śriyaḥ || 25 ||
children.translated_text: and should follow truth alone, for prosperity is rooted in <s>Dharma</s>. || 25 ||
When a self-controlled king adjudicates legal cases in accordance with <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: sambhavanti guṇāḥ sapta sapta vahner ivārciṣaḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: seven virtues arise, like the seven flames of fire. || 26 ||

children.text: dharmaś cārthaś ca kīrtiś ca lokapaktir upagrahaḥ |
prajābhyo bahumānaś ca svarge sthānaṃ ca śāśvatam || 27 ||
children.translated_text: respect from subjects, and an eternal place in heaven. || 27 ||
Therefore, having ascended the seat of justice, the king, free from jealousy,

children.text:
samaḥ syāt sarvabhūteṣu bibhrad vaivasvataṃ vratam || 28
                            ||
children.translated_text: should be impartial toward all beings, observing the vow of <s>Vaivasvata</s> (Yama). || 28 ||
Keeping the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> (legal treatise) foremost, abiding by the opinion of the chief judge,
with a composed mind he should examine legal cases in due order. || 29 ||
First the formal plaint should be made, then the title of law;

children.text: vivitsā nirṇayaś caiva darśanaṃ syāc caturvidham || 30 ||
children.translated_text: inquiry and decision — thus the trial is fourfold. || 30 ||
In conformity with both the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> and the <s>Arthaśāstra</s>, by the proper method,
examining carefully, one should guide the course of legal proceedings. || 31 ||

children.text: yathā mṛgasya viddhasya vyādho mṛgapadaṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: Just as a hunter traces the track of a wounded deer,
through the thicket by drops of blood, so should one trace the path of <s>Dharma</s>. || 32 ||
Where there is a conflict between the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> and the <s>Arthaśāstra</s>,
one should set aside what is stated in the <s>Arthaśāstra</s> and follow what is stated in the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>. || 33 ||
But when there is a conflict with the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, even what is supported by reasoning, from the standpoint of <s>Dharma</s>,
legal procedure is indeed powerful, and by it <s>Dharma</s> may be overridden. || 34 ||

children.text: sūkṣmo hi bhagavān dharmaḥ parokṣo durvicāraṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: For the venerable <s>Dharma</s> is subtle, invisible, and difficult to ascertain;
therefore one should guide the course of legal proceedings by the path of visible evidence. || 35 ||

children.text: yāty acauro 'pi cauratvaṃ cauraś cāyāty acauratām |
children.translated_text: Even an innocent person may be convicted as a thief, and a thief may be acquitted;
<s>Māṇḍavya</s>, though innocent, was convicted as a thief through legal procedure. || 36 ||

children.text: strīṣu rātrau bahir grāmād antarveśmany arātiṣu |
children.translated_text: In cases involving women, at night, outside the village, inside the house, or with enemies —

children.text: vyavahāraḥ kṛto 'py eṣu punaḥ kartavyatām iyāt || 37 ||
children.translated_text: legal proceedings conducted even in these circumstances may be subject to retrial. || 37 ||
Because of the complexity of disputes and the limitations of memory,
in cases of debts and the like, one may take as much time as needed in the desire to ascertain the truth. || 38 ||
In matters concerning cattle, land, gold, women, theft, assault, and urgent cases,

children.text: sāhaseṣv abhiśāpe ca sadya eva vivādayet || 39 ||
children.translated_text: in cases of violence and false accusation, the dispute should be settled immediately. || 39 ||

children.text: anāvedya tu yo rājñe sandigdhe 'rthe pravartate |
children.translated_text: One who acts in a doubtful matter without informing the king,

children.text: prasahya sa vineyaḥ syāt sa cāsyārtho na sidhyati || 40 ||
children.translated_text: shall be punished forcibly, and his claim shall not succeed. || 40 ||

children.text: vaktavye 'rthe na tiṣṭhantam utkrāmantaṃ ca tadvacaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who does not stand by the matter to be stated, or who departs from his own statement —
the plaintiff should restrain him until the summons is presented. || 41 ||
Restraint may be of four kinds: based on place, based on time, based on travel, and based on occupation;

children.text: caturvidhaḥ syād āsedho nāsiddhas taṃ vilaṅghayet || 42 ||
children.translated_text: the restraining order is fourfold, and one who is not restrained should not violate it. || 42 ||
In cases of rivers, river-crossings, wilderness, difficult terrain, or calamities,
one who is restrained but crosses beyond the restraining boundary due to such causes does not offend. || 43 ||
One who is restrained during the period of restraint and yet violates the restraining order —

children.text:
sa vineyo 'nyathā kurvann āseddhā daṇḍabhāg bhavet || 44
                            ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished; if he acts otherwise, the restrainer shall be liable to penalty. || 44 ||
One who desires to discharge a debt, one afflicted by disease, one about to undertake a sacrifice, one in calamity,
one who is already charged by another, and one engaged in royal service — || 45 ||
Cowherds during the grazing of cattle, farmers at the time of harvest,

children.text: śilpinaḥ cāpi tatkālam āyudhīyāś ca vigrahe || 46 ||
children.translated_text: artisans during that same period, and soldiers during war — || 46 ||
one who has not yet reached the age for litigation, a messenger, one engaged in giving gifts, an ascetic observing vows,

children.text: viṣamasthaś ca nāsedhyo na ca-enān āhvayen nṛpaḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: and one in distress — these should not be restrained, nor should the king summon them. || 47 ||
One who is not himself charged should not bring a charge against another while his own case is pending;

children.text: na cābhiyuktam anyena na viddhaṃ veddhum arhati || 48 ||
children.translated_text: nor should one who is already charged by another be charged again, nor should a wounded person be struck again. || 48 ||

children.text: yam artham abhiyuñjīta na taṃ viprakṛtiṃ nayet |
children.translated_text: The matter on which one brings a charge, that he should not alter;

children.text:
nānyat pakṣāntaraṃ gacched gacchan pūrvāt sa hīyate || 49
                            ||
children.translated_text: nor should he shift to a different plea; if he does so, he forfeits the original claim. || 49 ||
One should not bring a false charge; the fault falls on the false accuser;

children.text: yas tatra vinayaḥ proktaḥ so 'bhiyoktāram āvrajet || 50 ||
children.translated_text: the penalty prescribed for that offense shall befall the accuser himself. || 50 ||

children.text: sāpadeśaṃ haran kālam abruvaṃś cāpi saṃsadi |
children.translated_text: Delaying with pretexts, remaining silent in the assembly,

children.text: uktvā vaco vibruvaṃś ca hīyamānasya lakṣaṇam || 51 ||
children.translated_text: and contradicting what was said — these are the marks of one who is losing his case. || 51 ||

children.text: palāyate ya āhūtaḥ prāptaś ca vivaden na yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who flees when summoned, and one who, having arrived, does not contest —

children.text: vineyaḥ sa bhaved rājñā hīna eva sa vādataḥ || 52 ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished by the king; he is deemed to have lost the case. || 52 ||
In cases already adjudicated, evidence is of no effect,

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo vāpi pūrvam āveditaṃ na cet || 53 ||
children.translated_text: whether documents or witnesses, if they were not previously presented. || 53 ||

children.text: yathā pakveṣu dhānyeṣu niṣphalāḥ prāvṛṣo guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as the virtues of the rainy season are fruitless when the grain is already ripe,
so too is evidence fruitless in cases already adjudicated. || 54 ||
Even what is untrue, if stated at the proper time, is examined;

children.text: yat tu pramādān na-ucyeta tad bhūtam api hīyate || 55 ||
children.translated_text: but what is not stated through negligence, even if true, is forfeited. || 55 ||

children.text: tīritaṃ cānuśiṣṭaṃ ca yo manyeta vidharmataḥ |
children.translated_text: One who considers a decided and instructed case to be unjust,

children.text: dviguṇaṃ daṇḍam āsthāya tat kāryaṃ punar uddharet || 56 ||
children.translated_text: may reopen that case by undertaking double the penalty. || 56 ||

children.text: durdṛṣṭe vyavahāre tu sabhyās taṃ daṇḍam āpnuyuḥ |
children.translated_text: But in a case wrongly decided, the assessors shall incur that penalty;

children.text: na hi jātu vinā daṇḍaṃ kaścin mārge 'vatiṣṭhate || 57 ||
children.translated_text: for indeed no one ever stays on the right path without the threat of punishment. || 57 ||

children.text: rāgād ajñānato vāpi lobhād vā yo 'nyathā vadet |
children.translated_text: An assessor who speaks falsely, whether from passion, ignorance, or greed,

children.text:
sabhyo 'sabhyaḥ sa vijñeyas taṃ rājā vinayed bhṛśam || 58
                            ||
children.translated_text: that assessor is to be considered unfit; the king should punish him severely. || 58 ||
But the king, especially while guarding his own <s>Dharma</s>,
should examine the virtue and vice of people, given the diversity of human minds. || 59 ||

children.text: puruṣāḥ santi ye lobhāt prabrūyuḥ sākṣyam anyathā |
children.translated_text: There are men who, out of greed, would give false testimony,
and there are other wicked people who forge false documents. || 60 ||

children.text: ataḥ parīkṣyam ubhayam etad rājñā viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore both of these should be examined by the king with special care:
documents written according to the rules of documentation, and witnesses according to the rules of testimony. || 61 ||
False things appear as if true, and true things appear as if false;

children.text: dṛśyante vividhā bhāvās tasmād yuktaṃ parīkṣaṇam || 62 ||
children.translated_text: various states of affairs are seen, therefore examination is proper. || 62 ||

children.text: talavad dṛśyate vyoma khadyoto havyavāḍ iva |
children.translated_text: The sky appears as if it has a surface, and a firefly appears like a sacrificial fire;

children.text: na talaṃ vidyate vyomni na khadyote hutāśanaḥ || 63 ||
children.translated_text: yet there is no surface in the sky, nor is there a conflagration in a firefly. || 63 ||
Therefore, even a matter seen with one's own eyes is proper to be examined;

children.text: parīkṣya jñāpayan arthān na dharmāt parihīyate || 64 ||
children.translated_text: by examining and then making known the facts, one does not fall from <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). || 64 ||

children.text: evaṃ paśyan sadā rājā vyavahārān samāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus the king, always observing lawsuits with concentration,
having spread brilliant fame here, attains the realm of <s>Bradhna</s> (the Sun). || 65 ||
The plaintiff, whose firm basis of strength is well-established, impelled by his own interest,
should have the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (plaint) written down, having determined his case. ||
The defendant, having heard the substance of the plaint, thereafter
should present the <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-plea), connected with the substance of the plaint. ||

children.text: śvo lekhanaṃ vā sa labhet tryahaṃ saptāham eva vā |
children.translated_text: He may obtain a day for writing, or three days, or even seven days;

children.text: arthī tṛtīyapāde tu yuktaṃ sadyo dhruvaṃ jayī ||
children.translated_text: but if the plaintiff proves his case in the third stage, he is certainly and immediately the victor. ||

children.text: mithyā sampratipattir vā pratyavaskandam eva vā |

children.translated_text: or a plea based on a former judgment -- the reply is fourfold. ||

children.text: mithyaitan nābhijānāmi tadā tatra na sannidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: "This is false," "I do not know," "I was not present there at that time,"

children.text: ajātaś cāsmi tatkāla evaṃ mithyā caturvidhā ||
children.translated_text: "I was not yet born at that time" -- thus denial is fourfold. ||

children.text: mithyā ca viparītaṃ ca punaḥ śabdasamāgamam |
children.translated_text: Denial, and contradiction, and again, verbal agreement,
and connection with the substance of the plaint -- the reply is fourfold. ||

children.text: bhāṣāyā uttaraṃ yāvat pratyarthī na niveśayet |
children.translated_text: Until the defendant presents his reply to the plaint,

children.text: arthī tu lekhayet tāvad yāvad vastu vivakṣitam ||
children.translated_text: the plaintiff may continue to write as much of the matter as he wishes to state. ||
Concerning another matter, devoid of substance, lacking evidence and authority,
deficient, excessive, or damaged in writing -- these are declared to be defects of a plaint. ||

children.text: labdhavyaṃ yena yad yasmāt sa tat tasmād avāpnuyāt |
children.translated_text: Whatever is to be obtained, by whom, and from whom -- he should obtain that from that person;

children.text:
na tv anyo 'nyad athānyasmād ity anyārtham idaṃ tridhā || J
                            edn Mā 2.9 ||
children.translated_text: but not another person, nor another thing, nor from another -- thus "concerning another matter" is threefold. || J edn Mā 2.9 ||
"Even in my mind I have been thought of by your friend here as an enemy;
otherwise, out of great forbearance, you have been brought here by me." ||
That which is devoid of specification of the thing claimed and lacks a basis for the remedy --
that is called a defect of the written document, lacking evidence, and should be rejected. ||
The defect of lacking authority should be avoided in the first stage of the plaint;
likewise when one person's case conflicts with many or with the city and realm. ||
In dots, syllables, words, and letters, with a single discrepancy (?),

children.text: hīnādhikā bhaved vyarthā tāṃ yatnena vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: the plaint becomes deficient or excessive and useless; one should carefully avoid that. ||

children.text: bhraṣṭaṃ tu duḥsthitaṃ yat syāj jalatailādibhir hatam |
children.translated_text: That which is damaged, ill-placed, or ruined by water, oil, and such --

children.text: bhāṣāyāṃ tad api spaṣṭaṃ vispaṣṭārthaṃ vivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: even if the plaint is clear in meaning, one should reject what is of very unclear meaning. ||

children.text: satyā bhāṣā na bhavati yady api syāt pratiṣṭhitā |
children.translated_text: A plaint does not become true even if it is well-established,

children.text: bahiś ced bhraśyate dharmān niyatād vyavahārikāt ||
children.translated_text: if it falls outside the established rules of legal procedure. ||
"That was entrusted by me to him while he was residing on <s>Gandhamādana</s>" --
being outside the scope of legal procedure, this does not succeed. ||
By insertion of other letters and by leading to a different meaning,

children.text: ākulaṃ ca kriyādānaṃ kriyā caivākulā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the offering of evidence becomes confused, and the legal procedure itself becomes confused. ||

children.text: rāgādīnāṃ yad ekena kopitaḥ karaṇe vadet |
children.translated_text: Whatever one who is agitated by passion and the like says during the proceedings,

children.text: tad ādau tu likhet sarvaṃ vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: all of that should first be written down on the litigant's board and other records. ||
For the sake of clear comprehension, well-deliberated by the judges,

children.text: tasmād anyad vyapohyaṃ syād vādinaḥ phalakādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: whatever else should be removed from the litigant's board and other records. ||

children.text: vādibhyām abhyanujñātaṃ śeṣaṃ ca phalake sthitam |
children.translated_text: What remains, approved by both litigants, and what stands on the board --

children.text: sasākṣikaṃ likheyus te pratipattiṃ ca vādinoḥ ||
children.translated_text: they should write that down with witnesses, along with the statements of both litigants. ||

children.text: vādibhyāṃ likhitāc cheṣaṃ yat punar vādinā smṛtam |
children.translated_text: Whatever beyond what was written by both litigants is later recalled by a litigant --

children.text: tat pratyākalitaṃ nāma svapāde tasya likhyate ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>pratyākalita</s> (subsequently recalled) and is written in his own section. ||
Whether appointed by the plaintiff or sent by the defendant,
whoever litigates on behalf of another -- victory and defeat belong to those two principals. ||

children.text: yo na bhrātā na ca pitā na putro na niyogakṛt |
children.translated_text: He who is neither a brother, nor a father, nor a son, nor an appointed agent,
who speaks on behalf of another in a lawsuit, should be punished even while so pleading. ||
He who abandons the former plea and again takes up another --

children.text: vādasaṅkramaṇāj jñeyo hīnavādī sa vai naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: through shifting of his plea, that man should be known as one whose suit has failed. ||
In all disputes, one does not lose through a quibble of words;
in cases concerning cattle, women, land, and debts, even one who is punished does not lose his claim. ||
If the accused denies the accusation,

children.text: abhiyoktā diśed deśyaṃ pratyavaskandito na cet ||
children.translated_text: the accuser should present evidence, unless a special plea has been entered. ||
What has been written in the first stage, verbatim and in full --
the plaintiff in the third stage should establish it through proof. ||

children.text: kriyāpi dvividhā proktā mānuṣī daivikī tathā |
children.translated_text: Proof is also declared to be twofold: human and divine;
human proof is through documents and witnesses; the ordeal by balance and such is considered divine. ||

children.text: divā kṛte kāryavidhau grāmeṣu nagareṣu vā |
children.translated_text: When the legal matter was done during the day, in villages or in cities,

children.text: sambhave sākṣiṇāṃ caiva divyā na bhavati kriyā ||
children.translated_text: and where witnesses are available, the divine proof does not apply. ||
In a forest, in a deserted place, at night, inside a house, or in a case of violence,
and also in the denial of a deposit -- the divine proof applies. ||
When the plaint is contradicted through a plea of justification,
the burden of proof lies with the accused, and it should be understood as equivalent to the plaint. ||
He who flees when summoned, he who remains silent, he who is defeated by witnesses,
he who has himself confessed, and he who has failed in his case -- these are the four types of the defeated. ||
He who speaks on another matter, he who evades the proof, he who does not appear, he who gives no answer,
and he who flees when summoned -- the defeated party is declared to be of five kinds. ||
Gems such as rubies and the like, gold coins and other golden objects,
pearls, corals, conches, and the like -- when found to be defective, they revert to the owner. ||

children.text: gandhamālyam adattaṃ tu bhūṣaṇaṃ vāsa eva vā |
children.translated_text: Perfume, garlands not given as gift, ornaments, or clothing,

children.text: pādukā-iti rājā-uktaṃ tad ākrāman vadham arhati ||
children.translated_text: or sandals -- these are declared by the king; whoever treads upon them deserves death. ||

children.text: paṇyamūlyaṃ bhṛtir nyāso daṇḍo yac cāvahārakam |
children.translated_text: The price of goods, wages, a deposit, a fine, and whatever is a surcharge --
gratuitous gifts, gambling stakes, and wagers do not accrue interest when not intended. ||
Those of <s>Śūdra</s> birth who bring false accusations against <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (twice-born) --

children.text: teṣāṃ jihvāṃ samutkṛtya rājā śūle vidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: the king should have their tongues cut out and impale them on a stake. ||
A royal decree, a written document, a charter, or an edict,

children.text:
ādhiḥ pattraṃ vikrayo vā
                            krayo vā |
children.translated_text: a mortgage, a deed, a sale, or a purchase --
whoever first makes a representation to the king,
his plaint should be recognized by those learned in the law. ||
When witnesses are challenged, the prior witnesses must first be examined for credibility;

children.text: śuddheṣu sākṣiṣu tataḥ paścāt sākṣyaṃ viśodhayet ||
children.translated_text: once the witnesses are found to be pure, then afterward the testimony should be examined. ||
For those defeated by witnesses or assessors, a re-examination is possible upon challenge;
but for those defeated by their own conduct, there is no procedure for a second trial. ||
Even one who has himself confessed, or one defeated by his own conduct,
or even one defeated by proof, may still be entitled to a final determination by the assessors. ||

children.text: pakṣān utsārya kāryas tu sabhyaiḥ kāryaviniścayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having removed the parties, the assessors should determine the case;
if the verdict is rendered without removing the parties, there is sin both hereafter and in this world. ||

children.text: sabhair eva jitaḥ paścād rājñā śāsyaḥ svaśāstrataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who has been defeated by the assessors should afterward be punished by the king according to the law;

children.text: jayine cāpi deyaṃ syād yathāvaj jayapatrakam ||
children.translated_text: and to the victor should be given a decree of victory as is proper. ||
This introductory procedure of lawsuits was formerly declared by the Self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>);

children.text: mukhaśuddhau hi śuddhiḥ syād vyavahārasya nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: for only when the introduction is pure is the lawsuit itself pure, and not otherwise. ||
One who is not appointed should never speak in a lawsuit;
but one who is appointed should speak words free from partiality. || 1 ||
An assessor speaking what is fitting does not incur the sins of hatred;

children.text:
bruvāṇas tv anyathā sabhyas tad eva-ubhayam āpnuyāt || 2
                            ||
children.translated_text: but an assessor speaking otherwise would incur both of those. || 2 ||

children.text: rājā tu dhārmikān sabhyān niyuñjyāt suparīkṣitān |
children.translated_text: The king should appoint as assessors righteous men who have been well-examined,

children.text: vyavahāradhuraṃ voḍhuṃ ye śaktāḥ sadgavā iva || 3 ||
children.translated_text: who are capable of bearing the yoke of legal proceedings, like good oxen. || 3 ||
Skilled in the meaning of the <s>dharmaśāstra</s> (legal texts), of good family, truthful in speech,

children.text: samāḥ śatrau ca mitre ca nṛpateḥ syuḥ sabhāsadaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: impartial toward enemies and friends alike -- such should be the king's court assessors. || 4 ||

children.text: tatpratiṣṭhaḥ smṛto dharmo dharmamūlaś ca pārthivaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) is declared to rest upon that, and the king is the root of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: saha sadbhir ato rājā vyavahārān viśodhayet || 5 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the king should decide lawsuits together with righteous men. || 5 ||
When lawsuits are properly decided, the assessors attain purity;

children.text:
śuddhiś ca teṣāṃ dharmād dhi dharmam eva vadet tataḥ || 6
                            ||
children.translated_text: and their purity comes from <s>dharma</s>, so one should therefore speak only <s>dharma</s>. || 6 ||

children.text: yatra dharmo hy adharmeṇa satyaṃ yatrānṛtena ca |
children.translated_text: Where <s>dharma</s> is destroyed by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), and truth by falsehood,
while the assessors look on -- the assessors themselves are slain there. || 7 ||

children.text: viddho dharmo hy adharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatra-upatiṣṭhate |
children.translated_text: Where <s>dharma</s>, pierced by <s>adharma</s>, enters the court,

children.text: na ced viśalyaḥ kriyate viddhās tatra sabhāsadaḥ || 8 ||
sabhā vā na praveṣṭavyā vaktavyaṃ vā samañjasam |
abruvan vibruvan vāpi naro bhavati kilbiṣī || 9 ||
ye tu sabhyāḥ sabhāṃ gatvā tūṣṇīṃ dhyāyanta āsate |
pādaḥ sabhāsadaḥ sarvān pādo rājānam ṛcchati || 11 ||
rājā bhavaty anenās tu mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ |
eno gacchati kartāraṃ nindārho yatra nindyate || 12 ||
parokṣam arthavaikalyād bhāṣate yaḥ sabhāṃ gataḥ || 13 ||
vacas tathāvidhaṃ brūyād yathā na narakaṃ patet || 14 ||
yathā śalyaṃ bhiṣag vidvān uddhared yantrayuktitaḥ |
yatra sabhyo janaḥ sarvaḥ sādhv etad iti manyate |

sa niḥśalyo vivādaḥ syāt saśalyaḥ syād ato 'nyathā || 16
                            ||
na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā

vṛddhā na te ye na
                            vadanti dharmam |
nāsau dharmo yatra na satyam asti
ṛṇaṃ deyam adeyaṃ ca yena yatra yathā ca yat |
pitary uparate putrā ṛṇaṃ dadyur yathāṃśataḥ |
vibhaktā hy avibhaktā vā yas tām udvahate dhuram || 2 ||
pitṛvyeṇāvibhaktena bhrātrā vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛtam |

mātrā vā yat kuṭumbārthe dadyus tad rikthino 'khilam || 3
                            ||
kramād avyāhataṃ prāptaṃ putrair yan narṇam uddhṛtam |
dadyuḥ paitāmahaṃ pautrās tac caturthān nivartate || 4 ||
icchanti pitaraḥ putrān svārthahetor yatas tataḥ |
ataḥ putreṇa jātena svārtham utsṛjya yatnataḥ |
pitā mokṣitavya ṛṇād yathā na narakaṃ patet || 6 ||
tapasvī cāgnihotrī ca ṛṇavān mriyate yadi |
tapaś caivāgnihotraṃ ca sarvaṃ tad dhanināṃ dhanam || 7 ||
na putrarṇaṃ pitā dadyād dadyāt putras tu paitṛkam |
pitur eva niyogād yat kuṭumbabharaṇāya ca |
kṛtaṃ vā yad ṛṇaṃ kṛcchre dadyāt putrasya tat pitā || 9 ||
nārvāg viṃśatimād varṣāt pitari proṣite sutaḥ |
ṛṇaṃ dadyāt pitṛvye vā jyeṣṭhe bhrātary athāpi vā || 11 ||
dāpyaḥ pararṇam eko 'pi jīvatsv adhikṛtaiḥ kṛtam |
preteṣu tu na tatputraḥ pararṇaṃ dātum arhati || 12 ||
na strī patikṛtaṃ dadyād ṛṇaṃ putrakṛtaṃ tathā |
abhyupetād ṛte yadvā saha patyā kṛtaṃ bhavet || 13 ||
dadyād aputrā vidhavā niyuktā yā mumūrṣuṇā |
yo vā tadriktham ādadyād yato riktham ṛṇaṃ tataḥ || 14 ||
na ca bhāryākṛtam ṛṇaṃ kathañcit patyur ābhavet |
āpatkṛtād ṛte puṃsāṃ kuṭumbārtho hi vistaraḥ || 15 ||
teṣāṃ tatpratyayā vṛttiḥ kuṭumbaṃ ca tadāśrayam || 16 ||
putriṇī tu samutsṛjya putraṃ strī yānyam āśrayet |
ṛkthaṃ tasyā haret sarvaṃ niḥsvāyāḥ putra eva tu || 17 ||
yā tu sapradhanaiva strī sāpatyā cānyam āśrayet |

so 'syā dadyād ṛṇaṃ bhartur utsṛjed vā tathaiva tām || 18
                            ||
adhanasya hy aputrasya mṛtasyopaiti yaḥ striyam |
ṛṇaṃ voḍhuḥ sa bhajate tad evāsya dhanaṃ smṛtam || 19 ||
uttamā svairiṇī yā syād uttamā ca punarbhuvām |
ṛṇaṃ tayoḥ patikṛtaṃ dadyād yas tām upāśnute || 21 ||
etāny api pramāṇāni bhartā yady anumanyate |
putraḥ patyur abhāve vā rājā vā patiputrayoḥ || 23 ||
bhartrā prītena yad dattaṃ striyai tasmin mṛte 'pi tat |
sā yathākāmam aśnīyād dadyād vā sthāvarād ṛte || 24 ||
anyatra svāmisandeśān na dāsaḥ prabhur ātmanaḥ || 25 ||
putreṇa ca kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ yat syāt pitur anicchataḥ |
tad apy akṛtam evāhur dāsaḥ putraś ca tau samau || 26 ||
aprāptavyavahāraś cet svatantro 'pi hi na rṇabhāk |

svātantryaṃ tu smṛtaṃ jyeṣṭhe jyaiṣṭhyaṃ guṇavayaḥkṛtam || 27
                            ||
trayaḥ svatantrā loke 'smin rājācāryas tathaiva ca |
prati prati ca varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ svagṛhe gṛhī || 28 ||
asvatantraḥ smṛtaḥ śiṣya ācārye tu svatantratā || 29 ||
asvatantrāḥ striyaḥ putrā dāsāś ca saparigrahāḥ |
svatantras tatra tu gṛhī yasya yat syāt kramāgatam || 30 ||
garbhasthaiḥ sadṛśo jñeya ā varṣād aṣṭamāc chiṣuḥ |
bāla ā ṣoḍaśāj jñeyaḥ pogaṇḍaś cāpi śabdyate || 31 ||
abhāve bījino mātā tadabhāve tu pūrvajaḥ || 33 ||
anuśiṣṭau visarge ca vikraye ceśvarā matāḥ || 34 ||
yad bālaḥ kurute kāryam asvatantras tathaiva ca |
akṛtaṃ tad iti prāhuḥ śāstre śāstravido janāḥ || 35 ||
svatantro 'pi hi yat kāryaṃ kuryād aprakṛtiṃ gataḥ |
tad apy akṛtam evāhur asvatantraḥ sa hetutaḥ || 36 ||
rāgadveṣaparītāś ca jñeyās tv aprakṛtiṃ gatāḥ || 37 ||
kule jyeṣṭhas tathā śreṣṭhaḥ prakṛtisthaś ca yo bhavet |
tatkṛtaṃ syāt kṛtaṃ kāryaṃ nāsvatantrakṛtaṃ kṛtam || 38 ||
dhanamūlāḥ kriyāḥ sarvā yatnas tatsādhane mataḥ |
rakṣaṇaṃ vardhanaṃ bhoga iti tasya vidhiḥ kramāt || 39 ||
tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ śuklaṃ śabalam eva ca |
kṛṣṇaṃ ca tasya vijñeyaḥ prabhedaḥ saptadhā pṛthak || 40 ||
dhanaṃ saptavidhaṃ śuklam udayo 'py asya tadvidhaḥ || 41 ||
vyājenopārjitaṃ yac ca tat kṛṣṇaṃ samudāhṛtam || 43 ||
tena krayo vikrayaś ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca |
vividhāś ca pravartante kriyāḥ sambhoga eva ca || 44 ||
tathāvidham avāpnoti sa phalaṃ pretya ceha ca || 45 ||
sādhāraṇaṃ syāt trividhaṃ śeṣaṃ navavidhaṃ smṛtam || 46 ||
kramāgataṃ prītidāyaḥ prāptaṃ ca saha bhāryayā |
yuddhopalabdhaṃ kāraś ca daṇḍaś ca vyavahārataḥ || 49 ||
sarveṣām eva varṇānām eṣa dharmyo dhanāgamaḥ |
viparyayād adharmyaḥ syān na ced āpad garīyasī || 51 ||
vaiśyavṛttis tataś coktā na jaghanyā kathañcana || 52 ||
na kathañcana kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ karma vārṣalam |
vṛṣalaḥ karma na brāhmaṃ patanīye hi te tayoḥ || 53 ||
utkṛṣṭaṃ cāpakṛṣṭaṃ ca tayoḥ karma na vidyate |
madhyame karmaṇī hitvā sarvasādhāraṇe hi te || 54 ||
āpadaṃ brāhmaṇas tīrtvā kṣatravṛttyā hṛtair dhanaiḥ |
utsṛjet kṣatravṛttiṃ tāṃ kṛtvā pāvanam ātmanaḥ || 55 ||
tasyām eva tu yo vṛttau brāhmaṇo ramate rasāt |

children.translated_text: One who has been branded on the back and has fallen from the [righteous] path is declared to be unworthy of sitting in a row (<s>apāṅkteya</s>). || 56 ||
In the occupation of a <s>Vaiśya</s>, milk and curds are not to be sold by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,
nor ghee, honey, beeswax, lac, alkali, juice, and liquor. || 57 ||
Meat, cooked rice, sesame, linen, <s>Soma</s>, flowers, fruits, and vegetables,
human beings, poison, weapons, water, salt, cakes, and herbs; || 58 ||
indigo, silk, leather, bones, cotton cloth, and single-hoofed animals, clay,
white-spotted [cattle], hair, oil-cakes, potherbs, and likewise medicines; || 59 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu vikreyaṃ śuṣkaṃ dāru tṛṇāni ca |
children.translated_text: But what may be sold by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is dry wood and grass,
except for fragrant substances, red dye, cane, cotton, roots, and husks. || 60 ||

children.text: svayaṃ śīrṇaṃ ca vidalaṃ phalānāṃ badareṅgude |
children.translated_text: And [he may sell] that which has fallen of itself, split fruits, jujubes and <s>iṅguda</s> berries among fruits,

children.text: rajjuḥ kārpāsikaṃ sūtraṃ tac ced avikṛtaṃ bhavet || 61 ||
children.translated_text: rope, and cotton thread — provided these are unprocessed. || 61 ||
In case of inability, for the purpose of medicine or for the sake of a sacrifice,

children.text: yady avaśyaṃ tu vikreyās tilā dhānyena tatsāmāḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: if sesame must absolutely be sold, [they should be exchanged] for an equal quantity of grain. || 62 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sells items that are forbidden for sale has fallen from the path;

children.text: mārge punar avasthāpya rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā || 63 ||
children.translated_text: he should be restored to the path by the king through a heavy fine. || 63 ||

children.text: , Chapter iv. On Evidence by Writing

children.translated_text: The standards of evidence (<s>pramāṇa</s>) must be carefully maintained by those established in authority,
for the standards of evidence decline when the standards are not firmly established. || 64 ||

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇo bhuktiḥ pramāṇaṃ trividhaṃ smṛtaṃ |
children.translated_text: Documents (<s>likhita</s>), witnesses (<s>sākṣin</s>), and possession (<s>bhukti</s>) — evidence is declared to be threefold,
by which the owner of wealth obtains [recovery of] his wealth. || 65 ||

children.text: likhitaṃ balavan nityaṃ jīvantas tv eva sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: A document is always the strongest; witnesses [are valid only] while they are alive;
possession [becomes evidence] through lapse of time — this is the settled rule in the <s>śāstras</s>. || 66 ||
Of this threefold visible evidence, in due order,

children.text: pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ guru jñeyaṃ bhuktir ebhyo garīyasī || 67 ||
children.translated_text: each preceding one is to be known as weightier, [but] possession is the weightiest of all. || 67 ||

children.text: vidyamāne 'pi likhite jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: Even when a document exists and even when witnesses are alive,

children.text:
viśeṣataḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ yan na bhuktaṃ na tat sthiram || 68
                            ||
children.translated_text: especially regarding immovable property, that which has not been enjoyed through possession is not secure. || 68 ||

children.text: bhujyamānān parair arthān yaḥ svān maurkhyād upekṣate |
children.translated_text: One who through foolishness neglects his own property while it is being enjoyed by others —

children.text: samakṣaṃ jīvato 'py asya tān bhuktiḥ kurute vaśe || 69 ||
children.translated_text: even while he is alive and present, possession brings that [property] under [another's] control. || 69 ||

children.text: yatkiñcid daśa varṣāṇi sannidhau prekṣate dhanī |
children.translated_text: Whatever property the owner watches for ten years in [the other's] presence,

children.text: bhujyamānaṃ parais tūṣṇīṃ na sa tal labdhum arhati || 70 ||
children.translated_text: while it is being enjoyed by others in silence, he does not deserve to recover it. || 70 ||

children.text: upekṣāṃ kurvatas tasya tūṣṇīṃ bhūtasya tiṣṭhataḥ |
children.translated_text: When one neglects [his property] and remains silent while present,
after the aforementioned period has passed, the legal action does not succeed. || 71 ||

children.text: ajaḍaś ced apogaṇḍo viṣaye cāsya bhujyate |
children.translated_text: If [the owner] is not mentally impaired, not a minor, and [the property] is enjoyed within his jurisdiction,

children.text: bhuktaṃ tad vyavahāreṇa bhoktā tad dhanam arhati || 72 ||
children.translated_text: that is [considered] enjoyed through legal process, and the enjoyer deserves that property. || 72 ||
A pledge (<s>ādhi</s>), a boundary (<s>sīmā</s>), the property of a minor (<s>bāladhana</s>), a deposit (<s>nikṣepa</s>), a sealed deposit (<s>upanidhi</s>), women,
royal property, and the property of a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>) — these are not extinguished by enjoyment. || 73 ||
Through direct enjoyment by the owner for twenty years,
even pledges and the like are extinguished, except for the property of women, kings, and [learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>]. || 74 ||

children.text: strīdhanaṃ ca narendrāṇāṃ na kadācana jīryate |
children.translated_text: The property of women and of kings is never extinguished,
even if enjoyed without title for hundreds of years. || 75 ||

children.text: nirbhogo yatra dṛśyeta na dṛśyetāgamaḥ kvacit |
children.translated_text: Where enjoyment is absent but no title [of the possessor] is seen anywhere,

children.text: āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra na bhogas tatra kāraṇam || 76 ||
children.translated_text: title is the decisive factor there, not enjoyment. || 76 ||

children.text: anāgamaṃ bhujyate yan na tad bhogo 'tivartate |
children.translated_text: That which is enjoyed without title — enjoyment does not override [the original owner's right];

children.text: prete tu bhoktari dhanaṃ yāti tadvaṃśyabhogyatām || 77 ||
children.translated_text: but when the enjoyer dies, the property passes to his descendants for their enjoyment. || 77 ||
The claimant, when challenged, should produce proof of ownership of the property;

children.text:
bhuktir eva viśuddhiḥ syāt prāptānāṃ pitṛtaḥ kramāt || 78
                            ||
children.translated_text: possession itself is sufficient proof for those who have obtained [property] in succession from their father. || 78 ||
That which is entrusted (<s>anvāhita</s>), seized (<s>hṛta</s>), deposited (<s>nyasta</s>), held by force (<s>balāvaṣṭabdha</s>), or borrowed (<s>yācita</s>),

children.text: apratyakṣaṃ ca yad bhuktaṃ ṣaḍ etāny āgamaṃ vinā || 79 ||
children.translated_text: and that which is enjoyed in the owner's absence — these six are without title [of acquisition]. || 79 ||
Likewise, when a litigant whose case has been commenced dies,

children.text:
putreṇa so 'rthaḥ saṃśodhyo na taṃ bhogo 'tivartate || 80
                            ||
children.translated_text: that claim must be pursued by his son; enjoyment does not override it. || 80 ||

children.text: yad vināgamam apy ūrdhvaṃ bhuktaṃ pūrvais tribhir bhavet |
children.translated_text: That which, even without title, has been enjoyed by three generations of predecessors,

children.text: na tac chakyam apākartuṃ kramāt tripuruṣāgatam || 81 ||
children.translated_text: cannot be taken away, having come down in succession through three generations. || 81 ||

children.text: santo 'pi na pramāṇaṃ syur mṛte dhanini sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Witnesses are not valid evidence when the owner of the property has died,

children.text: anyatra śrāvitaṃ yat syāt svayam āsannamṛtyunā || 82 ||
children.translated_text: except for what was declared by the [owner] himself when near death. || 82 ||

children.text: na hi pratyarthini prete pramāṇaṃ sākṣiṇāṃ vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the adversary has died, the testimony of witnesses is not evidence;

children.text: sākṣimat karaṇaṃ tatra pramāṇaṃ syād viniścaye || 83 ||
children.translated_text: in that case, a document attested by witnesses is the evidence for determining [the matter]. || 83 ||

children.text: śrāvitas tv ātureṇāpi yas tv artho dharmasaṃhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: But a matter declared even by one who was ill, if it is connected with <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: mṛte 'pi tatra sākṣī syāt ṣaṭsu cānvāhitādiṣu || 84 ||
children.translated_text: may be testified to even after [the declarant's] death, and in the six cases beginning with entrustment (<s>anvāhita</s>). || 84 ||
In all [cases] such as debts and the like, the later [evidence] prevails over the earlier;
but in gifts, purchases, and appropriations, the earlier is weightier. || 85 ||
Lending for the purpose of profit through interest is what is intended,

children.text: tat kusīdam iti proktaṃ tena vṛttiḥ kusīdinām || 86 ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>kusīda</s> (usury), and by it the usurers (<s>kusīdin</s>) make their livelihood. || 86 ||

children.text: kāyikā kālikā caiva kāritā ca tathā smṛtā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāyikā</s> (bodily or stipulated interest), <s>kālikā</s> (periodic interest), and likewise <s>kāritā</s> (compelled interest) are mentioned,

children.text: cakravṛddhiś ca śāstreṣu tasya vṛddhiś caturvidhā || 87 ||
children.translated_text: and <s>cakravṛddhi</s> (compound interest) — thus interest is fourfold according to the <s>śāstras</s>. || 87 ||
<s>Kāyikā</s> is that which does not conflict with the principal, always a quarter <s>paṇa</s> [per month on each hundred];

children.text: pratimāsaṃ sravati yā vṛddhiḥ sā kālikā smṛtā || 88 ||
children.translated_text: that interest which accrues monthly is called <s>kālikā</s>. || 88 ||

children.text: vṛddhiḥ sā kāritā nāma ya rṇikena svayaṅkṛtā |
children.translated_text: That interest which is voluntarily undertaken by the debtor himself is called <s>kāritā</s>;

children.text: vṛddher api punar vṛddhiś cakravṛddhir udāhṛtā || 89 ||
children.translated_text: interest upon interest is termed <s>cakravṛddhi</s> (compound interest). || 89 ||
This is declared to be the universal rule regarding interest on debts,

children.text: deśācāravidhis tv anyo yatra rṇam avatiṣṭhati || 90 ||
children.translated_text: but another rule is that of local custom, wherever the debt is situated. || 90 ||
In one [place] it is double, in another triple, and in yet another fourfold,
and in another eightfold — it varies from region to region. || 91 ||
For gold, grain, and cloth, the interest is twofold, threefold, and fourfold [respectively];
for ghee, the interest is eightfold; and for women and cattle, [the interest is] their offspring. || 92 ||
For thread, cotton, ferments, tin, and lead,
and for all weapons, leather, copper, and iron, || 93 ||

children.text: anyeṣāṃ caiva sarveṣām iṣṭakānāṃ tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: and for all other [commodities] and likewise for bricks —

children.text: akṣayyā vṛddhir eteṣāṃ manur āha prajāpatiḥ || 94 ||
children.translated_text: the interest on these is unlimited, so <s>Manu</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> has declared. || 94 ||
For all oils, all liquors, honey, and ghee,

children.text: vṛddhir aṣṭaguṇā jñeyā guḍasya lavaṇasya ca || 95 ||
children.translated_text: the interest is to be known as eightfold, and likewise for sugar and salt. || 95 ||

children.text: na vṛddhiḥ prītidattānāṃ syād anākāritā kvacit |
children.translated_text: No interest accrues on gifts made out of affection, if it has not been demanded;
but even [a loan] not demanded increases after half a year. || 96 ||
This rule of interest has been declared for [a debtor] who pays according to <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: vṛddhis tu yoktā dhānyānāṃ vārdhuṣyaṃ tad udāhṛtam || 97 ||
children.translated_text: but interest that increases upon grain is called <s>vārdhuṣya</s> (usurious gain). || 97 ||
A <s>Vaiśya</s> may freely overcome adversity through usurious transactions;

children.text: āpatsv api hi kaṣṭāsu brāhmaṇasya na vārdhuṣam || 98 ||
children.translated_text: but even in the most dire calamities, usury is not [permitted] for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 98 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇasya tu yad deyaṃ sānvayasya na cāsti saḥ |
children.translated_text: But that which is owed to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has descendants — if he is no longer alive,
it should be paid to a member of his family (<s>svakulya</s>), and in their absence, to his kinsmen (<s>bandhu</s>). || 99 ||

children.text: yadā tu na svakulyāḥ syur na ca sambandhibāndhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: But when there are no family members, no relatives or kinsmen,

children.text:
tadā dadyāt svajātibhyas teṣv asatsv apsu nikṣipet || 100
                            ||
children.translated_text: then it should be given to persons of the same caste; if none exist, it should be cast into water. || 100 ||
The creditor should accept interest that has accrued and give [a receipt] to the debtor;
if he does not give [a receipt] when asked, he shall suffer loss of the balance. || 101 ||

children.text: lekhyaṃ dadyād ṛṇe śuddhe tadabhāve pratiśravam |
children.translated_text: Upon discharge of a debt, [the creditor] should give a written release; in its absence, an oral declaration;
thus there shall be mutual acquittance between creditor and debtor. || 102 ||

children.text: viśrambhahetū dvāv atra pratibhūr ādhir eva ca |
children.translated_text: There are two means of trust in this [matter]: a surety (<s>pratibhū</s>) and a pledge (<s>ādhi</s>);

children.text: likhitaṃ sākṣiṇaś ca dve pramāṇe vyaktikārake || 103 ||
children.translated_text: and documents (<s>likhita</s>) and witnesses (<s>sākṣin</s>) are the two means of evidence that establish [a claim]. || 103 ||
For [ensuring] appearance, for payment, and for trustworthiness,

children.text:
trividhaḥ pratibhūr dṛṣṭas triṣv evārtheṣu sūribhiḥ || 104
                            ||
children.translated_text: a surety (<s>pratibhū</s>) is recognized by the wise as being of three kinds in these three purposes. || 104 ||
When debtors fail to repay, or when a surety for trustworthiness is disputed,

children.text: pratibhūs tad ṛṇaṃ dadyād anupasthāpayaṃs tathā || 105 ||
children.translated_text: the surety shall pay that debt, and likewise if he fails to produce [the debtor]. || 105 ||

children.text: bahavaś cet pratibhuvo dadyus te 'rthaṃ yathākṛtam |
children.translated_text: If there are many sureties, they shall pay the amount in the proportion [they guaranteed];

children.text: arthe 'viśeṣite hy eṣu dhaninaś chandataḥ kriyā || 106 ||
children.translated_text: but if the amount is undivided among them, the creditor may proceed at his discretion. || 106 ||
Whatever amount the surety pays under pressure from the creditor,
the debtor shall repay double that amount to the surety. || 107 ||

children.text: adhikriyata ity ādhiḥ sa vijñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: That which is pledged (<s>adhikriyate</s>) is called <s>ādhi</s> (pledge); it is to be known as being of two kinds:
one redeemable at a fixed time, and one [held] until the debt is paid. || 108 ||

children.text: sa punar dvividhaḥ prokto gopyo bhogyas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: It is further declared to be of two kinds: one to be preserved (<s>gopya</s>) and one to be enjoyed (<s>bhogya</s>);
likewise its restoration, and loss of profit in the contrary case. || 109 ||

children.text: pramādād dhaninas tadvad ādhau vikṛtim āgate |
children.translated_text: Similarly, through negligence of the creditor, if the pledge undergoes deterioration,
or if it is destroyed, the principal is lost — except [when caused] by an act of God or the king. || 110 ||
Where a pledge, even though being preserved, deteriorates over time,

children.text: ādhir anyo 'dhikartavyo deyaṃ vā dhanine dhanam || 111 ||
children.translated_text: another pledge must be given, or the debt must be paid to the creditor. || 111 ||
Now, if the debtor becomes unable [to pay] due to reversal of fortune,

children.text: śakyaprekṣam ṛṇaṃ dāpyaḥ kāle kāle yathodayam || 112 ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay the debt in installments at intervals, according to his means and income. || 112 ||

children.text: śakto vā yadi daurātmyān na dadyād dhanine dhanam |
children.translated_text: Or if, though able, he does not pay the creditor out of dishonesty,

children.text: rājñā dāpayitavyaḥ syād gṛhītvāṃśaṃ tu viṃśakam || 113 ||
children.translated_text: the king should compel him to pay, taking a twentieth share [as fee]. || 113 ||
If the amount of the debtor's debt is lost over time,
the proof of caste, name, domicile, and origin is to be established from a written document. || 114 ||

children.text: lekhyaṃ tu dvividhaṃ jñeyaṃ svahastānyakṛtaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: A written document is to be known as of two kinds: one written by one's own hand and one written by another,

children.text: asākṣimat sākṣimac ca siddhir deśasthites tayoḥ || 115 ||
children.translated_text: [and each may be] without witnesses or with witnesses; their validity depends on local practice. || 115 ||
A document that does not conflict with local custom, that clearly indicates the parties and the subject matter,
that is unbroken in sequence of syllables — such is declared to be valid evidence. || 116 ||
A document executed by one who is intoxicated, under prosecution, a woman, a minor, or under compulsion,
is not valid evidence; likewise one made through fear or fraud. || 117 ||
Where the witnesses, the creditor, the debtor, and the scribe have all died,

children.text:
tad apy apārthaṃ likhitam ṛte tv ādheḥ sthirāśrayāt || 118
                            ||
children.translated_text: such a document is also without effect — except for a pledge that has a permanent object [as security]. || 118 ||

children.text: ādhir yo dvividhaḥ prokto jaṅgamaḥ sthāvaras tathā |
children.translated_text: A pledge (<s>ādhi</s>), which has been declared to be of two kinds — movable and immovable —

children.text: siddhir atrobhayasyāsya bhogo yady asti nānyathā || 119 ||
children.translated_text: the validity of both is established through enjoyment, if it exists; otherwise not. || 119 ||

children.text: darśitaṃ pratikālaṃ yac chrāvitaṃ śrāvitaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: A document that has been shown periodically and that has been publicly declared,

children.text: lekhyaṃ sidhyati sarvatra mṛteṣv api hi sākṣiṣu || 120 ||
children.translated_text: is valid everywhere, even when the witnesses have died. || 120 ||
A document whose contents have not been heard [by witnesses], whose subject matter has not been seen,

children.text: na lekhyaṃ siddhim āpnoti jīvatsv api hi sākṣiṣu || 121 ||
children.translated_text: and one [made] for the purpose of litigation, does not attain validity, even when the witnesses are alive. || 121 ||
When a document has been deposited in another country, burnt, badly written, or stolen,
if [the original party] is alive, a fresh document should be made; if dead, evidence of witnesses [who] saw [should suffice]. || 122 ||

children.text: yasmin syāt saṃśayo lekhye bhūtābhūtakṛte kvacit |
children.translated_text: Regarding any document about which there is doubt, whether it was genuinely or fraudulently made,
One should recover it by means of the handwriting, marks of one's own hand, acquisition, and reasoning. || 123 ||
A document that bears another person's name or mark, and was made for a different reason,
in case of doubt, that should be examined through relationship, tradition, and reasoning. || 124 ||
A document that bears another person's name or mark, and was made for a different reason,
in case of doubt, that should be examined through relationship, tradition, and reasoning. || 124-1 ||
A written document should be defeated only by a written document; one supported by witnesses, only by witnesses.

children.text: sākṣibhyo likhitaṃ śreyo likhitena tu sākṣiṇaḥ || 125 ||
children.translated_text: Witnesses are superior to a document, but a document is superior to witnesses. || 125 ||
When documents are cut, torn, stolen, effaced, lost, or badly written,

children.text:
kartavyam anyal lekhyaṃ syād eṣa lekhyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 126
                            ||
children.translated_text: another document should be prepared — this is declared to be the rule concerning documents. || 126 ||

children.text:
, Chapter v. On Evidence by Witnesses
                        ...

children.translated_text: In doubtful cases, when two parties are disputing,
witnesses provide clear perception through having seen, heard, or experienced the matter. || 127 ||
A witness (<s>sākṣin</s>) is so called because of direct perception by ear and eye;

children.text: śrotrasya yat paro brūte cakṣuṣaḥ kāyakarma yat || 128 ||
children.translated_text: what another declares is the province of the ear; bodily action is the province of the eye. || 128 ||

children.text: ekādaśavidhaḥ sākṣī sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: A witness is seen by the wise to be of eleven kinds;
of these, the appointed (<s>kṛta</s>) witness is of five kinds, and the undesignated (<s>akṛta</s>) is said to be of six kinds. || 129 ||

children.text: likhitaḥ smāritaś caiva yadṛcchābhijña eva ca |
children.translated_text: The recorded (<s>likhita</s>), the reminded (<s>smārita</s>), the chance witness (<s>yadṛcchābhijña</s>),

children.text: gūḍhaś cottarasākṣī ca sākṣī pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ || 130 ||
children.translated_text: the secret (<s>gūḍha</s>), and the corroborating witness (<s>uttarasākṣin</s>) — thus the appointed witness is remembered as fivefold. || 130 ||
The undesignated (<s>akṛta</s>) witness is also declared by the learned to be sixfold:

children.text: grāmaś ca prāḍvivākaś ca rājā ca vyavahāriṇām || 131 ||
children.translated_text: the village, the judge (<s>prāḍvivāka</s>), and the king, for those involved in litigation; || 131 ||

children.text: kāryeṣv abhyantaro yaḥ syād arthinā prahitaś ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: one who is an insider in the affairs, and one sent by the plaintiff,
and the family in disputes among families — these too may serve as witnesses. || 132 ||
Those of noble birth, upright, pure by birth, conduct, and wealth,
not fewer than three, blameless, honest, and intelligent — such should be the witnesses. || 133 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā ye cāpy aninditāḥ |
prativarṇaṃ bhaveyus te sarve sarveṣu vā punaḥ || 134 ||
children.translated_text: they should be witnesses for their own <s>varṇa</s> (caste), or alternatively, all for all. || 134 ||
In guilds (<s>śreṇī</s>), guild-members should be witnesses; in their own groups, group-members;

children.text: bahirvāsiṣu bāhyāś ca striyaḥ striṣu ca sākṣiṇaḥ || 135 ||
children.translated_text: for those dwelling outside, outsiders; and women should be witnesses in cases involving women. || 135 ||

children.text: śreṇyādiṣu tu vargeṣu kaścic ced dveṣyatām iyāt |
children.translated_text: But in guilds and other groups, if someone should incur enmity,

children.text: tebhya eva na sākṣī syād dveṣṭāraḥ sarva eva te || 136 ||
children.translated_text: he should not be a witness from among them, for they are all hostile. || 136 ||

children.text: asākṣy api hi śāstreṣu dṛṣṭaḥ pañcavidho budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: A non-witness (<s>asākṣin</s>) too is seen by the wise as being of five kinds in the legal texts:
by declaration, by defect, by contradiction, by self-disclosure, and by the death of the other party. || 137 ||
Learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and others are disqualified by declaration; thieves and others by the perception of fault;

children.text: bhedād vipratipattiḥ syād vivāde yatra sākṣiṇaḥ || 138 ||
children.translated_text: by contradiction, there is inconsistency among the witnesses in a dispute. || 138 ||

children.text: svayamukter anirdiṣṭaḥ svayam evaitya yo vadet |
children.translated_text: By self-disclosure, one who was not designated but comes forward of his own accord to testify;
by death of the other party, when the plaintiff is dead, except when one has been made to hear by a dying person. || 139 ||

children.text: śrotriyās tāpasā vṛddhā ye ca pravrajitā narāḥ |
children.translated_text: Learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>), ascetics (<s>tāpasa</s>), elders, and those who have renounced the world (<s>pravrajita</s>),

children.text: asākṣiṇas te vacanān nātra hetur udāhṛtaḥ || 140 ||
children.translated_text: they are non-witnesses by declaration — no reason for this is stated. || 140 ||

children.text: stenāḥ sāhasikāś caṇḍāḥ kitavā vadhakās tathā |
children.translated_text: Thieves, violent criminals (<s>sāhasika</s>), the fierce, gamblers, and murderers,

children.text: asākṣiṇas te duṣṭatvāt teṣu satyaṃ na vidyate || 141 ||
children.translated_text: they are non-witnesses due to their wickedness — truth is not found in them. || 141 ||
When witnesses accepted by the king for determining a single matter,

children.text: vacanaṃ yatra bhidyate te syur bhedād asākṣiṇaḥ || 142 ||
children.translated_text: contradict each other in their testimony, they become non-witnesses by reason of contradiction. || 142 ||

children.text: anirdiṣṭas tu sākṣitve svayam evaitya yo vadet |
children.translated_text: One who, not designated for witnessing, comes forward of his own accord to testify,

children.text: sūcīty uktaḥ sa śāstreṣu na sa sākṣitvam arhati || 143 ||
children.translated_text: is called an informer (<s>sūcī</s>) in the legal texts — he does not deserve the status of witness. || 143 ||

children.text: yo 'rthaḥ śrāvayitavyaḥ syāt tasminn asati cārthini |
children.translated_text: When the matter about which testimony is to be given, and the plaintiff in that case, no longer exists,

children.text: kva tad vadatu sākṣitvam ity asākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ || 144 ||
children.translated_text: where shall the witness testify about that? — thus one is a non-witness when the other party is dead. || 144 ||

children.text: yo 'rthaḥ śrāvayitavyaḥ syāt tasminn asati cārthini |
children.translated_text: When the matter about which testimony is to be given, and the plaintiff in that case, no longer exists,

children.text:
kva tad vadatu sākṣitvam ity asākṣī mṛtāntaraḥ || 144-1
                            ||
children.translated_text: where shall the witness testify about that? — thus one is a non-witness when the other party is dead. || 144-1 ||

children.text: dvayor vivadator arthe dvayoḥ satsu ca sākṣiṣu |
children.translated_text: When two parties dispute a matter and both have witnesses,

children.text: pūrvapakṣo bhaved yasya bhaveyus tasya sākṣiṇaḥ || 145 ||
children.translated_text: the witnesses of the one who has the prior claim (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) shall prevail. || 145 ||

children.text: ādharyaṃ pūrvapakṣasya yasminn arthe vaśād bhavet |
children.translated_text: When the burden of proof necessarily falls upon the plaintiff (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) in a matter,
the witnesses of the defendant (<s>prativādin</s>) should be examined in that dispute. || 146 ||

children.text: na pareṇa samuddiṣṭam upeyāt sākṣiṇaṃ rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not approach in private a witness designated by the opposing party,

children.text: bhedayet taṃ na cānyena hīyetaivaṃ samācaran || 147 ||
children.translated_text: nor should one try to corrupt him through another — one who acts thus would lose the case. || 147 ||

children.text: sākṣy uddiṣṭo yadi preyād gacched vāpi digantaram |
children.translated_text: If a designated witness should die or go to a distant land,

children.text:
tacchrotāraḥ pramāṇaṃ syuḥ pramāṇaṃ hy uttarakriyā || 148
                            ||
children.translated_text: those who heard his testimony shall be authoritative, for the subsequent procedure is the authority. || 148 ||
Even after a very long time, a written document may achieve validity.

children.text: jānatā cātmanā lekhyaṃ ajānānas tu lekhayet || 149 ||
children.translated_text: One who knows should write the document himself; one who does not know should have it written. || 149 ||
The validity of a reminded witness (<s>smārita</s>) is from the eighth year onward;

children.text: ā pañcamāt tathā siddhir yadṛcchopagatasya tu || 150 ||
children.translated_text: similarly, the validity of a chance witness (<s>yadṛcchopagata</s>) is up to the fifth year. || 150 ||

children.text: ā tṛtīyāt tathā varṣāt siddhir gūḍhasya sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Similarly, the validity of a secret witness (<s>gūḍha</s>) is up to the third year;

children.text: ā vai saṃvatsarāt siddhiṃ vadanty uttarasākṣiṇaḥ || 151 ||
children.translated_text: they say the corroborating witnesses (<s>uttarasākṣin</s>) have validity up to one year. || 151 ||

children.text: athavā kālaniyamo na dṛṣṭaḥ sākṣiṇaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, no time limit is prescribed for witnesses;

children.text: smṛtyapekṣaṃ hi sākṣitvam āhuḥ śāstravido janāḥ || 152 ||
children.translated_text: for witness-status depends on memory, say those who know the legal texts. || 152 ||

children.text: yasya nopahatā puṃsaḥ smṛtiḥ śrotraṃ ca nityaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: A person whose memory and hearing are perpetually unimpaired,

children.text: sudīrgheṇāpi kālena sa sākṣī sākṣyam arhati || 153 ||
children.translated_text: even after a very long time, that witness is competent to give testimony. || 153 ||
There are six types of disputes declared in which no witness-proof is required (<s>asākṣipratyaya</s>);

children.text: lakṣaṇāny eva sākṣitvaṃ eṣām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || 154 ||
children.translated_text: the visible marks themselves constitute the witness-proof in those cases, say the wise. || 154 ||
One holding a firebrand (<s>ulkāhasta</s>) is known to be an arsonist; one with a weapon in hand is a killer;
one caught grasping another by the hair is at once recognized as an adulterer (<s>pāradārika</s>). || 155 ||
One with a spade in hand, standing nearby, is known as a breaker of embankments;
likewise, one with an axe in hand is declared to be a forest-cutter. || 156 ||
A person bearing fresh wound-marks is known to be the perpetrator of assault (<s>daṇḍapāruṣya</s>).

children.text: asākṣipratyayā hy ete pāruṣye tu parīkṣaṇam || 157 ||
children.translated_text: These are cases requiring no witness-proof, but in assault cases, investigation is needed. || 157 ||

children.text: kaścit kṛtvātmanaś cihnaṃ dveṣāt param upadravet |
children.translated_text: Someone might inflict marks upon himself and out of enmity accuse another;
therefore, investigation is proper in such cases through motive, purpose, circumstances, and capacity. || 158 ||

children.text: nārthasambandhino nāptā na sahāyā na vairiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those connected with the matter, kinsmen, associates, enemies,

children.text: na dṛṣṭadoṣāḥ praṣṭavyāś na vyādhyārtā na dūṣitāḥ || 159 ||
children.translated_text: those with visible faults, those afflicted by illness, and those who are corrupt — none of these should be questioned as witnesses. || 159 ||
Slaves, deceitful persons, faithless ones, the aged, women, children, tricksters,
drunkards, the insane, the careless, the distressed, gamblers, and village priests, || 160 ||
long-distance travelers, seafaring merchants, wandering ascetics, the sick,
hunters, learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>), those lacking good conduct, eunuchs, and performers, || 161 ||
atheists (<s>nāstika</s>), outcaste <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>vrātya</s>), those who have abandoned their wives, sacred fire, and sacrificial duties, those who sacrifice for the unworthy,
those who share a common kitchen, companions, enemies, relatives, and blood-relations, || 162 ||
those previously found guilty, actors, snake-charmers, and jugglers,
poisoners, arsonists, destroyers of embankments, <s>Śūdras</s>, sons of <s>Śūdra</s> women, and fallen persons, || 163 ||
the exhausted, the violent, the weary, the destitute, and those of the lowest occupations,
those of broken livelihood, those who have not completed their studies, the dull-witted, oil-pressers, and root-gatherers, || 164 ||
those possessed by spirits, those hated by the king, those who foretell rain and astral events,
those who confess sins, those who sell themselves, the maimed, and those who live by begging — || 165 ||
those with deformed nails, those with dark faces, those with leucoderma, betrayers of friends, rogues, and liquor-sellers,
sorcerers, the greedy, the fierce, and those opposed to guilds and corporations — || 166 ||
murderers, painters of deceptive pictures, wandering bards, outcasts, forgers,
deceivers, those of degraded occupations, thieves, and royal servants — || 167 ||
sellers of human beings, poisons, weapons, water, salt, cakes, and herbs,

children.text: vikretā brāhmaṇaś caiva dvijo vārdhuṣikaś ca yaḥ || 168 ||
children.translated_text: and also a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> engaged in trade, and a twice-born person who is a usurer — || 168 ||
one fallen from his own <s>dharma</s> (duty), a dishonest person, a flatterer, one who serves the low,

children.text: pitrā vivadamānaś ca bhedakṛc cety asākṣiṇaḥ || 169 ||
children.translated_text: one who disputes with his father, and one who creates dissension — all these are non-witnesses. || 169 ||
Those who have been declared non-witnesses, beginning with slaves and deceitful persons,
when the gravity of the case demands it, even they may serve as witnesses. || 170 ||
In all cases of violence (<s>sāhasa</s>), in cases of theft and receiving stolen goods,

children.text: pāruṣyayoś cāpy ubhayor na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ || 171 ||
children.translated_text: and in both kinds of assault (<s>pāruṣya</s>), one should not scrutinize the witnesses. || 171 ||

children.text: teṣām api na bālaḥ syān naiko na strī na kūṭakṛt |
children.translated_text: Even among those, a child should not be a witness, nor a single person, nor a woman, nor a forger;

children.text: na bāndhavo na cārātir brūyus te sākṣyam anyathā || 172 ||
children.translated_text: nor a relative, nor an enemy — for they would give false testimony. || 172 ||

children.text: bālo 'jñānād asatyāt strī pāpābhyāsāc ca kūṭakṛt |
children.translated_text: A child would testify falsely out of ignorance; a woman, out of untruthfulness; a forger, out of habitual sin;
a relative would speak falsely out of affection; an enemy, out of desire for revenge. || 173 ||
Or alternatively, one who is approved by both disputing parties,

children.text:
asākṣy eko 'pi sākṣitve praṣṭavyaḥ syāt sa saṃsadi || 174
                            ||
children.translated_text: even though otherwise disqualified, may be questioned as a witness in the assembly. || 174 ||

children.text: yas tv ātmadoṣabhinnatvād asvastha iva lakṣyate |
children.translated_text: One who, due to the disclosure of his own faults, appears as if disturbed,
who moves from one place to another, and runs up to each person individually, || 175 ||
who coughs without restraint, who sighs repeatedly without cause,

children.text: bhūmiṃ likhati pādābhyāṃ bāhu vāso dhunoti ca || 176 ||
children.translated_text: who scratches the ground with his feet, and shakes his arms and clothing, || 176 ||
whose facial color changes, whose forehead perspires,

children.text:
śoṣam āgacchataś coṣṭhāv ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca vīkṣate || 177
                            ||
children.translated_text: whose lips become dry, and who looks upward and sideways — || 177 ||
who speaks much and incoherently as if in haste, without being asked,

children.text: kūṭasākṣī sa vijñeyas taṃ pāpaṃ vinayen nṛpaḥ || 178 ||
children.translated_text: he should be recognized as a false witness (<s>kūṭasākṣin</s>) — the king should punish that wicked person. || 178 ||

children.text: śrāvayitvā ca yo 'nyebhyaḥ sākṣitvaṃ tad vinihnute |
children.translated_text: One who, having made others hear his testimony, then denies that witnessing,

children.text: sa vineyo bhṛśataraṃ kūṭasākṣyadhiko hi saḥ || 179 ||
children.translated_text: he should be punished most severely, for he is worse than a false witness. || 179 ||

children.text: āhūya sākṣiṇaḥ pṛcchen niyamya śapathair bhṛśam |
children.translated_text: Having summoned the witnesses, the judge should question them, binding them firmly with oaths,
all together, those whose conduct is known and whose understanding of the matter is established, each one separately. || 180 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be adjured by truth; a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by his vehicles and weapons;

children.text:
gobījakāñcanair vaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvais tu pātakaiḥ || 181
                            ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśya</s> by his cows, seeds, and gold; a <s>Śūdra</s> by all sins. || 181 ||
By reciting ancient <s>dharma</s> (law) texts, by proclaiming the greatness of truth,
and by denouncing falsehood, the witnesses should be thoroughly frightened. || 182 ||
Naked, shaven, holding a skull, begging for alms, afflicted by hunger and thirst,

children.text: dīnaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacched yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet || 183 ||
children.translated_text: wretched, he shall go to the house of his enemy — he who gives false testimony. || 183 ||
Confined in the city, starving at the outer gate,

children.text: amitrān bhūyaśaḥ paśyed yaḥ sākṣyam anṛtaṃ vadet || 184 ||
children.translated_text: he shall see enemies everywhere — he who gives false testimony. || 184 ||

children.text: yāṃ rātrim adhivinnā strī yāṃ caivākṣaparājitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The night that a woman who has been superseded by a co-wife experiences, and the night one who has been defeated at dice experiences,

children.text: yāṃ ca bhārābhitaptāṅgo durvivaktā sa tāṃ vaset || 185 ||
children.translated_text: and the night one whose limbs are scorched by heavy burdens experiences — such a night shall the false witness endure. || 185 ||
A witness who acts crookedly and evasively at the time of giving testimony,
binds upon himself a thousand nooses of <s>Varuṇa</s>. || 186 ||

children.text: tasya varṣaśate pūrṇe pāśam ekaṃ pramucyate |
children.translated_text: Upon the completion of a hundred years, one noose is released;

children.text: evaṃ sa bandhanāt tasmān mucyate niyutāḥ samāḥ || 187 ||
children.translated_text: thus he is freed from that bondage after a million years. || 187 ||

children.text: yāvato bāndhavāṃs yasmin hanti sākṣye 'nṛtaṃ vadan |
children.translated_text: As many kinsmen as one destroys by speaking falsehood in testimony,
hear, O gentle one, in order, the count of those destroyed in each case. || 188 ||

children.text: pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte |
children.translated_text: One destroys five by lying about cattle, ten by lying about cows,
one destroys a hundred by lying about horses, and a thousand by lying about a man. || 189 ||

children.text: hanti jātān ajātāṃś ca hiraṇyārthe 'nṛtaṃ vadan |
children.translated_text: One who speaks falsehood for the sake of gold destroys both those born and those unborn;

children.text: sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛte hanti mā sma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadīḥ || 190 ||
children.translated_text: by falsehood concerning land one destroys everything — do not speak falsehood concerning land! || 190 ||

children.text: ekam evādvitīyaṃ tat prāhuḥ pāvanam ātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: They declare that the one supreme purifier of the self, unequalled,

children.text: satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya naur iva || 191 ||
children.translated_text: is truth — the stairway to heaven, like a boat for crossing the ocean. || 191 ||

children.text: aśvamedhasahasraṃ ca satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam |
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifices) and truth were weighed on a balance;
truth indeed surpasses a thousand <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifices. || 192 ||

children.text: varaṃ kūpaśatād vāpi varaṃ vāpīśatāt kratuḥ |
children.translated_text: Better than a hundred wells is a tank, better than a hundred tanks is a sacrifice,

children.text: varaṃ kratuśatāt putraḥ satyaṃ putraśatād varam || 193 ||
children.translated_text: better than a hundred sacrifices is a son, and better than a hundred sons is truth. || 193 ||
The earth supports by truth, by truth the sun rises,

children.text: satyena vāyuḥ pavate satyenāpaḥ sravanti ca || 194 ||
children.translated_text: by truth the wind blows, and by truth the waters flow. || 194 ||

children.text: satyam eva paraṃ dānaṃ satyam eva paraṃ tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: Truth alone is the supreme gift, truth alone is the supreme <s>tapas</s> (austerity),

children.text: satyam eva paro dharmo lokānām iti naḥ śrutam || 195 ||
children.translated_text: truth alone is the supreme <s>dharma</s> (law) of the worlds — so we have heard. || 195 ||

children.text: satyaṃ devāḥ samāsena manuṣyās tv anṛtaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: In brief, truth is the gods, while falsehood is said to be the nature of humans;

children.text: ihaiva tasya devatvaṃ yasya satye sthitā matiḥ || 196 ||
children.translated_text: one whose mind is established in truth attains divinity even here in this world. || 196 ||

children.text: satyaṃ brūhy anṛtaṃ tyaktvā satyena svargam eṣyasi |
children.translated_text: Speak truth, abandon falsehood — by truth you shall attain heaven;
having spoken falsehood, one shall fall into terrible hell. || 197 ||

children.text: nirayeṣu ca te śaśvaj jihvām utkṛtya dāruṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: In the hells, the cruel and mighty servants of <s>Yama</s> shall forever
cut out your tongue and slash you with swords. || 198 ||
Enraged, they shall pierce you, crying out and helpless, with spears,
and casting you headlong downward, they shall hurl you into lakes of fire. || 199 ||

children.text: anubhūya ca duḥkhās tāś ciraṃ narakavedanāḥ |
children.translated_text: And having endured for a long time those painful sufferings of hell,
you shall be reborn here in wretched wombs of vultures, crows, and the like. || 200 ||

children.text: jñātvaitān anṛte doṣāñ jñātvā satye ca sadguṇān |
children.translated_text: Having known these faults of falsehood and having known the good qualities of truth,
speak truth and uplift yourself — do not cause yourself to fall! || 201 ||

children.text: na bāndhavā na suhṛdo na dhanāni mahānty api |
children.translated_text: Neither kinsmen, nor friends, nor even great wealth

children.text: alaṃ tārayituṃ śaktās tamasy ugre nimajjataḥ || 202 ||
children.translated_text: are able to rescue one who is sinking in terrible darkness. || 202 ||

children.text: pitaras tv avalambante tvayi sākṣitvam āgate |
children.translated_text: The ancestors are watching anxiously when you come as a witness:
'Will he save us, or will he cause himself to fall?' || 203 ||

children.text: satyam ātmā manuṣyasya satye sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam |
children.translated_text: Truth is the self of a man; everything is established in truth;
by all means you shall unite yourself with what is beneficial through your own self. || 204 ||

children.text: yāṃ ca rātrim ajaniṣṭhā yāṃ rātriṃ ca mariṣyasi |
children.translated_text: The night on which you were born and the night on which you shall die —

children.text:
vṛthā tadantaraṃ te syāt kuryāś cet satyam anyathā || 205
                            ||
children.translated_text: the interval between them would be in vain if you should render truth otherwise. || 205 ||

children.text: nāsti satyāt paro dharmo nānṛtāt pātakaṃ param |
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> (law) higher than truth, and no sin greater than falsehood;

children.text: sākṣidharme viśeṣeṇa satyam eva vadet tataḥ || 206 ||
children.translated_text: in the law of witnesses especially, one should therefore speak the truth. || 206 ||

children.text: yaḥ parārthe praharati svāṃ vācaṃ puruṣādhamaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, the lowest of men, perverts his speech for the sake of another —

children.text: ātmārthe kiṃ na kuryāt sa pāpo narakanirbhayaḥ || 207 ||
children.translated_text: what would that sinful wretch, without fear of hell, not do for his own sake? || 207 ||

children.text: arthā vai vāci niyatā vāṅmūlā vāgviniḥsṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Lawsuits are dependent on speech, rooted in speech, and issued from speech;

children.text: yo hy etāṃ stenayed vācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛn naraḥ || 208 ||
children.translated_text: he who steals this speech is a man who commits all theft. || 208 ||
When witnesses are in disagreement, the majority is authoritative;
when they are equal in number, those of good character are to be accepted; when those too are equal, those with better knowledge of the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition). || 209 ||
But where in a dispute equality among witnesses learned in <s>smṛti</s> is seen,
because of the subtlety of the law of witnesses, the testimony is set aside. || 210 ||

children.text: nirdiṣṭeṣv arthajāteṣu sākṣī cet sākṣyam āgataḥ |
children.translated_text: If a witness, having come to testify regarding the matters specified,

children.text: na brūyād akṣarasamaṃ na tan nigaditaṃ bhavet || 211 ||
