children.translated_text: does not state even a syllable's worth, that shall not be regarded as testimony. || 211 ||
Where there is disagreement regarding place, time, age, substance,

children.text: yatra vipratipattiḥ syāt sākṣyaṃ tad asad ucyate || 212 ||
children.translated_text: measure, appearance, or caste, that testimony is declared invalid. || 212 ||

children.text: ūnam abhyadhikaṃ cārthaṃ prabrūyur yatra sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where witnesses state an amount less or more than the actual claim,

children.text: tad apy anuktaṃ vijñeyam eṣa sākṣyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 213 ||
children.translated_text: that too should be known as not having been stated — this is the prescribed rule of testimony. || 213 ||

children.text: pramādād dhanino yatra na syāl lekhyaṃ na sākṣiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Where through negligence a wealthy person has neither a document nor witnesses,

children.text: arthaṃ cāpahnuyād vādī tatroktas trividho vidhiḥ || 214 ||
children.translated_text: and the defendant denies the claim, a threefold procedure is prescribed in that case. || 214 ||

children.text: codanā pratikālaṃ ca yuktileśas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: Demand, inference from circumstances, and also a trace of reasoning,

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ śapathaś coktas tair evaṃ sādhayet kramāt || 215 ||
children.translated_text: and the third is the oath — by these one should establish the case in order. || 215 ||

children.text: abhīkṣṇaṃ codyamāno yaḥ pratihanyān na tadvacaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, when repeatedly challenged, does not refute that statement
three, four, or five times — the claim shall be awarded against him thereafter. || 216 ||
When the demand is not refuted, one should pursue him with traces of reasoning,
through connections of place, time, subject matter, measure, action, and the like. || 217 ||

children.text: yuktiṣv apy asamarthāsu śapathair enam ardayet |
children.translated_text: When even reasoning proves insufficient, one should press him with oaths,
with due regard to the value, the time, and the strength of the case — by fire, water, merit, and other means. || 218 ||

children.text: dīptāgnir yaṃ na dahati yam antardhārayanty āpaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whom blazing fire does not burn and whom the waters hold up,

children.text: sa taraty abhiśāpaṃ taṃ kilbiṣī syād viparyaye || 219 ||
children.translated_text: he overcomes that accusation; in the contrary case he is guilty. || 219 ||
In charges against the chastity of women, in cases of theft and violence as well,

children.text: eṣa eva vidhir dṛṣṭaḥ sarvārthāpahnaveṣu ca || 220 ||
children.translated_text: this same procedure is prescribed, and also in all cases of denial. || 220 ||

children.text: śapathā hy api devānām ṛṣīṇām api ca smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Oaths are also known to have been taken by gods and sages;

children.text: vasiṣṭhaḥ śapathaṃ śepe yātudhāne tu śaṅkitaḥ || 221 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> took an oath when he was suspected of being a <s>Rākṣasa</s> (demon). || 221 ||
Likewise the Seven Sages, having assembled before <s>Indra</s> in the matter of <s>Puṣkara</s>,
took oaths calmly for the mutual purification of one another. || 222 ||

children.text: ayuktaṃ sāhasaṃ kṛtvā pratyāpattiṃ bhajeta yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, having committed an improper act of violence, repents

children.text: brūyāt svayaṃ vā sadasi tasyārdhavinayaḥ smṛtaḥ || 223 ||
children.translated_text: or confesses it himself in the assembly — for him, half the punishment is prescribed. || 223 ||

children.text: gūhamānas tu daurātmyād yadi pāpaṃ sa jīyate |
children.translated_text: But if one conceals wickedness out of depravity and is then convicted,

children.text: sabhyāś cātra na tuṣyanti tīvro daṇḍaś ca pātyate || 224 ||
children.translated_text: the assessors of the court are not satisfied, and a severe punishment is imposed. || 224 ||
Where one deposits one's own property with trust and without apprehension,

children.text: nikṣepo nāma tat proktaṃ vyavahārapadaṃ budhaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: that is called <s>nikṣepa</s> (deposit) — a title of law, according to the learned. || 1 ||
Property that is covered by other goods and that is not specifically described,
when deposited in another's house, is known as <s>aupanidhika</s> (sealed deposit). || 2 ||

children.text: sa punar dvividhaḥ proktaḥ sākṣimān itaras tathā |
children.translated_text: This is further declared to be of two kinds: with witnesses and without;
its return shall be proof, and in case of dispute, the opposite applies. || 3 ||

children.text: yācyamānas tu yo dātrā nikṣepaṃ na prayacchati |
children.translated_text: He who, when asked by the depositor, does not return the deposit

children.text: daṇḍyaḥ sa rājñā dāpyaś ca naṣṭe dāpyaś ca tatsamam || 4 ||
children.translated_text: shall be punished by the king and made to pay; if it is lost, he shall be made to pay the equivalent. || 4 ||

children.text: yaś cārthaṃ sādhayet tena nikṣeptur ananujñayā |
children.translated_text: And he who uses that property without the depositor's permission,

children.text: tatrāpi daṇḍyaḥ sa bhavet tac ca sodayam āvahet || 5 ||
children.translated_text: he too shall be punished in that case and shall restore it with interest. || 5 ||

children.text: grahītuḥ saha yo 'rthena naṣṭo naṣṭaḥ sa dāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: If the property is lost together with the receiver's own goods, it is likewise lost for the depositor;

children.text: daivarājakṛte tadvan na cet taj jihmakāritam || 6 ||
children.translated_text: this applies when it is due to an act of god, theft, or the king — but not if it was caused by fraud. || 6 ||
This same rule is prescribed for borrowed items, articles entrusted for delivery, and the like,
for deposits with artisans, for goods placed nearby, and for counter-deposits as well. || 7 ||

children.text: pratigṛhṇāti pogaṇḍaṃ yaś ca sapradhanaṃ naraḥ |
children.translated_text: And he who receives the property of a minor together with the principal,

children.text: tasyāpy eṣa bhaved dharmaḥ ṣaḍ ete vidhayaḥ samāḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: the same rule applies to him as well — these six procedures are equal. || 8 ||
Where merchants and others undertake work jointly,
that is known as <s>sambhūyasamutthāna</s> (partnership venture) — a title of law. || 1 ||
For those who jointly undertake work by some means for the sake of profit,
the investment is the basis, and they should therefore share profits in proportion to their shares. || 2 ||

children.text: samo 'tirikto hīno vā yatrāṃśo yasya yādṛśaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whether the share of each partner is equal, greater, or less,

children.text: kṣayavyayau tathā vṛddhis tasya tatra tathāvidhāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: his loss, expense, and profit shall be of the same proportion accordingly. || 3 ||
The inspection of goods, bulk expenditure, deduction of costs, burden, and quality
they should carry out faithfully, each abiding by their agreed terms. || 4 ||

children.text: pramādān nāśitaṃ dāpyaḥ pratiṣiddhakṛtaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: What is destroyed through negligence, and what is done against prohibition,

children.text: asandiṣṭaś ca yat kuryāt sarvaiḥ sambhūyakāribhiḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and what one does without authorization — all partners jointly shall make him pay. || 5 ||
When a calamity caused by divine agency, thieves, or the king arises,

children.text: yas tat svaśaktyā saṃrakṣet tasyāṃśo daśamaḥ smṛtaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: he who protects the goods by his own strength is entitled to a tenth share. || 6 ||

children.text: ekasya cet syād vyasanaṃ dāyādo 'sya tad āpnuyāt |
children.translated_text: If one partner suffers a calamity, his heir shall receive his share;

children.text: anyo vāsati dāyāde śaktāś cet sarva eva vā || 7 ||
children.translated_text: or in the absence of an heir, another, or if able, all the partners together. || 7 ||

children.text: ṛtvijāṃ vyasane 'py evam anyas tat karma nistaret |
children.translated_text: Likewise, if a calamity befalls one of the officiating priests, another shall complete the rite;
he shall receive the share of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) that was allotted from that. || 8 ||

children.text: ṛtvig yājyam aduṣṭaṃ yas tyajed anapakāriṇam |
children.translated_text: A priest who abandons an innocent sacrificer who has done no wrong,

children.text: aduṣṭaṃ va rtvijaṃ yājyo vineyau tāv ubhāv api || 9 ||
children.translated_text: or a sacrificer who abandons an innocent priest — both of them shall be punished. || 9 ||

children.text: ṛtvik tu trividho dṛṣṭaḥ pūrvajuṣṭaḥ svayaṅkṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: A priest is known to be of three kinds: one inherited from the family, one chosen by oneself,

children.text: yadṛcchayā ca yaḥ kuryād ārtvijyaṃ prītipūrvakam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: and one who performs the priestly office voluntarily out of affection. || 10 ||

children.text: kramāgateṣv eṣa dharmo vṛteṣv ṛtvikṣu ca svayam |
children.translated_text: This rule applies to priests inherited by succession and to those personally chosen;

children.text: yādṛcchike tu saṃyājye tattyāge nāsti kilbiṣam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: but in abandoning one who came voluntarily, there is no offense. || 11 ||

children.text: śulkasthānaṃ vaṇik prāptaḥ śulkaṃ dadyād yathopagam |
children.translated_text: A merchant who has reached a toll station should pay the toll as appropriate;

children.text: na tad vyatihared rājñāṃ balir eṣa prakalpitaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: he should not evade it, for this is the tribute established for kings. || 12 ||
One who bypasses the toll station, who buys or sells at the wrong time,
or who falsely states the quantity, shall be made to pay eight times the duty as a fine. || 13 ||

children.text: kaścic cet sañcaran deśāt preyād abhyāgato vaṇik |
children.translated_text: If a merchant traveling from another region should die on the way,

children.text: rājāsya bhāṇḍaṃ tad rakṣet yāvad dāyādadarśanam || 14 ||
children.translated_text: the king should protect his goods until his heirs appear. || 14 ||

children.text: dāyāde 'sati bandhubhyo jñātibhyo vā tad arpayet |
children.translated_text: In the absence of an heir, the goods should be given to relatives or kinsmen;

children.text: tadabhāve suguptaṃ tad dhārayed daśatīḥ samāḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: in their absence too, the goods should be kept safely for ten years. || 15 ||
After that, property that has remained for ten years without an owner or heir

children.text: rājā tad ātmasāt kuryād evaṃ dharmo na hīyate || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the king may appropriate for himself — thus <s>dharma</s> (law) is not violated. || 16 ||

children.text: dattvā dravyam asamyag yaḥ punar ādātum icchati |
children.translated_text: He who, having improperly given property, wishes to take it back again —
that is called <s>dattāpradānika</s> (resumption of gifts) — a title of dispute. || 1 ||

children.text: adeyam atha deyaṃ ca dattaṃ cādattam eva ca |
children.translated_text: What should not be given, what should be given, what has been given, and what has not been given —
in legal proceedings, the law of gifts should be known as fourfold. || 2 ||

children.text: tatra hyaṣṭāv adeyāni deyam ekavidhaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: Of these, there are eight things that should not be given, one kind that should be given,
seven kinds of gifts that are valid, and sixteen kinds of gifts that are invalid. || 3 ||

children.text: anvāhitaṃ yācitakam ādhiḥ sādhāraṇaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: An item entrusted for delivery, a borrowed article, a pledge, joint property,

children.text: nikṣepaḥ putradāraṃ ca sarvasvaṃ cānvaye sati || 4 ||
children.translated_text: a deposit, sons and wife, and the entire estate when there are heirs — || 4 ||

children.text: āpatsv api hi kaṣṭāsu vartamānena dehinā |
children.translated_text: even when one is in the most dire adversity,

children.text: adeyāny āhur ācāryā yac cānyasmai pratiśrutam || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the teachers declare these to be non-giveable, as well as what has been promised to another. || 5 ||
Whatever property remains after the maintenance of the family,

children.text: tad deyam upahṛtyānyad dadad doṣam avāpnuyāt || 6 ||
children.translated_text: that may be given; but one who gives otherwise incurs fault. || 6 ||
The price of goods, wages, a gift made out of satisfaction, out of affection, or as a return favor,
What is given for the benefit of a woman's bride-price (<s>strīśulka</s>) is known by those learned in giving as a gift. || 7 ||
But what is given by those afflicted with fear, anger, grief, agitation, or illness,
or through bribery (<s>utkoca</s>), jest, exchange, fraud, or deception — that is considered not given. || 8 ||
What is given by a child, a fool, one who is not independent, one who is distressed, one who is intoxicated, or one who is insane is excluded;

children.text: kartā mamāyaṃ karmeti pratilābhecchayā ca yat || 9 ||
children.translated_text: as is what is given saying 'this one shall be my agent' with the desire to receive something in return. || 9 ||

children.text: apātre pātram ity ukte kārye cādharmasaṃhite |
children.translated_text: When an unworthy recipient is declared to be worthy, or when the purpose is connected with <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),

children.text: yad dattaṃ syād avijñānād adattaṃ tad api smṛtam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: what is given through ignorance is also considered as not given. || 10 ||

children.text: gṛhṇāty adattaṃ yo lobhād yaś cādeyaṃ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: He who out of greed takes what is not given, and he who gives what should not be given —
the taker of what is not given deserves punishment, and likewise the giver of what should not be given. || 11 ||

children.text: abhyupetya tu śuśrūṣāṃ yas tāṃ na pratipadyate |
children.translated_text: He who, having undertaken service (<s>śuśrūṣā</s>), does not perform it —
this breach of contracted service is called a title of dispute (<s>vivādapada</s>). || 1 ||
A servant (<s>śuśrūṣaka</s>) is seen by the wise as being of five kinds in the <s>śāstra</s>,
a laborer (<s>karmakara</s>) is of four kinds, and slaves (<s>dāsa</s>) among them are fifteen. || 2 ||
A pupil (<s>śiṣya</s>), a resident student (<s>antevāsin</s>), a hired worker (<s>bhṛtaka</s>), and fourthly, a superintendent (<s>adhikarmakṛt</s>) —

children.text: ete karmakarāḥ proktā dāsās tu gṛhajādayaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: these are declared to be the laborers, while slaves are those born in the household and others. || 3 ||
The wise say that lack of independence is common to all of them,

children.text: jātikarmakṛtas tūkto viśeṣo vṛttir eva ca || 4 ||
children.translated_text: but the distinction is said to lie in whether their status arises from birth or from work, and also in their livelihood (<s>vṛtti</s>). || 4 ||

children.text: karmāpi dvividhaṃ jñeyam aśubhaṃ śubham eva ca |
children.translated_text: Work (<s>karma</s>) should also be known as twofold: impure (<s>aśubha</s>) and pure (<s>śubha</s>);
impure work is said to be the work of slaves, and pure work is that of laborers. || 5 ||
Cleaning of the house, the gate, impure places, the street, and the refuse heap;
touching the private parts, handling leftovers, excrement, and urine, and disposing of them; || 6 ||
attending upon the master's body as desired, and at the very end —

children.text: aśubhaṃ karma vijñeyaṃ śubham anyad ataḥ param || 7 ||
children.translated_text: this should be known as impure work; pure work is everything other than this. || 7 ||

children.text: ā vidyāgrahaṇāc chiṣyaḥ śuśrūṣet prayato gurum |
children.translated_text: A pupil (<s>śiṣya</s>) should serve the teacher (<s>guru</s>) with devotion until the completion of his studies;
his conduct should be the same toward the teacher's wife and the teacher's son. || 8 ||
A <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) should beg for alms, sleep on the ground, and wear no ornaments;
he should be the last to sleep and the first to rise among all in the teacher's house. || 9 ||

children.text: nāsandiṣṭaḥ pratiṣṭheta tiṣṭhed vāpi guruṃ kvacit |
children.translated_text: He should not stop unless instructed, nor should he ever stand still when the teacher is present;

children.text: sandiṣṭaḥ karma kurvīta śaktaś ced avicārayan || 10 ||
children.translated_text: when instructed, he should perform the task if capable, without questioning. || 10 ||

children.text: yathākālam adhīyīta yāvan na vimanā guruḥ |
children.translated_text: He should study at the proper time, as long as the teacher is not displeased,

children.text: āsīno 'dho guroḥ kūrce phalake vā samāhitaḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: seated below the teacher on a mat or a plank, with concentrated mind. || 11 ||

children.text: anuśāsyaś ca guruṇā na ced anuvidhīyate |
children.translated_text: If, being instructed by the teacher, he does not comply,
the teacher may, as a reprimand, strike him with a rope or a bamboo strip. || 12 ||

children.text: bhṛśaṃ na tāḍayed enaṃ nottamāṅge na vakṣasi |
children.translated_text: He should not strike him severely, nor on the head, nor on the chest;
the pupil should be disciplined and made trustworthy; otherwise the teacher should be punished by the king. || 13 ||
Having completed his studies (<s>samāvṛtta</s>) and having given the teacher's fee (<s>gurudakṣiṇā</s>),
he should return to his own home — this is declared to be the conduct of a pupil. || 14 ||
One who wishes to learn a craft (<s>śilpa</s>), with the permission of his relatives,

children.text: ācāryasya vased ante kālaṃ kṛtvā suniścitam || 15 ||
children.translated_text: should reside with the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), having fixed a definite period of time. || 15 ||
The teacher should instruct him, providing food from his own house,

children.text: na cānyat kārayet karma putravac cainam ācaret || 16 ||
children.translated_text: and should not make him do other work, treating him like a son. || 16 ||

children.text: śikṣayantam aduṣṭaṃ ca yas tv ācāryaṃ parityajet |
children.translated_text: But he who abandons a teacher who is instructing him and is blameless —

children.text: balād vāsayitavyaḥ syād vadhabandhau ca so 'rhati || 17 ||
children.translated_text: he should be forcibly made to reside there and deserves beating and imprisonment. || 17 ||
Even after being instructed, the resident student (<s>antevāsin</s>) should complete the fixed period;

children.text: tatra karma ca yat kuryād ācāryasyaiva tatphalam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever work he does there, the fruit of that belongs to the teacher alone. || 18 ||
Having learned the craft, at the appointed time, having circumambulated the teacher,
the apprentice should depart, honoring the teacher according to his ability. || 19 ||
A hired worker (<s>bhṛtaka</s>) should be known as threefold: superior, middling, and inferior;
their wages should correspond to their ability, devotion, and the nature of their work. || 20 ||

children.text: uttamas tv āyudhīyo 'tra madhyamas tu kṛṣīvalaḥ |
children.translated_text: The superior one here is a warrior, the middling one is a farmer,

children.text: adhamo bhāravāhaḥ syād ity evaṃ trividho bhṛtaḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: and the inferior one is a burden-carrier — thus the hired worker is of three kinds. || 21 ||

children.text: artheṣv adhikṛto yaḥ syāt kuṭumbasya tathopari |
children.translated_text: He who is appointed over affairs and over the household —

children.text: so 'dhikarmakaro jñeyaḥ sa ca kauṭumbikaḥ smṛtaḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: he should be known as the superintendent (<s>adhikarmakara</s>), and he is also called the household manager (<s>kauṭumbika</s>). || 22 ||
These four are declared to be laborers engaged in pure work;
but the remaining ones, engaged in impure work, are the fifteen kinds of slaves (<s>dāsa</s>). || 23 ||

children.text: gṛhajātas tathā krīto labdho dāyād upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: One born in the house (<s>gṛhaja</s>), one purchased (<s>krīta</s>), one obtained (<s>labdha</s>), one received through inheritance (<s>dāyāt</s>), one who has come of his own accord (<s>upāgata</s>),

children.text: anākālabhṛtas tadvad ādhattaḥ svāminā ca yaḥ || 24 ||
children.translated_text: likewise one maintained during a famine (<s>anākālabhṛta</s>), and one pledged by his master (<s>ādhatta</s>); || 24 ||

children.text: mokṣito mahataś carṇāt prāpto yuddhāt paṇe jitaḥ |
children.translated_text: one rescued from a great debt, one captured in war, one won in a wager,
one who has come saying 'I am yours,' one who has fallen from asceticism (<s>pravrajyāvasita</s>), and one who is made a slave; || 25 ||
a slave for food (<s>bhaktadāsa</s>) should also be recognized, likewise one maintained for a mare (<s>vaḍavābhṛta</s>),

children.text: vikretā cātmanaḥ śāstre dāsāḥ pañcadaśā smṛtāḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: and one who sells himself — in the <s>śāstra</s>, fifteen kinds of slaves are declared. || 26 ||

children.text: tatra pūrvaś caturvargo dāsatvān na vimucyate |
children.translated_text: Of these, the first group of four is not released from slavery,
except by the grace of the master — their slavery has come down in succession. || 27 ||

children.text: yaś caiṣāṃ svāminaṃ kaścin mokṣayet prāṇasaṃśayāt |
children.translated_text: And whoever among these should rescue the master from mortal danger,

children.text: dāsatvāt sa vimucyeta putrabhāgaṃ labheta ca || 28 ||
children.translated_text: he is released from slavery and should receive a son's share of the inheritance. || 28 ||
One maintained during a famine is released from slavery by giving a pair of oxen;

children.text:
sambhakṣitaṃ yad durbhikṣe na tac chudhyeta karmaṇā || 29
                            ||
children.translated_text: what was consumed during the famine cannot be purified by labor alone. || 29 ||

children.text: ādhatto 'pi dhanaṃ dattvā svāmī yady enam uddharet |
children.translated_text: Even one who is pledged, if the master redeems him by paying the amount,
or if he makes him approach voluntarily — he ranks next after one who is purchased. || 30 ||

children.text: dattvā tu sodayam ṛṇaṃ ṛṇī dāsyāt pramucyate |
children.translated_text: By paying the debt with interest, the debtor is released from slavery;
one who has agreed for a fixed period is also released upon its completion. || 31 ||

children.text: tavāham ity upagato yuddhaprāptaḥ paṇe jitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who has come saying 'I am yours,' one captured in war, and one won in a wager —
these are released by providing a substitute and performing equivalent service. || 32 ||

children.text: rājña eva tu dāsaḥ syāt pravrajyāvasito naraḥ |
children.translated_text: A man who has fallen from asceticism becomes a slave of the king alone;

children.text: na tasya pratimokṣo 'sti na viśuddhiḥ kathañcana || 33 ||
children.translated_text: there is no redemption for him, nor purification in any way. || 33 ||
By neglect of food, a food-slave (<s>bhaktadāsa</s>) is immediately released;
and by mistreatment of the mare, the mare-slave (<s>vaḍavābhṛta</s>) is released. || 34 ||

children.text: vikrīṇīte ya ātmānaṃ svatantraḥ san narādhamaḥ |
children.translated_text: A vile person who sells himself while being free —

children.text: sa jaghanyataras teṣāṃ naiva dāsyāt pramucyate || 35 ||
children.translated_text: he is the lowest among them and is never released from slavery. || 35 ||
Those who are stolen by thieves and sold, and those forcibly enslaved —

children.text: rājñā mokṣayitavyās te dāsatvaṃ teṣu neṣyate || 36 ||
children.translated_text: the king should set them free; slavery is not recognized in their case. || 36 ||
Slavery is not prescribed for those of higher <s>varṇa</s> (caste) in relation to those of lower;
except for one who abandons his own <s>dharma</s> — slavery is considered like marital dependency. || 37 ||
And one who is not independent and offers himself saying 'I am yours' —

children.text: na sa taṃ prāpnuyāt kāmaṃ pūrvasvāmī labheta tam || 38 ||
children.translated_text: the new master cannot claim him; the former master obtains him. || 38 ||

children.text: adhanās traya evoktā bhāryā dāsas tathā sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: Three are declared to be without property: a wife, a slave, and a son;

children.text: yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya tad dhanam || 39 ||
children.translated_text: whatever they acquire belongs to the one to whom they belong. || 39 ||

children.text: svadāsam icched yaḥ kartum adāsaṃ prītamānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, with a pleased mind, wishes to make his own slave a free man (<s>adāsa</s>) —

children.text: skandhād ādāya tasyāpi bhindyāt kumbhaṃ sahāmbhasā || 40 ||
children.translated_text: should take a water-pot from his shoulder and break it along with the water. || 40 ||
He should scatter unbroken rice grains and flowers upon his head,

children.text: adāsa iti coktvā triḥ prāṅmukhaṃ tam athotsṛjet || 41 ||
children.translated_text: and having declared three times 'you are not a slave,' he should release him facing east. || 41 ||
From that time on, he should be called one protected by the master's grace;

children.text: bhojyānnaḥ pratigṛhyaś ca bhavaty abhimataś ca saḥ || 42 ||
children.translated_text: he becomes one whose food may be accepted, one from whom gifts may be received, and one who is respected. || 42 ||
The procedure for giving and receiving wages of hired workers has been stated;
the nonpayment of wages (<s>vetanasyānapākarma</s>) is declared a title of dispute (<s>vivādapada</s>). || 1 ||
The employer (<s>karmasvāmin</s>) should pay the hired worker his wages in due order,

children.text: ādau madhye 'vasāne vā karmaṇo yad viniścitam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: at the beginning, middle, or end of the work, as was agreed upon. || 2 ||
But when the wages are not fixed, they should receive a tenth share
of the profits, cattle, seed, and crops — whether they are traders, cowherds, farmers, or laborers. || 3 ||

children.text: karmopakaraṇaṃ caiṣāṃ kriyāṃ prati yad āhṛtam |
children.translated_text: Whatever tools and implements are brought for performing their work,
they should handle them faithfully and not deal with them dishonestly. || 4 ||

children.text: karmākurvan pratiśrutya kāryo dattvā bhṛtiṃ balāt |
children.translated_text: One who, having promised, does not perform the work, should be compelled to do so by withholding the wages forcibly;
one who, having received the wages, does not perform the work, should pay double the wages. || 5 ||
If he abandons the work before the agreed time, he deserves loss of wages;
but if he departs due to the master's fault, he should receive wages for what has been done. || 6 ||
Having agreed upon one-sixth of the wages, one who abandons yoked work on the road,

children.text: adadat kārayitvā tu karmaivaṃ sodayāṃ bhṛtim || 7 ||
children.translated_text: or one who, having had the work done, does not pay — should pay the wages with interest. || 7 ||
One who, having hired a vehicle or conveyance for goods, does not deliver them,
should be made to pay one-fourth of the wages if he abandons the work midway, or the full amount. || 8 ||
A carrier who likewise does not deliver should suffer loss of wages;

children.text: dviguṇāṃ tu bhṛtiṃ dāpyaḥ prasthāne vighnam ācaran || 9 ||
children.translated_text: but one who creates an obstruction at the time of departure should be made to pay double the wages. || 9 ||
If goods meet with disaster due to the carrier's fault,

children.text: dāpyo yat tatra naṣṭaṃ syād daivarājakṛtād ṛte || 10 ||
children.translated_text: he should be made to pay for what is lost there, except when caused by fate or the king. || 10 ||

children.text: gavāṃ śatād vatsatarī dhenuḥ syād dviśatād bhṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: For a hundred cows, a heifer is the wages of a cowherd; for two hundred, a milch cow;
this is per year, and every eighth day the cowherd may milk them. || 11 ||
One should bring the cows to the cowherd every day at daybreak,

children.text: cīṛṇāḥ pītāś ca tā gopaḥ sāyāhne pratyupānayet || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and the cowherd should bring them back in the evening after they have grazed and drunk. || 12 ||

children.text: syāc ced govyasanaṃ gopo vyāyacchet tatra śaktitaḥ |
children.translated_text: If a calamity befalls the cows, the cowherd should exert himself to the best of his ability;

children.text: aśaktas tūrṇam āgamya svāmine tan nivedayet || 13 ||
children.translated_text: but if unable, he should quickly come and report it to the master. || 13 ||
A cowherd who does not exert himself, does not cry out for help, and does not report to the master,

children.text: voḍhum arhati gopas tāṃ vinayaṃ cāpi rājani || 14 ||
children.translated_text: deserves to bear the loss and also punishment from the king. || 14 ||
An animal that is lost, destroyed, killed by worms, killed by dogs, or that dies in rough terrain,
or that perishes due to lack of human effort — the loss falls upon the cowherd alone. || 15 ||

children.text: ajāvike tathāruddhe vṛkaiḥ pāle tv anāyati |
children.translated_text: When sheep and goats are penned and wolves attack while the herdsman does not bring them in,

children.text: yat prasahya vṛko hanyāt pāle tatkilbiṣam bhavet || 16 ||
children.translated_text: whatever a wolf kills by force — that is the herdsman's fault. || 16 ||
But when they are unpenned and wandering together in the forest,

children.text: yām utpatya vṛko hanyān na pālas tatra kilbiṣī || 17 ||
children.translated_text: whichever one a wolf kills by pouncing — the herdsman is not at fault in that case. || 17 ||

children.text: vighuṣya tu hṛtaṃ caurair na pālo dātum arhati |
children.translated_text: Having raised an alarm, the herdsman is not liable to pay for what is stolen by thieves,

children.text: yadi deśe ca kāle ca svāminaḥ svasya śaṃsati || 18 ||
children.translated_text: if he reports to the master the place and the time without delay. || 18 ||
By this, the dispute concerning all herdsmen has been stated;
and in the case of animals that have died, the herdsman's innocence is established by showing the brand marks and other identifying signs. || 19 ||

children.text: śulkaṃ gṛhītvā paṇyastrī necchantī dvis tad āvahet |
children.translated_text: A courtesan (<s>paṇyastrī</s>) who, having received the fee (<s>śulka</s>), is unwilling, should return it twofold;

children.text: aprayacchaṃs tadā śulkam anubhūya pumān striyam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: and a man who, having enjoyed the woman, does not pay the fee — || 20 ||

children.text: ayonau kramate yas tu bahubhir vāpi vāsayet |
children.translated_text: he who uses her in an unnatural manner, or makes her serve many men,

children.text: śulkam aṣṭaguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayas tāvad eva ca || 21 ||
children.translated_text: should be made to pay eight times the fee, and the punishment should be equally severe. || 21 ||

children.text: parājire gṛhaṃ kṛtvā stomaṃ dattvā vaset tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who builds a house on another's land, and having paid rent (<s>stoma</s>), resides there,
he should take away the thatch, wood, bricks, and other materials when he departs. || 22 ||
Goods for which rent has been paid should be returned when the period is complete;

children.text: grahītur ābhaved bhagnaṃ naṣṭaṃ cānyatra samplavāt || 23 ||
children.translated_text: would be broken or lost elsewhere due to flooding for the receiver. || 23 ||

children.text: nikṣiptaṃ vā paradravyaṃ naṣṭaṃ labdhvāpahṛtya vā |
children.translated_text: Whether it is deposited property of another, or lost and found, or seized,
that which is sold secretly is to be understood as <s>asvāmivikraya</s> (sale by a non-owner). || 1 ||
The owner, having recovered property sold by a non-owner, shall obtain it back;

children.text:
prakāśaṃ krayataḥ śuddhiḥ kretuḥ steyaṃ rahaḥ krayāt || 2
                            ||
children.translated_text: purity comes from buying openly; buying secretly constitutes theft for the buyer. || 2 ||

children.text: asvāmyanumatād dāsād asataś ca janād rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: From a slave without his master's consent, or from a dishonest person, secretly,
one who buys at a low price and at an improper time shall be liable for that fault. || 3 ||

children.text: na gūhetāgamaṃ kretā śuddhis tasya tadāgamāt |
children.translated_text: A buyer should not conceal the source of acquisition; his purity comes from declaring that source;
in the opposite case, he is equally guilty and deserves the punishment for theft. || 4 ||

children.text: vikretā svāmine 'rthaṃ ca kretur mūlyaṃ ca tatkṛtam |
children.translated_text: The seller shall give the property to the owner and the price paid to the buyer;

children.text: dadyād daṇḍaṃ tathā rājñe vidhir asvāmivikraye || 5 ||
children.translated_text: he shall also pay a fine to the king — this is the rule in cases of sale by a non-owner. || 5 ||

children.text: pareṇa nihitaṃ labdhvā rājany upaharen nidhim |
children.translated_text: Having found a treasure deposited by another, one should present it to the king;

children.text: rājagāmī nidhiḥ sarvaḥ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte || 6 ||
children.translated_text: all treasure belongs to the king, for everyone except a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 6 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇo 'pi nidhiṃ labdhvā kṣipraṃ rājñe nivedayet |
children.translated_text: Even a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having found a treasure, should promptly report it to the king;

children.text: tena dattaṃ ca bhūñjīta stenaḥ syād anivedayan || 7 ||
children.translated_text: he may enjoy what is given by the king, but one who does not report it becomes a thief. || 7 ||

children.text: svam apy arthaṃ tathā naṣṭaṃ labdhvā rājñe nivedayet |
children.translated_text: Likewise, having found one's own lost property, one should report it to the king;

children.text:
gṛhṇīyāt tatra taṃ śuddham aśuddhaṃ syāt tato 'nyathā || 8
                            ||
children.translated_text: one may take it there as purified, but otherwise it would be impure. || 8 ||

children.text: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yan na pradīyate |
children.translated_text: When goods sold for a price are not delivered to the buyer,
that non-delivery after sale is called a topic of dispute. || 1 ||

children.text: loke 'smin dvividhaṃ dravyaṃ jaṅgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: In this world, property is of two kinds: movable and immovable;
all of that is called merchandise in the laws of buying and selling. || 2 ||

children.text: ṣaḍvidhas tasya tu budhair dānādānavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise have declared the method of giving and receiving to be sixfold:

children.text: gaṇimaṃ tulimaṃ meyaṃ kriyayā rūpataḥ śriyā || 3 ||
children.translated_text: by counting, by weighing, by measuring, by action, by appearance, and by quality. || 3 ||

children.text: vikrīya paṇyaṃ mūlyena kretur yo na prayacchati |
children.translated_text: One who sells goods for a price and does not deliver them to the buyer
shall be made to pay the loss for immovable property and the product of labor for movable property. || 4 ||

children.text: arghaś ced apahīyeta sodayaṃ paṇyam āvahet |
children.translated_text: If the price were to decline, the seller should take back the goods with interest;
this rule applies to stationary goods; for goods that travel, the profit belongs to the destination. || 5 ||
If the goods are destroyed, or burned, or carried away,
that loss belongs to the seller alone who sells but does not deliver. || 6 ||

children.text: nirdoṣaṃ darśayitvā tu sadoṣaṃ yaḥ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: One who shows something faultless but delivers something faulty

children.text: mūlyaṃ taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vinayaṃ tāvad eva ca || 7 ||
children.translated_text: shall be made to pay double the price, and an equal amount as penalty. || 7 ||
Likewise, one who sells to one person but delivers to another

children.text: so 'pi taddviguṇaṃ dāpyo vineyas tāvad eva ca || 8 ||
children.translated_text: shall also be made to pay double that amount, and shall be punished equally. || 8 ||

children.text: dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇāti krītaṃ paṇyaṃ ca yaḥ krayī |
children.translated_text: If a buyer does not accept goods that are being delivered after purchase,
the seller, selling them elsewhere, shall not be at fault. || 9 ||
This is the declared rule for goods whose price has been paid;
when the price has not been paid, except by agreement, there is no transgression by the seller. || 10 ||
For the sake of profit, merchants engage in buying and selling of all goods;

children.text: sa ca lābho 'rgham āsādya mahān bhavati vā na vā || 11 ||
children.translated_text: and that profit, depending on the market price, may be great or not. || 11 ||

children.text: tasmād deśe ca kāle ca vaṇig arghaṃ parākramet |
children.translated_text: Therefore, a merchant should strive for the right price according to place and time;

children.text: na jihmena pravarteta śreyān evaṃ vaṇikpathaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: he should not proceed by crooked means — thus the path of the merchant is honorable. || 12 ||

children.text: krītvā mūlyena yaḥ paṇyaṃ kretā na bahu manyate |
children.translated_text: When a buyer, having purchased goods for a price, does not value them,
that is called <s>krītānuśaya</s> (reneging on a purchase), a topic of dispute. || 1 ||

children.text: krītvā mūlyena yat paṇyaṃ duṣkrītaṃ manyate krayī |
children.translated_text: When a buyer considers goods purchased for a price to be a bad purchase,

children.text: vikretuḥ pratideyaṃ tat tasminn evāhny avikṣatam || 2 ||
children.translated_text: they are to be returned to the seller on the same day, undamaged. || 2 ||

children.text: dvitīye 'hni dadat kretā mūlyāt triṃśāṃśam āvahet |
children.translated_text: A buyer returning on the second day shall forfeit one-thirtieth of the price;

children.text: dviguṇaṃ tat tṛtīye 'hni parataḥ kretur eva tat || 3 ||
children.translated_text: double that on the third day; after that, the goods belong to the buyer. || 3 ||

children.text: kretā paṇyaṃ parīkṣeta prāk svayaṃ guṇadoṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: A buyer should examine the goods beforehand, personally, for their merits and faults;

children.text: parīkṣyābhimataṃ krītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: once examined and approved, what is purchased shall not revert to the seller. || 4 ||

children.text: tryahād dohyaṃ parīkṣeta pañcāhād vāhyam eva tu |
children.translated_text: Milch animals should be tested for three days, beasts of burden for five days;
for pearls, diamonds, and coral, the period of examination shall be seven days. || 5 ||

children.text: dvipadām ardhamāsaṃ syāt puṃsāṃ taddviguṇaṃ striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: For bipeds, it shall be half a month; for men, double that for women;
ten days for all seeds, and one day for metals and cloth. || 6 ||

children.text: paribhuktaṃ ca yad vāsaḥ kliṣṭarūpaṃ malīmasam |
children.translated_text: A garment that has been used, worn-looking, and soiled,

children.text: sadoṣam api vikrītaṃ vikretur na bhavet punaḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: even if sold with defects, shall not revert to the seller. || 7 ||
One-eighth of the price is deducted for a cloth washed once;

children.text:
dviḥ pādas tris tribhāgas tu catuḥkṛtvo 'rdham eva ca || 8
                            ||
children.translated_text: one-quarter for twice washed, three-quarters for thrice, and half for washed four times. || 8 ||
After the half is exhausted, the deduction decreases by a quarter-part in sequence,
until it is worn out to the tenth degree; for a completely worn garment, there is no fixed rule on depreciation. || 9 ||
For all metals too, the cause of loss is in the process of working with fire;
the loss of metals being refined is observed from contact with fire. || 10 ||

children.text: suvarṇasya kṣayo nāsti rajate dvipalaṃ śatam |
children.translated_text: There is no loss for gold; for silver, two <s>palas</s> per hundred;

children.text: śatam aṣṭapalaṃ jñeyaṃ kṣayas syāt trapusīsayoḥ || 11 ||
children.translated_text: the loss for tin and lead should be known as eight <s>palas</s> per hundred. || 11 ||

children.text: tāmre pañcapalaṃ vidyād vikārā ye ca tanmayāḥ |
children.translated_text: For copper, one should know it to be five <s>palas</s>, and for alloys made thereof;
due to the diversity of their constituent metals, there is no fixed rule for the loss of iron. || 12 ||
In the processing of textiles, both loss and gain are stated:
for thread, cotton, and wool, the gain is ten <s>palas</s> per hundred. || 13 ||
For those with coarse thread, the gain is five per hundred for medium ones;
for very fine ones, the inner loss is stated as three <s>palas</s>. || 14 ||
One-thirtieth is the loss for hair-pierced textiles and those worked upon;

children.text: kauṣeyavalkalānāṃ tu naiva vṛddhir na ca kṣayaḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: but for silk and bark-cloth, there is neither gain nor loss. || 15 ||
A merchant skilled in goods should not renege after purchasing;

children.text: vṛddhikṣayau tu jānīyāt paṇyānām āgamaṃ tathā || 16 ||
children.translated_text: he should know the gain and loss, and likewise the source of the goods. || 16 ||
The established practice of heretical sects, guilds, and the like is called a convention;
the nonobservance of a convention is regarded as a topic of dispute. || 1 ||
Among heretical sects, guilds, corporations, associations, fraternities, and other groups,

children.text: saṃrakṣet samayaṃ rājā durge janapade tathā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: the king should protect their conventions, both in the fort and in the countryside. || 2 ||

children.text: yo dharmaḥ karma yac caiṣām upasthānavidhiś ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever is their <s>dharma</s> (law), their customary practice, and their rule of attendance,

children.text: yac caiṣāṃ vṛttyupādānam anumanyeta tat tathā || 3 ||
children.translated_text: and whatever is their means of livelihood — the king should approve all that accordingly. || 3 ||

children.text: pratikūlaṃ ca yad rājñaḥ prakṛtyavamataṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: But whatever is hostile to the king, or despised by the subjects,

children.text: bādhakaṃ ca yad arthānāṃ tat tebhyo vinivartayet || 4 ||
children.translated_text: or harmful to property — that the king should cause them to abandon. || 4 ||
Mutual conspiracy, carrying weapons for harmful purposes,

children.text: parasparopaghātaṃ ca teṣāṃ rājā na marṣayet || 5 ||
children.translated_text: and mutual injury — the king should not tolerate these among them. || 5 ||

children.text: pṛthag gaṇāṃś ca ye bhindyus te vineyā viśeṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who would separately split the groups should be punished especially;

children.text: āvaheyur bhayaṃ ghoraṃ vyādhivat te hy upekṣitāḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: for if neglected, they would bring terrible danger, like a disease. || 6 ||
Whatever practice is harmful and not sanctioned by tradition,

children.text: pravṛttam api tad rājā śreyaskāmo nivartayet || 7 ||
children.translated_text: even if already in effect, a king desiring welfare should put a stop to it. || 7 ||
Matters concerning embankments, rice-fields, boundaries, and determinations of cultivated and uncultivated land,

children.text: kṣetrādhikārā yatra syur vivādaḥ kṣetrajas tu saḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: where there are disputes about rights over fields — that is called a dispute arising from land. || 1 ||
In disputes over field boundaries, the decision comes from the neighbors:
the headmen of towns and villages, and the most elderly persons. || 2 ||

children.text: grāmasīmāsu ca bahir ye syus tatkṛṣijīvinaḥ |
children.translated_text: And those who live by farming outside the village boundaries,
cowherds, fowlers, hunters, and others who frequent the forest — || 3 ||
they should demarcate the boundary, identified by markers:
husks, charcoal, potsherds, jars, shrines, and trees. || 4 ||
And by well-known features such as anthills, elevations, depressions, and the like,
and by ancient rice-fields, gardens, paths, and embankments. || 5 ||
In lands whose marks have been carried away by rivers, abandoned, or lost,
determination should be made by inference from the locality, by evidence, and by witness of enjoyment. || 6 ||

children.text: atha ced anṛtaṃ brūyuḥ sāmantās tadviniścaye |
children.translated_text: But if the neighbors should speak falsehood in that determination,

children.text: sarve pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: they should each be individually fined by the king with the middle <s>sāhasa</s> (amercement). || 7 ||

children.text: gaṇavṛddhādayas tv anye daṇḍaṃ dāpyāḥ pṛthak pṛthak |
children.translated_text: The elders of the group and others should be made to pay fines individually;
those who persist in falsehood should be punished with the first <s>sāhasa</s> (amercement). || 8 ||

children.text: naikaḥ samunnayet sīmāṃ naraḥ pratyayavān api |
children.translated_text: A single person, even if trustworthy, should not demarcate the boundary;

children.text: gurutvād asya dharmasya kriyaiṣā bahuṣu sthitā || 9 ||
children.translated_text: due to the gravity of this matter, this procedure is established among many. || 9 ||

children.text: ekaś ced unnayet sīmāṃ sopavāsaḥ samāhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: If a single person were to demarcate the boundary, he should do so while fasting and concentrated,
wearing red garlands and red garments, placing earth upon his head. || 10 ||

children.text: yadā ca na syur jñātāraḥ sīmāyā na ca lakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: When there are no persons who know the boundary, nor any markers,

children.text: tadā rājā dvayoḥ sīmām uddhared iṣṭataḥ svayam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: then the king himself should demarcate the boundary between the two parties as he sees fit. || 11 ||
By this same method, the rule for disputes concerning houses, gardens, wells, and shrines
has been declared, and likewise for disputes between villages. || 12 ||
With rubbish heaps, pits, ditches, drains, and the like,
one should not obstruct crossroads, temple grounds, streets, and pathways. || 13 ||

children.text: parakṣetrasya madhye tu setur na pratiṣidhyate |
children.translated_text: An embankment in the middle of another's field is not prohibited,

children.text: mahāguṇo 'lpabādhaś ca vṛddhir iṣṭā kṣaye sati || 14 ||
children.translated_text: provided it is of great benefit and causes little harm — increase is desirable where there is decline. || 14 ||

children.text: setus tu dvididho jñeyaḥ kheyo bandhyas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: An embankment should be known as twofold: one for digging and one for damming;
it is for digging when it directs water flow, and for damming when it stops it. || 15 ||
Without water, crops perish, but they also perish from excess water;

children.text: ya evānudake doṣaḥ sa evābhyudake smṛtaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the fault that exists in the absence of water is the same as that declared for excess water. || 16 ||

children.text: pūrvapravṛttam utsannam apṛṣṭvā svāminaṃ tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who, without asking the owner, restores an embankment that was previously established but had fallen into disuse,

children.text: setuṃ pravartayet kaścin na sa tatphalabhāg bhavet || 17 ||
children.translated_text: shall not receive the fruits thereof. || 17 ||

children.text: mṛte tu svāmini punas tadvaṃśye vāpi mānave |
children.translated_text: But when the owner has died, or if there is a person of his lineage,

children.text: rājānam āmantrya tataḥ prakuryāt setukarma tat || 18 ||
children.translated_text: one should inform the king and then undertake that embankment work. || 18 ||
Otherwise, one would suffer hardship, following the analogy of the deer-hunter:

children.text: iṣavas tasya naśyanti yo viddham anuvidhyati || 19 ||
children.translated_text: the arrows of one who shoots an already-wounded animal are lost. || 19 ||
When the field owners are incapable, deceased, or have disappeared, without prohibition,

children.text: kṣetraṃ ced vikṛṣet kaścid aśnuvīta sa tatphalam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: if someone cultivates the field, he shall enjoy the fruits thereof. || 20 ||

children.text: vikṛṣyamāṇe kṣetre cet kṣetrikaḥ punar āvrajet |
children.translated_text: But if the field owner returns while the field is being cultivated,

children.text: khilopacāraṃ tat sarvaṃ dattvā svakṣetram āpnuyāt || 21 ||
children.translated_text: he shall recover his own field after paying all the costs of restoring the fallow land. || 21 ||
With a deduction of one-eighth of that each year, until seven years have passed;

children.text:
samprāpte tv aṣṭame varṣe bhuktaṃ kṣetraṃ labheta saḥ || 22
                            ||
children.translated_text: but upon the arrival of the eighth year, the cultivator shall obtain the field he has enjoyed. || 22 ||
In one year it becomes half-fallow; in three years it becomes fully fallow;
A field neglected for five years becomes like a wilderness. || 23 ||

children.text: kṣetraṃ tripuruṣaṃ yat syād gṛhaṃ vā syāt kramāgatam |
children.translated_text: A field that has been held for three generations, or a house that has come down by succession,

children.text: rājaprasādād anyatra na tadbhogaḥ paraṃ nayet || 24 ||
children.translated_text: except by royal grant, its enjoyment should not be taken to another. || 24 ||

children.text: utkramya tu vṛtiṃ yatra sasyaghāto gavādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Where, through transgression of the boundary, there is destruction of crops by cattle and the like,

children.text: pālaḥ śāsyo bhavet tatra na cec chaktyā nivārayet || 25 ||
children.translated_text: the herdsman should be punished there, if he does not prevent it when able. || 25 ||
When there is destruction of crops along with their roots, the owner of those [cattle] shall receive an equal [fine];

children.text: vadhena pālo mucyeta daṇḍaṃ svāmini pātayet || 26 ||
children.translated_text: the herdsman shall be released from corporal punishment, and the fine shall be imposed upon the owner. || 26 ||
A cow that has recently calved within ten days, great bulls, goats, sheep, and elephants,

children.text: nivāryās tu prayatnena teṣāṃ svāmī na daṇḍabhāk || 27 ||
children.translated_text: should be restrained with effort; their owner is not liable for a fine. || 27 ||

children.text: māṣaṃ gāṃ dāpayed daṇḍaṃ dvau māṣau mahiṣīṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: For a cow, one should impose a fine of one <s>māṣa</s>; for a buffalo, two <s>māṣas</s> likewise;

children.text: ajāvike savatse tu daṇḍaḥ syād ardhamāṣakaḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: for goats and sheep with their young, the fine shall be half a <s>māṣaka</s>. || 28 ||

children.text: adaṇḍyā hastino 'śvāś ca prajāpālā hi te smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Elephants and horses are not to be fined, for they are considered protectors of the people;

children.text: adaṇḍyā garbhiṇī gauś ca sūtikā cābhisāriṇī || 29 ||
children.translated_text: nor is a pregnant cow to be fined, nor a cow that has recently calved, nor one that is roaming. || 29 ||

children.text: proktas tu dvir niṣaṇṇānāṃ vasantyāṃ tu caturguṇam |
children.translated_text: For those [cattle] that sit down twice [in a field], the fine is declared doubled; in the spring season, it is fourfold;
for those caught grazing openly, the punishment of a thief is prescribed. || 30 ||

children.text: yā naṣṭāḥ pāladoṣeṇa gāvaḥ kṣetraṃ samāśritāḥ |
children.translated_text: Cattle that are lost through the herdsman's fault and have entered a field,

children.text: na tatra gomino daṇḍaḥ pālas taṃ daṇḍam arhati || 31 ||
children.translated_text: for those the cattle owner incurs no fine; the herdsman deserves that fine. || 31 ||
Or seized by the king's officers, or struck by thunderbolt and lightning,

children.text: atha sarpeṇa daṣṭo vā giry agrāt patito 'pi vā || 32 ||
children.translated_text: or bitten by a serpent, or fallen from a mountain peak, || 32 ||
or killed by a lion or tiger, or felled by diseases,

children.text: na tatra doṣaḥ pālasya na ca doṣo 'sti gominām || 33 ||
children.translated_text: in such cases there is no fault of the herdsman, nor is there any fault of the cattle owners. || 33 ||

children.text: gobhis tu bhakṣitaṃ dhānyaṃ yo naraḥ pratimārgati |
children.translated_text: A man who tracks back grain eaten by cattle,

children.text: sāmantasya śado deyo dhānyaṃ yat tatra vāpitam |
children.translated_text: should give a share to the neighboring field owner, and the grain that was sown there;

children.text: gavatraṃ gomine deyaṃ dhānyaṃ tatkarṣikasya tu || 34 ||
children.translated_text: the fodder for the cattle should be given to the cattle owner, and the grain to the cultivator. || 34 ||

children.text: grāmopānte ca yat kṣetraṃ vivītānte mahāpathe |
children.translated_text: A field that is on the outskirts of a village, at the edge of a pasture, or on a highway,

children.text: anāvṛte cet tannāśe na pālasya vyatikramaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: if it is unenclosed, when there is damage to it, there is no transgression on the part of the herdsman. || 35 ||

children.text: pathi kṣetre vṛtiḥ kāryā yām uṣṭro nāvalokayet |
children.translated_text: A fence should be made on the path and field such that a camel cannot look over it,

children.text: na laṅghayet paśur nāśvo na bhidyād yāṃ ca sūkaraḥ || 36 ||
children.translated_text: a domestic animal or horse cannot leap over it, and a pig cannot break through it. || 36 ||

children.text: gṛhaṃ kṣetraṃ ca vijñeyaṃ vāsahetuḥ kuṭumbinām |
children.translated_text: A house and a field should be known as the basis of livelihood for householders;

children.text: tasmāt tan nākṣiped rājā tad dhi mūlaṃ kuṭumbinām || 37 ||
children.translated_text: therefore the king should not destroy them, for they are the foundation of householders. || 37 ||

children.text: vṛddhe janapade rājño dharmaḥ kośaś ca vardhate |
children.translated_text: When the population grows, the king's <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and treasury increase;

children.text: hīyate hīyamāne ca vṛddhihetum ataḥ śrayet || 38 ||
children.translated_text: they diminish when the population diminishes; therefore one should foster the cause of growth. || 38 ||

children.text: vivāhādividhiḥ strīṇāṃ yatra puṃsāṃ ca kīrtyate |
children.translated_text: Where the rules beginning with marriage for women and men are declared,
this topic of litigation is called <s>Strīpuṃsayoga</s> (relations between men and women). || 1 ||

children.text: strīpuṃsayos tu sambandhād varaṇaṃ prāg vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: From the union of a man and a woman, betrothal is first ordained;
from betrothal comes the taking of the hand, and then the consecration is of two kinds. || 2 ||
Of these two, betrothal is declared to be revocable, on account of the perception of defects;
by the taking of the hand and the mantras, the mark of wifehood is irrevocable. || 3 ||

children.text: svajātyā śreyasī bhāryā svajātyaś ca patiḥ striyāḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: a wife of one's own <s>varṇa</s> (caste) is the best, and a husband of one's own <s>varṇa</s> is best for a woman. || 4 ||
For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the order of <s>anuloma</s> (with the grain), there are three other wives;
for a <s>Śūdrā</s> woman, in the order of <s>pratiloma</s> (against the grain), there are likewise three other husbands. || 5 ||
A <s>Kṣatriya</s> has two other wives; for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, one is declared;

children.text: vaiśyāyā dvau patī jñeyāv eko 'nyaḥ kṣatriyāpatiḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśyā</s> woman may have two husbands, and a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> woman one other husband. || 6 ||

children.text: ā saptamāt pañcamād vā bandhubhyaḥ pitṛmātṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Up to the seventh or fifth degree of kinship on the father's and mother's side,
those of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage) and those of the same <s>pravara</s> (ancestral lineage) are not marriageable. || 7 ||
A man should be tested for virility by his own bodily characteristics;

children.text: pumāṃś ced avikalpena sa kanyāṃ labdhum arhati || 8 ||
children.translated_text: if he is undoubtedly a man, he deserves to obtain a maiden. || 8 ||
One whose collar-bones, knees, and bones are well-knit, whose shoulders and neck are well-formed,
who has a thick neck, thin body and skin, and an unimpeded gait and voice, || 9 ||

children.text: viṭ cāsya plavate nāpsu hlādi mūtraṃ ca phenilam |
children.translated_text: whose excrement floats on water, whose urine is pleasant and frothy,

children.text: pumān syāṃl lakṣaṇair etair viparītais tu paṇḍakaḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: by these characteristics he is a man; by the opposite characteristics, he is a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch). || 10 ||

children.text: caturdaśavidhaḥ śāstre sa tu dṛṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: He is seen to be of fourteen kinds in the <s>śāstra</s> (legal treatise) by the wise;

children.text: cikitsyaś cācikitsyaś ca teṣām ukto vidhiḥ kramāt || 11 ||
children.translated_text: some are curable and some incurable; their treatment is stated in order. || 11 ||

children.text: nisargapaṇḍo vadhriś ca pakṣapaṇḍas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>nisargapaṇḍa</s> (congenital eunuch) and the <s>vadhri</s> (castrated one), and likewise the <s>pakṣapaṇḍa</s> (periodic eunuch),

children.text: abhiśāpād guro rogād devakrodhāt tathaiva ca || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and those [impotent] from a curse, from a teacher's [curse], from disease, and from divine wrath likewise, || 12 ||

children.text: īrṣyāpaṇḍaś ca sevyaś ca vātaretā mukhebhagaḥ |
children.translated_text: and the <s>īrṣyāpaṇḍa</s> (one impotent from jealousy), the <s>sevya</s> (one who serves sexually), the <s>vātaretā</s> (one whose semen is expelled by wind), the <s>mukhebhaga</s> (one who practices oral sex),

the <s>ākṣipta</s> (one distracted by another), the <s>moghabīja</s> (one with ineffective seed), the <s>śālīna</s> (the bashful one), and the <s>anyapati</s> (one who is husband to another) likewise. || 13 ||
Of these, the first two are without remedy; the one called <s>pakṣa</s> (periodic) should observe [abstinence] for a month;
for the next three in order, the prescribed period is one year. || 14 ||
The four others beginning with <s>īrṣyāpaṇḍa</s> (one impotent from jealousy) that have been enumerated,
are to be abandoned like outcasts, as are women with defective reproductive organs. || 15 ||
When the husband is of the <s>ākṣipta</s> (distracted) or <s>moghabīja</s> (ineffective seed) type and there is no remedy,

children.text: patir anyaḥ smṛto nāryā vatsaraṃ sampratīkṣya tu || 16 ||
children.translated_text: another husband is prescribed for the woman, after waiting for one year. || 16 ||
Even the <s>śālīna</s> (bashful one), through union with a bold woman, may have his virility restored;
one of diminished vigor should be treated with other women, young women, and the like. || 17 ||

children.text: anyasyām yo manuṣyaḥ syād amanuṣyaḥ svayoṣiti |
children.translated_text: A man who is potent with another woman but impotent with his own wife,

children.text: labheta sānyaṃ bhartāram etat kāryaṃ prajāpateḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: she may obtain another husband; this is the ordinance of <s>Prajāpati</s>. || 18 ||

children.text: apatyārthaṃ striyaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ strī kṣetraṃ bījinaḥ prajāḥ |
children.translated_text: Women are created for the sake of offspring; the wife is the field, and the offspring belong to the one who owns the seed;

children.text: kṣetraṃ bījavate deyaṃ nābījī kṣetram arhati || 19 ||
children.translated_text: the field should be given to one who possesses seed; one without seed does not deserve a field. || 19 ||

children.text: pitā dadyāt svayaṃ kanyām bhrātā vānumate pituḥ |
children.translated_text: The father himself should give the maiden, or the brother with the father's consent;

children.text: mātāmaho mātulaś ca sakulyā bāndhavās tathā || 20 ||
children.translated_text: the maternal grandfather, the maternal uncle, kinsmen of the same family, and relatives likewise. || 20 ||

children.text: mātābhāve tu sarveṣāṃ prakṛtau yadi vartate |
children.translated_text: In the absence of a mother, if all of them are in their natural state,
when she is not in her natural state, members of one's own <s>jāti</s> (caste) should give the maiden. || 21 ||

children.text: yadā tu naiva kaścit syāt kanyā rājānam āvrajet |
children.translated_text: When there is no one at all, the maiden should approach the king;

children.text: anujñayā tasya varaṃ pratītya varayet svayam || 22 ||
children.translated_text: with his permission, having found a groom, she may choose [him] herself. || 22 ||
One of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste) and of suitable family, form, age, and learning;

children.text: saha dharmaṃ caret tena putrāṃś cotpādayet tataḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: she should practice <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) together with him and beget sons from him. || 23 ||

children.text: pratigṛhya ca yaḥ kanyāṃ naro deśāntaraṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: A man who, having accepted a maiden, goes to another country,

children.text: trīn ṛtūn samatikramya kanyānyaṃ varayed varam || 24 ||
children.translated_text: after three menstrual periods have passed, the maiden may choose another groom. || 24 ||
A maiden should not be kept waiting for marriage; she should report to her kinsmen;

children.text:
te cen na dadyus tāṃ bhartre te syur bhrūṇahabhiḥ samāḥ || 25
                            ||
children.translated_text: if they do not give her to a husband, they shall be equal to those who commit <s>bhrūṇahatyā</s> (embryo-killing). || 25 ||

children.text: yāvantaś ca rtavas tasyāḥ samatītā patiṃ vinā |
children.translated_text: As many menstrual periods as have passed for her without a husband,

children.text: tāvatyo bhrūṇahatyāḥ syus tasya yo na dadāti tām || 26 ||
children.translated_text: that many sins of <s>bhrūṇahatyā</s> (embryo-killing) shall accrue to the one who does not give her [in marriage]. || 26 ||

children.text: ato 'pravṛtte rajasi kanyāṃ dadyāt pitā sakṛt |
children.translated_text: Therefore, before the onset of menstruation, the father should give the maiden once;

children.text: mahad enaḥ spṛśed enam anyathaiṣa vidhiḥ satām || 27 ||
children.translated_text: great sin touches him who does otherwise; this is the rule of the virtuous. || 27 ||

children.text: sakṛd aṃśo nipatati sakṛt kanyā pradīyate |
children.translated_text: The inheritance falls once; the maiden is given once;

children.text: sakṛd āha dadānīti trīṇy etāni sakṛt sakṛt || 28 ||
children.translated_text: "I give" is said once — these three are [done] once and once only. || 28 ||

children.text: brāhmādiṣu vivāheṣu pañcasv eṣu vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the five marriages beginning with <s>Brāhma</s> and the others, this rule is prescribed;

children.text: guṇāpekṣaṃ bhaved dānam āsurādiṣu ca triṣu || 29 ||
children.translated_text: the giving should be based on the groom's qualities, and in the three beginning with <s>Āsura</s>. || 29 ||

children.text: kanyāyām prāptaśulkāyāṃ jyāyāṃś ced vara āvrajet |
children.translated_text: When the bride-price has been received for a maiden, if a superior groom arrives,
speaking falsely would there be connected with <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire). || 30 ||

children.text: nāduṣṭāṃ dūṣayet kanyāṃ nāduṣṭaṃ dūṣayed varam |
children.translated_text: One should not defame an unblemished maiden, nor defame an unblemished groom;

children.text: doṣe tu sati nāgaḥ syād anyonyaṃ tyajatos tayoḥ || 31 ||
children.translated_text: but when a defect exists, there is no sin when the two abandon each other. || 31 ||

children.text: dattvā nyāyena yaḥ kanyāṃ varāya na dadāti tām |
children.translated_text: One who, having given a maiden according to law, does not hand her over to the groom,

children.text: aduṣṭaś ced varo rājñā sa daṇḍyas tatra coravat || 32 ||
children.translated_text: if the groom is without fault, he should be punished by the king like a thief. || 32 ||

children.text: yas tu doṣavatīṃ kanyām anākhyāya prayacchati |
children.translated_text: One who gives a maiden with defects without disclosing them,
the king should impose upon him a fine prescribed for the first degree of <s>sāhasa</s> (violence). || 33 ||

children.text: akanyeti tu yaḥ kanyāṃ brūyād dveṣeṇa mānavaḥ |
children.translated_text: A man who out of malice calls a maiden 'not a maiden',

children.text: sa śataṃ prāpnuyād daṇḍaṃ tasyā doṣam adarśayan || 34 ||
children.translated_text: he shall incur a fine of one hundred, if he cannot demonstrate her defect. || 34 ||

children.text: pratigṛhya tu yaḥ kanyām aduṣṭām utsṛjed varaḥ |
children.translated_text: A groom who, having accepted an unblemished maiden, rejects her,

children.text: vineyaḥ so 'py akāmo 'pi kanyāṃ tām eva codvahet || 35 ||
children.translated_text: should be compelled, even if unwilling, to marry that very maiden. || 35 ||
Being tall, being despised, afflicted with disease, having a deformed body, having had sexual intercourse,
being bold, and having affection directed toward another — these are declared as defects in a maiden. || 36 ||
Insane, fallen from caste, impotent, ill-fated, and abandoned by kinsmen,

children.text: kanyādoṣau ca yau pūrvau eṣa doṣagaṇo vare || 37 ||
children.translated_text: and the first two defects of the maiden [being tall and despised] — this is the list of defects in a groom. || 37 ||
Eight forms of marriage are declared for the <s>varṇas</s> (castes) for the purpose of sacramental rites;

children.text: brāhmas tu prathamas teṣāṃ prājāpatyas tathaiva ca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Brāhma</s> is the first of these, and likewise the <s>Prājāpatya</s>. || 38 ||

children.text: ārṣaś caivātha daivaś ca gāndharvaś cāsuras tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Ārṣa</s> and then the <s>Daiva</s>, and the <s>Gāndharva</s> and the <s>Āsura</s> likewise;

children.text:
rākṣaso 'nantaras tasmāt paiśācas tv aṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ || 39
                            ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Rākṣasa</s> comes next after that, and the <s>Paiśāca</s> is remembered as the eighth. || 39 ||

children.text: satkṛtyāhūya kanyāṃ tu brāhme dadyād tv alaṅkṛtām |
children.translated_text: Having honored and invited [the groom], one should give the adorned maiden in the <s>Brāhma</s> [marriage];

children.text: saha dharmaṃ carety uktvā prājāpatyo vidhīyate || 40 ||
children.translated_text: by saying 'Practice <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) together,' the <s>Prājāpatya</s> is ordained. || 40 ||

children.text: vastragomithune dattvā vivāhas tv ārṣa ucyate |
children.translated_text: By giving a garment and a pair of cattle, the marriage is called <s>Ārṣa</s>;

children.text: antarvedyāṃ tu daivaḥ syād ṛtvije karma kurvate || 41 ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Daiva</s> takes place within the sacrificial enclosure, to the officiating priest performing the rite. || 41 ||

children.text: icchantīm icchate prāhur gāndharvo nāma pañcamam |
children.translated_text: When a willing woman meets a willing man, they call it the fifth, the <s>Gāndharva</s>;
the <s>Āsura</s> marriage is to be known from the transaction of the bride-price. || 42 ||

children.text: prasahya haraṇād ukto vivāho rākṣasas tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Rākṣasa</s> marriage is declared to be by forcible abduction;
the <s>Paiśāca</s>, by approaching a woman who is asleep or intoxicated, is the eighth and the lowest. || 43 ||

children.text: eṣāṃ tu dharmyās catvāro brāhmādyāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: Of these, four are righteous, beginning with the <s>Brāhma</s>, as enumerated;

children.text:
sādhāraṇaḥ syād gāndharvas trayo 'dharmyās tv ataḥ pare || 44
                            ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Gāndharva</s> is common; the three beyond that are unrighteous. || 44 ||

children.text: parapūrvāḥ striyas tv anyāḥ sapta proktā yathākramam |
children.translated_text: There are seven other types of women who have had previous husbands, stated in order;

children.text: punarbhūs trividhā tāsāṃ svairiṇī tu caturvidhā || 45 ||
children.translated_text: of these, the <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman) is of three kinds, and the <s>svairiṇī</s> (wanton woman) is of four kinds. || 45 ||
A maiden whose womb is intact but who has been tainted by [a prior] taking of the hand,

children.text: punarbhūḥ prathamā soktā punaḥ saṃskāram arhati || 46 ||
children.translated_text: she is called the first type of <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman); she deserves a renewed consecration. || 46 ||

children.text: kaumāraṃ patim utsṛjya yānyaṃ puruṣam āśritā |
children.translated_text: Having abandoned her childhood husband and taken refuge with another man,

children.text: punaḥ patyur gṛham yāyāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā || 47 ||
children.translated_text: if she returns to her husband's house, she is declared the second type. || 47 ||

children.text: asatsu devareṣu strī bāndhavair yā pradīyate |
children.translated_text: A woman who, in the absence of <s>devara</s>s (brothers-in-law), is given by her kinsmen,
to one of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste) who is not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> (close relative), she is declared the third type. || 48 ||

children.text: strī prasūtāprasūtā vā patyāv eva tu jīvati |
children.translated_text: A woman, whether she has borne children or not, while her husband is still alive,

children.text: kāmāt samāśrayed anyaṃ prathamā svairiṇī tu sā || 49 ||
children.translated_text: if she resorts to another out of desire, she is the first type of <s>svairiṇī</s> (wanton woman). || 49 ||

children.text: mṛte bhartari yā prāptān devarān apy apāsya tu |
children.translated_text: A woman who, when her husband has died, rejects the available <s>devara</s>s (brothers-in-law),

children.text: upagacchet paraṃ kāmāt sā dvitīyā prakīrtitā || 50 ||
children.translated_text: and goes to another out of desire, she is declared the second type. || 50 ||

children.text: prāptā deśād dhanakrītā kṣutpipāsāturā ca yā |
children.translated_text: A woman obtained from [another] region, purchased with wealth, or afflicted by hunger and thirst,

children.text: tavāham ity upagatā sā tṛtīyā prakīrtitā || 51 ||
children.translated_text: who approaches [a man] saying 'I am yours,' she is declared the third type. || 51 ||

children.text: deśadharmān apekṣya strī gurubhir yā pradīyate |
children.translated_text: A woman who, in consideration of regional customs, is given by her elders,
She who, having produced offspring through violence (<s>sāhasa</s>), gives herself to another is known as a <s>svairiṇī</s> (wanton woman). || 52 ||

children.text: punarbhuvāṃ eṣa vidhiḥ svairiṇīnāṃ ca kīrtitaḥ |
children.translated_text: This is the rule declared for <s>punarbhūs</s> (remarried women) and <s>svairiṇīs</s> (wanton women);
among them, each earlier type is better than the later one, and each successive one is progressively inferior. || 53 ||

children.text: apatyam utpādayitus tāsāṃ yā śulkato hṛtā |
children.translated_text: The offspring of these women belongs to the begetter if the woman was taken with a bride-price (<s>śulka</s>);
but in the case of one taken without a bride-price, the fruit belongs to the owner of the field (<s>kṣetrika</s>) alone. || 54 ||

children.text: kṣetrikasya yad ajñātaṃ kṣetre bījaṃ pradīyate |
children.translated_text: When seed is deposited in a field belonging to the <s>kṣetrika</s> (field-owner) without his knowledge,

children.text: na tatra bījino bhāgaḥ kṣetrikasyaiva tad bhavet || 55 ||
children.translated_text: the sower has no share therein; it shall belong to the <s>kṣetrika</s> (field-owner) alone. || 55 ||
When seed carried by flood or wind sprouts in someone's field,

children.text:
phalabhug yasya tat kṣetraṃ na bījī phalabhāg bhavet || 56
                            ||
children.translated_text: the fruit belongs to the owner of that field; the sower of the seed shall not partake of the fruit. || 56 ||

children.text: mahokṣo janayed vatsān yasya goṣu vraje caran |
children.translated_text: If a great bull, wandering in the herd, begets calves among another's cows,

children.text: tasya te yasya tā gāvo moghaṃ syanditam ārṣabham || 57 ||
children.translated_text: those calves belong to the owner of those cows; the bull's seed is shed in vain. || 57 ||
When seed is released in a field with the consent of the <s>kṣetrika</s> (field-owner),
the offspring is considered to belong to both the sower (<s>bījika</s>) and the field-owner (<s>kṣetrika</s>). || 58 ||

children.text: narte kṣetraṃ bhavet sasyaṃ na ca bījaṃ vināsti tat |
children.translated_text: Without the field there can be no crop, nor can it exist without seed;

children.text: ato 'patyaṃ dvayor iṣṭaṃ pitur mātuś ca dharmataḥ || 59 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the offspring is desired by both, the father and the mother, according to <s>dharma</s>. || 59 ||
When a man is found with the wife of another who has a protector, staying together in another's house,

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ tajjñair nāgatāyāḥ svayaṃ gṛhe || 60 ||
children.translated_text: the learned recognize it as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach), but not if the woman came to the house of her own accord. || 60 ||
In the case of a man whose wife is corrupt, abandoned, or who is impotent or patient (<s>kṣamaka</s>),

children.text: svecchayopeyuṣo dārān na doṣaḥ sāhaso bhavet || 61 ||
children.translated_text: if the woman approaches another of her own will, there is no offense of violence (<s>sāhasa</s>). || 61 ||
When a man and another's wife meet at an improper time or place,
being present together, conversing, and exchanging perfumes — these are the three stages of <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 62 ||

children.text: nadīnāṃ saṅgame tīrtheṣv ārāmeṣu vaneṣu ca |
children.translated_text: At the confluence of rivers, at sacred fords (<s>tīrthas</s>), in gardens, and in forests,

children.text:
strī pumāṃś ca sameyātāṃ grāhyaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ bhavet || 63
                            ||
children.translated_text: if a woman and a man meet, it should be treated as <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 63 ||
Sending a female messenger, dispatching letters,

children.text: anyair api vyabhicāraiḥ sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 64 ||
children.translated_text: and other acts of illicit approach — all are considered <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 64 ||

children.text: striyaṃ spṛśed adeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marśayet tathā |
children.translated_text: He who touches a woman in an improper place, or she who, being touched, permits the touching,
when done with mutual consent, that too constitutes <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 65 ||

children.text: bhakṣair vā yadi vā bhojyair vastrair mālyais tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: By sending eatables, cooked food, garments, garlands,

children.text:
sampreṣyamānair gandhaiś ca sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 66
                            ||
children.translated_text: and perfumes — all such acts are considered <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 66 ||

children.text: darpād vā yadi vā mohāc chlāghayā vā svayaṃ vadet |
children.translated_text: If out of pride, delusion, or boastfulness one declares,
'This woman was enjoyed by me before' — all such statements are considered <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 67 ||

children.text: pāṇau yaś ca nigṛhṇīyad veṇyāṃ vastrāntare 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: He who seizes a woman by the hand, by the braid, or by the edge of her garment,

children.text:
tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti vā bruyāt sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam || 68
                            ||
children.translated_text: or says 'Stop! Stop!' — all such acts are considered <s>saṅgrahaṇa</s> (sexual approach). || 68 ||
For men who transgress with women of their own <s>varṇa</s> (caste), the highest <s>sāhasa</s> (penalty) is prescribed;
in the reverse case, the middle penalty; and in <s>pratiloma</s> (against the natural order), the death penalty. || 69 ||
In the case of an unwilling maiden, cutting off two fingers is prescribed;

children.text: uttamāyāṃ vadhas tv eva sarvasvaharaṇaṃ tathā || 70 ||
children.translated_text: for one of the highest caste, death is the penalty, along with confiscation of all property. || 70 ||

children.text: sakāmāyāṃ tu kanyāyāṃ savarṇe nāsty atikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: But in the case of a willing maiden of the same <s>varṇa</s> (caste), there is no offense;

children.text: kintv alaṅkṛtya satkṛtya sa evaināṃ samudvahet || 71 ||
children.translated_text: rather, he should adorn and honor her, and marry her himself. || 71 ||
Mother, mother's sister, mother-in-law, maternal uncle's wife, father's sister,
wife of the father's brother's friend or pupil, sister, her friend, daughter-in-law, || 72 ||
daughter, teacher's wife, a woman of the same <s>gotra</s> (lineage), one who has sought refuge,

children.text: rājñī pravrajitā dhātrī sādhvī varṇottamā ca yā || 73 ||
children.translated_text: a queen, a female ascetic, a wet-nurse, a virtuous woman, and one of the highest <s>varṇa</s> (caste) — || 73 ||
he who approaches any one of these is called a <s>gurutalpaga</s> (violator of the teacher's bed);
cutting off the penis is the punishment prescribed, and no other penalty is ordained for that. || 74 ||

children.text: paśuyonyām atikrāman vineyaḥ sa damaṃ śatam |
children.translated_text: One who transgresses with an animal shall be fined one hundred <s>dama</s> (penalty units);
the middle <s>sāhasa</s> (penalty) applies in the case of cows, and the same for <s>antyāvasāyins</s> (outcaste women). || 75 ||
The punishment decreed by the king disciplines those who approach forbidden women;
in the domain of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation), the expiatory rite provides purification. || 76 ||

children.text: svairiṇy abrāhmaṇī veśyā dāsī niṣkāsinī ca yā |
children.translated_text: A <s>svairiṇī</s> (wanton woman), a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman, a courtesan (<s>veśyā</s>), a female slave (<s>dāsī</s>), and one who has been cast out (<s>niṣkāsinī</s>),

children.text: gamyāḥ syur ānulomyena striyo na pratilomataḥ || 77 ||
children.translated_text: these women may be approached in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>), but not in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>). || 77 ||

children.text: āsv eva tu bhujiṣyāsu doṣaḥ syāt paradāravat |
children.translated_text: But even among these approachable women (<s>bhujiṣyās</s>), the offense is like that of adultery with another's wife,

children.text: gamyā api hi nopeyās tāś ced anyaparigrahāḥ || 78 ||
children.translated_text: for even approachable women should not be visited if they belong to another man. || 78 ||

children.text: anutpannaprajāyās tu patiḥ preyād yadi striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: But if the husband of a woman who has not produced offspring dies,
she, being appointed by the elders, should approach the brother-in-law (<s>devara</s>) with the desire for a son. || 79 ||

children.text: sa ca tāṃ pratipadyeta tathaivā putrajanmataḥ |
children.translated_text: And he should accept her in the same manner until the birth of a son;

children.text: putre jāte nivarteta viplavaḥ syād ato 'nyathā || 80 ||
