children.translated_text: once a son is born, they should cease; otherwise, it would be a transgression. || 80 ||
Having anointed the body with ghee or with unadulterated oil,

children.text: mukhān mukhaṃ pariharan gātrair gātrāṇy asaṃspṛśan || 81 ||
children.translated_text: avoiding face-to-face contact and not touching limb to limb, || 81 ||
he should not approach a woman who already has a son, a barren woman, one past menstruation, or an unwilling woman;

children.text:
na gacched garbhiṇīṃ nindyām aniyuktāṃ ca bandhubhiḥ || 82
                            ||
children.translated_text: nor a pregnant woman, a despised woman, or one not appointed by the kinsmen. || 82 ||

children.text: aniyuktā tu yā nārī devarāj janayet sutam |
children.translated_text: But if an unappointed woman begets a son from the brother-in-law (<s>devara</s>),
the expounders of <s>dharma</s> declare that son to be illegitimate (<s>jārajāta</s>) and without inheritance rights. || 83 ||
Likewise, if an unappointed younger brother approaches the wife of the elder,

children.text: yavīyaso vā yo jyāyān ubhau tau gurutalpagau || 84 ||
children.translated_text: or an elder brother approaches the wife of the younger — both are guilty of violating the teacher's bed (<s>gurutalpaga</s>). || 84 ||

children.text: kule tadavaśeṣe tu santānārthaṃ na kāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: But when the family line is about to become extinct, for the purpose of continuing the lineage and not from desire,
one appointed by the elders should approach the wife of the younger brother. || 85 ||

children.text: avidyamāne tu gurau rājño vācyaḥ kulakṣayaḥ |
children.translated_text: But in the absence of an elder, the extinction of the family should be reported to the king;

children.text: tatas tadvacanād gacched anuśiṣya striyā saha || 86 ||
children.translated_text: then, by his command, one should approach the woman, having been duly instructed. || 86 ||
According to the procedure previously described, being pure, with the woman bathed as for the <s>puṃsavana</s> (male-producing rite),

children.text: sakṛd ā garbhādhānād vā kṛte garbhe snuṣaiva sā || 87 ||
children.translated_text: only once or until conception occurs; once she has conceived, she becomes a daughter-in-law again. || 87 ||

children.text: ato 'nyathā vartamānaḥ pumān strī vāpi kāmataḥ |
children.translated_text: A man or woman who acts otherwise than this, out of desire,

children.text: vineyau subhṛśaṃ rājñā kilbiṣī syād anigrahāt || 88 ||
children.translated_text: should be severely punished by the king; for failure to punish would make the king guilty of sin. || 88 ||
When a quarrel arises between husband and wife due to jealousy and envy, caused by passion,

children.text: dampatī vivadeyātāṃ na jñātiṣu na rājani || 89 ||
children.translated_text: the couple should settle it among themselves, not before kinsmen or the king. || 89 ||
When the two mutually abandon each other while being hostile to one another, there is no penalty for either,
in the case of both man and woman, except when the woman has committed secret adultery. || 90 ||

children.text: vyabhicāre striyā mauṇḍyam adhaḥśayanam eva ca |
children.translated_text: For a woman's adultery, the punishments are: shaving the head, sleeping on the ground,

children.text: kadannaṃ vā kuvāsaś ca karma cāvaskaroñjhanam || 91 ||
children.translated_text: eating bad food, wearing dirty clothes, and performing the work of removing refuse. || 91 ||
A woman who squanders her <s>strīdhana</s> (woman's property) and all possessions, who causes miscarriage,

children.text:
bhartuś ca vadham icchantīṃ striyaṃ nirvāsayed gṛhāt || 92
                            ||
children.translated_text: and who desires the death of her husband — such a woman should be expelled from the house. || 92 ||
Likewise, one who is constantly engaged in harmful conduct and one who speaks unpleasantly,

children.text: pūrvāśinīṃ ca yā bhartuḥ striyaṃ nirvāsayed budhaḥ || 93 ||
children.translated_text: and one who eats before her husband — such a woman should be expelled by a wise man. || 93 ||

children.text: vandhyāṃ strījananīṃ nindyāṃ pratikulāṃ ca sarvadā |
children.translated_text: A barren woman, one who bears only daughters, a despised woman, and one who is always hostile —

children.text: kāmato nābhinandeta kurvann evaṃ sa doṣabhāk || 94 ||
children.translated_text: one should not willingly favor such a woman; one who does so incurs blame. || 94 ||
But one who abandons a wife who is compliant, not foul-mouthed, skillful, virtuous, and who has borne children,

children.text: tyajan bhāryām avasthāpyo rājñā daṇḍena bhūyasā || 95 ||
children.translated_text: should be restrained by the king with a heavy fine. || 95 ||
A woman who was married without the husband knowing her faults, who has left but has not taken refuge with another man,

children.text: bandhubhiḥ sā niyoktavyā nirbandhuḥ svayam āśrayet || 96 ||
children.translated_text: should be directed by her kinsmen to return; if she has no kinsmen, she may seek shelter on her own. || 96 ||

children.text: naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe ca patite patau |
children.translated_text: When the husband is lost, dead, has renounced the world, is impotent, or has fallen from caste,

children.text: pañcasv āpatsu nārīṇāṃ patir anyo vidhīyate || 97 ||
children.translated_text: in these five calamities, another husband is ordained for women. || 97 ||

children.text: aṣṭau varṣāṇy udīkṣeta brāhmaṇī proṣitaṃ patim |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> (Brahmin woman) should wait eight years for a husband who has gone abroad;
if she has not borne children, four years; after that, she may take refuge with another. || 98 ||

children.text: kṣatriyā ṣaṭ samās tiṣṭhed aprasūtā samātrayam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriyā</s> (Kshatriya woman) should wait six years; if childless, three years;

children.text: vaiśyā prasūtā catvāri dve same tv itarā vaset || 99 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśyā</s> (Vaishya woman) who has borne children, four years; the other (childless), two years. || 99 ||

children.text: na śūdrāyāḥ smṛtaḥ kālo na ca dharmavyatikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: For a <s>Śūdrā</s> (Shudra woman), no waiting period is prescribed, nor is there transgression of <s>dharma</s>;
especially if she has not borne children, the maximum waiting period is one year. || 100 ||
This is the <s>dharma</s> declared for wives whose husbands have gone abroad, when there is no news;

children.text: jīvati śrūyamāṇe tu syād eṣa dviguṇo vidhiḥ || 101 ||
children.translated_text: but when the husband is heard to be alive, this period should be doubled. || 101 ||
This creation of <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of creatures) is for the propagation of beings;

children.text: ato 'nyagamane strīṇām evaṃ doṣo na vidyate || 102 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, in the case of women going to another man, there is no fault in this manner. || 102 ||

children.text: ānulomyena varṇānāṃ yaj janma sa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Birth in accordance with the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>) of the <s>varṇas</s> (castes) is the recognized rule;

children.text: prātilomyena yaj janma sa jñeyo varṇasaṅkaraḥ || 103 ||
children.translated_text: birth against the natural order (<s>pratiloma</s>) should be known as <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (caste-mixture). || 103 ||

children.text: anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ putraḥ putra ekāntaras tathā |
children.translated_text: A son of the immediately next caste (<s>anantara</s>) is recognized, and so is one removed by one interval (<s>ekāntara</s>),
and one removed by two intervals (<s>dvyantara</s>) — both in the natural (<s>anuloma</s>) and reverse (<s>pratiloma</s>) orders. || 104 ||
<s>Ugra</s>, <s>Pāraśava</s>, and <s>Niṣāda</s> — these are the sons born in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>),
declared as the sons of a <s>Śūdra</s> woman from the three higher castes respectively. || 105 ||
From a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> also are born <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, <s>Sūta</s>, and <s>Vaideha</s>,
three sons from the three lower castes respectively — these are to be known as born in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>). || 106 ||

children.text: ambaṣṭho māgadhaś caiva kṣattā ca kṣatriyāsutāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, and <s>Kṣattṛ</s> are the sons of <s>Kṣatriya</s> women;
one of them is born in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>), and two are to be known as born in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>). || 107 ||
The sons of <s>Vaiśya</s> women are <s>Dauṣṣanta</s>, <s>Yavana</s>, and <s>Āyogava</s>;
one of them is born in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>), and two are to be known as born in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>). || 108 ||
The <s>Sūta</s> and others born in the reverse order, who are born against the caste order,

children.text: te saṅkarāḥ śvapākādyās teṣāṃ triḥ saptako gaṇaḥ || 109 ||
children.translated_text: they are mixed castes (<s>saṅkara</s>); the <s>Śvapāka</s> and others — their count is thrice seven (twenty-one). || 109 ||
The son of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> by a man of the same <s>varṇa</s> is of equal caste; from a <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, the son is of the immediately next caste;
<s>Ambaṣṭha</s> and <s>Ugra</s> are likewise the sons of <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> women respectively. || 110 ||

children.text: ekāntaras tu dauṣṣanto vaiśyāyāṃ brāhmaṇāt sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dauṣṣanta</s> is the son removed by one interval, born of a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: śūdrāyāṃ kṣatriyāt tadvan niṣādo nāma jāyate || 111 ||
children.translated_text: similarly, from a <s>Śūdra</s> woman by a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a son called <s>Niṣāda</s> is born. || 111 ||

children.text: śūdrā pāraśavaṃ sūte brāhmaṇād uttaraṃ sutam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Śūdra</s> woman bears from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> a son called <s>Pāraśava</s>, who is of the furthest degree;

children.text: ānulomyena varṇānāṃ putrā hy ete prakīrtitāḥ || 112 ||
children.translated_text: these are declared as the sons of the <s>varṇas</s> in the natural order (<s>anuloma</s>). || 112 ||

children.text: sūtaś ca māgadhaś caiva putrāv āyogavas tathā |

children.translated_text: born in the reverse order (<s>pratiloma</s>) of the <s>varṇas</s>; these too are of the immediately next caste. || 113 ||

children.text: anantaraḥ smṛtaḥ sūto brāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatriyāt sutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Sūta</s> is recognized as the immediately next son, born of a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> by a <s>Kṣatriya</s>;
similarly, <s>Māgadha</s> and <s>Āyogava</s> are the two sons from <s>Vaiśya</s> and <s>Śūdra</s> men respectively. || 114 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇy ekāntaraṃ vaiśyāt sūte vaidehakaṃ sutam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> bears from a <s>Vaiśya</s> a son called <s>Vaidehaka</s>, removed by one interval;

children.text: kṣattāraṃ kṣatriyā śūdrāt putram ekāntaraṃ tathā || 115 ||
children.translated_text: likewise, a <s>Kṣatriyā</s> bears from a <s>Śūdra</s> a son called <s>Kṣattṛ</s>, also removed by one interval. || 115 ||
The most sinful, removed by two intervals in the reverse order, where caste-mixture exists,

children.text: cāṇḍālo jāyate śūdrād brāhmaṇī yatra muhyati || 116 ||
children.translated_text: is the <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, born of a <s>Śūdra</s> man where a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> is led astray. || 116 ||

children.text: rājñā parīkṣyaṃ na yathā jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ |
children.translated_text: The king should ensure that <s>varṇasaṅkara</s> (caste-mixture) does not arise;

children.text: tasmād rājñā viśeṣeṇa trayī rakṣyā tu saṅkarāt || 117 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, the king should especially protect the three (higher castes) from intermixture. || 117 ||
Where the partition of paternal property is undertaken by the sons,

children.text: dāyabhāga iti proktaṃ tad vivādapadaṃ budhaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: that topic of dispute is called <s>Dāyabhāga</s> (partition of inheritance) by the wise. || 1 ||

children.text: pitary ūrdhvaṃ mṛte putrā vibhajeyur dhanaṃ pituḥ |
children.translated_text: After the father has died, the sons should divide the father's wealth;
The daughters [should inherit] the mother's [property]; in the absence of daughters, their descendants [inherit it]. || 2 ||

children.text: mātur nivṛtte rajasi prattāsu bhaginīṣu ca |
children.translated_text: When the mother's menstruation has ceased, and the sisters have been given in marriage,
Or when the father, having discharged his obligations, has passed away or has relinquished all desires — || 3 ||

children.text: pitaiva vā svayaṃ putrān vibhajed vayasi sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The father himself, while still in his prime, may divide [the property] among his sons,

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ śreṣṭhavibhāgena yathā vāsya matir bhavet || 4 ||
children.translated_text: Giving the eldest a superior share, or as he may see fit. || 4 ||

children.text: bibhṛyād vecchataḥ sarvāñ jyeṣṭho bhrātā yathā pitā |
children.translated_text: The eldest brother should maintain all of them, if he so wishes, just as a father;

children.text: bhrātā śaktaḥ kaniṣṭho vā śaktyapekṣaḥ kule kriyā || 5 ||
children.translated_text: Or a capable younger brother [may do so]; family duties depend on ability. || 5 ||

children.text: śauryabhāryādhane hitvā yac ca vidyādhanaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: Setting aside what is acquired through valor, through a wife's property, and what constitutes wealth from learning —

children.text: trīṇy etāny avibhājyāni prasādo yaś ca paitṛkaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: These three are indivisible, as well as whatever is a gift of favor from the father. || 6 ||

children.text: mātrā ca svadhanaṃ dattaṃ yasmai syāt prītipūrvakam |
children.translated_text: And whatever personal property the mother gives with affection to whomever,

children.text: tasyāpy eṣa vidhir dṛṣṭo mātāpīṣṭe yathā pitā || 7 ||
children.translated_text: The same rule is seen for that as well — the mother has authority in her own domain, just as the father. || 7 ||
What is given before the nuptial fire, what is given at the time of the bridal procession, and what is given by the husband,
And what is received from brothers, mother, and father — <s>strīdhana</s> (women's property) is declared to be sixfold. || 8 ||
<s>Strīdhana</s> (women's property) goes to her offspring; in the case of childless women, it goes to the husband;
In the first four [marriage forms] beginning with <s>Brāhma</s>, they say [it goes to the husband]; but in the others, it goes to the father. || 9 ||

children.text: kuṭumbaṃ bibhṛyād bhrātur yo vidyām adhigacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who maintains the family of a brother who is pursuing learning

children.text: bhāgaṃ vidyādhanāt tasmāt sa labhetāśruto 'pi san || 10 ||
children.translated_text: Should receive a share from that brother's wealth earned through learning, even if he himself is unlearned. || 10 ||

children.text: vaidyo 'vaidyāya nākāmo dadyād aṃśaṃ svato dhanāt |
children.translated_text: A learned man need not unwillingly give a share from his own wealth to an unlearned one,

children.text: pitṛdravyaṃ tad āśritya na cet tena tad āhṛtam || 11 ||
children.translated_text: Unless that [wealth] was acquired by relying on the father's property. || 11 ||

children.text: dvāv āṃśau pratipadyeta vibhajann ātmanaḥ pitā |
children.translated_text: The father, when making a division, should receive two shares for himself;

children.text: samāṃśabhāginī mātā putrāṇāṃ syān mṛte patau || 12 ||
children.translated_text: The mother should be an equal-share holder with the sons when the husband has died. || 12 ||

children.text: jyeṣṭhāyāṃśo 'dhiko deyaḥ jyeṣṭhāya tu varaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: An additional share should be given to the eldest, and the best [of the property] is prescribed for the eldest;

children.text: samāṃśabhājaḥ śeṣāḥ syur aprattā bhaginī tathā || 13 ||
children.translated_text: The remaining [sons] should be equal sharers, and likewise an unmarried sister. || 13 ||

children.text: kṣetrajeṣv api putreṣu tadvaj jāteṣu dharmataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even for <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born) sons, when they are born lawfully,
There is a diminution of share for those born in lower <s>varṇas</s> (castes), in successive order for those born of married [wives]. || 14 ||

children.text: pitraiva tu vibhaktā ye hīnādhikasamair dhanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: But those who have been divided by the father himself with unequal, greater, or equal shares of wealth,

children.text: teṣāṃ sa eva dharmaḥ syāt sarvasya hi pitā prabhuḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: For them, that very arrangement is the law, for the father is master of all. || 15 ||

children.text: kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhāyāṃ yaś ca jāyate |
children.translated_text: A son born before marriage, one conceived before but born after marriage, and one born of a concealed [union] —

children.text: teṣāṃ voḍhāpitā jñeyas te ca bhāgaharāḥ smṛtāḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: The husband of the mother is to be known as their father, and they are declared to be sharers of the inheritance. || 16 ||
And a <s>kānīna</s> (son of an unmarried girl) whose father is unknown, born of an unwed mother —

children.text: mātāmahāya dadyāt sa piṇḍaṃ rikthaṃ hareta ca || 17 ||
children.translated_text: He should offer the <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral oblation) to his maternal grandfather and inherit his estate. || 17 ||

children.text: jātā ye tv aniyuktāyām ekena bahubhis tathā |
children.translated_text: But those born of a woman not formally appointed, whether by one man or by many —

children.text: arikthabhājas te sarve bījinām eva te sutāḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: All of them are without a share of the inheritance; they are the sons of the begetter alone. || 18 ||

children.text: dadyus te bījine piṇḍaṃ mātā cec chulkato hṛtā |
children.translated_text: They should offer the <s>piṇḍa</s> (funeral oblation) to the begetter, if the mother was taken with a bride-price;

children.text: aśulkopagatāyāṃ tu piṇḍadā voḍhur eva te || 19 ||
children.translated_text: But if she came without a bride-price, they are the <s>piṇḍa</s>-offerers of the husband [of the mother]. || 19 ||

children.text: pitṛdviṭ patitaḥ paṇḍo yaś ca syād aupapātikaḥ |
children.translated_text: One hostile to his father, an outcast, a eunuch, and one born of adultery —

children.text: aurasā api naite 'ṃśaṃ labheran kṣetrajāḥ kutaḥ || 20 ||
children.translated_text: Even these, if born of the body, shall not receive a share; how much less the <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born) sons? || 20 ||
Those afflicted with long and severe diseases, the mentally deficient, the insane, the blind, and the lame —

children.text:
bhartavyāḥ syuḥ kule caite tatputrās tv aṃśabhāginaḥ || 21
                            ||
children.translated_text: These should be maintained by the family, but their sons shall be sharers of the inheritance. || 21 ||
Sons who are <s>dvyāmuṣyāyaṇa</s> (belonging to two families) should offer the <s>piṇḍa</s> and water to both [fathers] separately,
And should take a half-share of the inheritance from both the begetter and the field-owner likewise. || 22 ||

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭināṃ tu yo bhāgas teṣām eva sa iṣyate |
children.translated_text: The share of those who are <s>saṃsṛṣṭin</s> (co-partners, undivided) is held to belong to them alone;
Otherwise, the share-holders among the seedless [families] would inherit from the others. || 23 ||

children.text: bhrātÏṛṇām aprajaḥ preyāt kaścic cet pravrajet tu vā |
children.translated_text: If among brothers one should die without issue, or if one should become a renunciant,

children.text: vibhajeyur dhanaṃ tasya śeṣās tu strīdhanaṃ vinā || 24 ||
children.translated_text: The remaining brothers should divide his property, excluding the <s>strīdhana</s> (women's property). || 24 ||

children.text: bharaṇam cāsya kurvīran strīṇām ā jīvitakṣayāt |
children.translated_text: And they should provide maintenance for his wives until the end of their lives,

children.text: rakṣanti śayyāṃ bhartuś ced ācchindyur itarāsu tu || 25 ||
children.translated_text: If they guard their husband's bed; but they should withhold [maintenance] from those who do otherwise. || 25 ||

children.text: syād yasya duhitā tasyāḥ pitraṃśo bharaṇe mataḥ |
children.translated_text: If one has a daughter, the father's share is considered [to be used] for her maintenance;

children.text: ā saṃskārād bhajed enāṃ parato bibhṛyāt patiḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: He should provide for her until her <s>saṃskāra</s> (marriage rite); after that, the husband should maintain her. || 26 ||

children.text: mṛte bhartary aputrāyāḥ patipakṣaḥ prabhuḥ striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: When the husband has died, if a woman is childless, the husband's family has authority over her,
In matters of her employment, protection, and maintenance, they are the masters. || 27 ||
When the husband's family has become extinct, devoid of members, without shelter,
Or when the <s>sapiṇḍas</s> (paternal kinsmen) are absent, the father's family has authority over the woman. || 28 ||

children.text: pakṣadvayāvasāne tu rājā bhartā smṛtaḥ striyāḥ |
children.translated_text: When both family lines have come to an end, the king is declared to be the protector of the woman;

children.text: sa tasyā bharaṇaṃ kuryān nigṛhṇīyāt pathaś cyutām || 29 ||
children.translated_text: He should provide her maintenance and restrain her if she strays from the [proper] path. || 29 ||

children.text: svātantryād vipraṇaśyanti kule jātā api striyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even women born in good families are ruined through independence;
Therefore <s>Prajāpati</s> ordained the lack of independence for them. || 30 ||

children.text: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane |
children.translated_text: The father protects her in childhood, the husband protects her in youth,

children.text:
putrā rakṣanti vaidhavye na strī svātantryam arhati || 31
                            ||
children.translated_text: The sons protect her in widowhood — a woman does not deserve independence. || 31 ||

children.text: yac chiṣṭaṃ pitṛdāyebhyo dattva rṇaṃ paitṛkaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Whatever remains of the father's estate after paying the father's debts,

children.text: bhrātṛbhis tad vibhaktavyam ṛṇī na syād yathā pitā || 32 ||
children.translated_text: That should be divided by the brothers, so that the father may not remain a debtor. || 32 ||

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca na kṛtāḥ pitrā saṃskāravidhayaḥ kramāt |
children.translated_text: Those for whom the father has not performed the prescribed <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacramental rites) in order,

children.text: kartavyā bhrātṛbhis teṣāṃ paitṛkād eva te dhanāt || 33 ||
children.translated_text: The brothers should perform those rites for them, from the father's property itself. || 33 ||

children.text: avidyamāne pitrye 'rthe svāṃśād uddhṛtya vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the absence of paternal property, having contributed from their own shares,
The <s>saṃskāras</s> must necessarily be performed for the brothers by those who were consecrated earlier. || 34 ||

children.text: kuṭumbārtheṣu codyuktas tatkāryaṃ kurute ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: And he who is engaged in family affairs and performs the family duties
Should be supported by the brothers with food, clothing, and conveyance. || 35 ||
In a dispute regarding the rules of partition among co-heirs, the determination [should be made]
By kinsmen, through partition-deeds, and by the commencement of separate transactions. || 36 ||
For undivided brothers, one single legal obligation applies;

children.text: vibhāge sati dharmo 'pi bhaved eṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak || 37 ||
children.translated_text: But when partition has occurred, their legal obligations become separate. || 37 ||
Giving, receiving, [transactions regarding] cattle, food, house, and field,
For those who are divided, these should be known to be separate: cooking, religious duties, income, and expenditure. || 38 ||

children.text: sākṣitvaṃ prātibhāvyaṃ ca dānaṃ grahaṇam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Bearing witness, standing surety, giving, and receiving —
Divided brothers may do these for one another, but undivided brothers may not [do so for each other]. || 39 ||

children.text: yeṣām etāḥ kriyā loke pravartante svarikthinām |
children.translated_text: Those among whom these transactions in the world proceed as [among] independent property-holders,

children.text: vibhaktān avagaccheyur lekhyam apy antareṇa tān || 40 ||
children.translated_text: One should recognize them as divided, even without a written document. || 40 ||
If many who are born of one [family] have separate legal obligations and separate activities,
And are endowed with separate occupations and qualities, they are not considered united in their affairs. || 41 ||

children.text: svān bhāgān yadi dadyus te vikrīṇīrann athāpi vā |
children.translated_text: If they were to give away their own shares, or sell them,

children.text: kuryur yatheṣṭaṃ tat sarvam īśante svadhanasya te || 42 ||
children.translated_text: They may do all of that as they please — they are masters of their own property. || 42 ||

children.text: aurasaḥ kṣetrajaś caiva putrikāputra eva ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>aurasa</s> (natural-born son), the <s>kṣetraja</s> (field-born son), and the son of an appointed daughter,

children.text: kānīnaś ca sahoḍhaś ca gūḍhotpannas tathaiva ca || 43 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kānīna</s> (son of an unmarried girl), the <s>sahoḍha</s> (son conceived before marriage), and the <s>gūḍhotpanna</s> (secretly born son) likewise, || 43 ||

children.text: paunarbhavo 'paviddhaś ca labdhaḥ krītaḥ kṛtas tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>paunarbhava</s> (son of a remarried woman), the <s>apaviddha</s> (abandoned son), the <s>labdha</s> (found son), the <s>krīta</s> (purchased son), and the <s>kṛta</s> (adopted son),
And the <s>svayam upagata</s> (self-offered son) — these twelve [types of] sons are enumerated. || 44 ||
Of these, six are kinsmen and heirs, and six are non-heirs but kinsmen;

children.text: pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ smṛtaḥ śreyāj jaghanyo yo ya uttaraḥ || 45 ||
children.translated_text: Each earlier one is considered superior, and each later one is inferior in order. || 45 ||

children.text: kramād dhy ete prapadyeran mṛte pitari taddhanam |
children.translated_text: In succession, these would inherit the father's property when he has died;
In the absence of each superior one, the next inferior one would obtain it. || 46 ||
In the absence of sons, a daughter [inherits], because of the equality observed in continuing the lineage;

children.text: putraś ca duhitā coktau pituḥ santānakārakau || 47 ||
children.translated_text: Both the son and the daughter are declared to be the continuers of the father's lineage. || 47 ||

children.text: abhāve tu duhitṝṇāṃ sakulyā bāndhavās tataḥ |
children.translated_text: In the absence of daughters, the <s>sakulya</s> (clansmen), then the <s>bāndhava</s> (kinsmen),

children.text: tataḥ sajātyāḥ sarveṣām abhāve rājagāmi tat || 48 ||
children.translated_text: Then those of the same <s>jāti</s> (caste); in the absence of all [of these], it goes to the king. || 48 ||
Except in the case of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, however; a king devoted to <s>dharma</s>

children.text: sa strīṇāṃ jīvanaṃ dadyād eṣa dāyavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ || 49 ||
children.translated_text: Should provide maintenance for the women — this is the declared rule of inheritance. || 49 ||
Whatever deed is done with violence by those intoxicated with power,

children.text: tat sāhasam iti proktaṃ saho balam ihocyate || 1 ||
children.translated_text: That is called <s>sāhasa</s> (violent crime); <s>saha</s> here means 'force.' || 1 ||

children.text: tat punas trividhaṃ jñeyaṃ prathamaṃ madhyamaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: That is to be known as threefold: the first degree, the middle degree,

children.text: uttamaṃ ceti śāstreṣu tasyoktaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak || 2 ||
children.translated_text: And the highest degree — their distinguishing characteristics are stated separately in the <s>śāstras</s> (legal treatises). || 2 ||
By breaking, throwing, crushing, and the like, of fruits, roots, water, and such,
And of agricultural implements — the first degree of <s>sāhasa</s> is declared. || 3 ||
Of clothing, cattle, food, and drink, and of household articles —
In the same manner, the middle degree of <s>sāhasa</s> is declared. || 4 ||
Assault with poison and weapons, violation of another's wife,
And whatever else endangers life — that is declared the highest degree of <s>sāhasa</s>. || 5 ||
The punishment for it depends on the act: for the first degree, the maximum is one hundred [<s>paṇas</s>];
For the middle degree, according to those learned in the <s>śāstras</s>, it should be known as up to five hundred. || 6 ||
Death, confiscation of all property, banishment from the city, branding,
And mutilation of the limb [that committed the offence] — this is declared as the punishment for the highest degree of <s>sāhasa</s>. || 7 ||
This rule of punishment is declared for all without distinction,

children.text: vadhād ṛte brāhmaṇasya na vadhaṃ brāhmaṇo 'rhati || 8 ||
children.translated_text: Except for the death penalty in the case of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> does not deserve execution. || 8 ||

children.text: śiraso muṇḍanaṃ daṇḍas tasya nirvāsanaṃ purāt |
children.translated_text: Shaving of the head is his punishment, banishment from the city,
A brand of infamy on the forehead, and being paraded on a donkey. || 9 ||

children.text: syātāṃ saṃvyavahāryau tau dhṛtadaṇḍau tu pūrvayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who have received punishment for the first two [degrees] may resume social transactions;
But one punished for the highest degree of <s>sāhasa</s> should be known as unfit for communal dining. || 10 ||

children.text: tasyaiva bhedaḥ steyaṃ syād viśeṣas tatra cocyate |
children.translated_text: Theft is a subdivision of that same [<s>sāhasa</s>], and its specific characteristics are stated;

children.text: atisāhasam ākramya steyam āhuś chalena tu || 11 ||
children.translated_text: They say that theft is [a crime] committed by stealth, overstepping the bounds of violent crime. || 11 ||

children.text: tad api trividhaṃ proktaṃ dravyāpekṣaṃ manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: That too is declared threefold by the wise, depending on the type of property —
From the taking of minor, middling, and superior articles. || 12 ||
Earthen vessels, seats, bedsteads, bones, wood, leather, grass, and the like,
<s>śamī</s> grain, <s>mudga</s> (mung beans), and such — these are cited as minor articles. || 13 ||

children.text: vāsaḥ kauśeyavarjaṃ ca govarjaṃ paśavas tathā |
children.translated_text: Clothing other than silk, cattle other than cows,

children.text: hiraṇyavarjaṃ lohaṃ ca madhyaṃ vrīhiyavā api || 14 ||
children.translated_text: Metal other than gold — these are middling; as well as rice and barley. || 14 ||
Gold, gems, silk, women, men, cows, elephants, and horses,
And the property of gods, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, and kings — these should be known as superior articles. || 15 ||
The carrying off of these by various stratagems, through deception,
From those who are sleeping, careless, or intoxicated — the wise call this theft. || 16 ||
Theft is [proven] by the seizure of stolen goods; in the absence of stolen goods, by the use [of the articles];
Suspicion [arises] from association with criminals, and from income and expenditure inconsistent [with one's means]. || 17 ||
Those who give food, shelter, and opportunity to thieves who are prowling,

children.text: śaktāś ca ya upekṣante te 'pi taddoṣabhāginaḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: And those who, being able [to prevent it], look on with indifference — they too share in that guilt. || 18 ||

children.text: utkrośatāṃ janānāṃ ca hriyamāṇe dhane 'pi ca |
children.translated_text: And when people are crying out while their property is being seized,
Those who, having heard, do not rush to help — they too share in that guilt. || 19 ||

children.text: sāhaseṣu ya evoktas triṣu daṇḍo manīṣibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The same punishment that is declared by the wise for the three degrees of <s>sāhasa</s>,

children.text: sa eva daṇḍaḥ steye 'pi dravyeṣu triṣv anukramāt || 20 ||
children.translated_text: That same punishment applies to theft as well, in proportion to the three [categories of] articles. || 20 ||

children.text: padenānveṣaṇaṃ kuryur ā mūlāt tadvido janāḥ || 21 ||
grāme vraje vivīte vā yatra sannipatet padam |

voḍhavyaṃ tad bhavet tena na cet so 'nyatra tan nayet || 22
                            ||
pade pramūḍhe bhagne vā viṣamatvāj janāntike |
yas tv āsannataro grāmo vrajo vā tatra pātayet || 23 ||
same 'dhvani dvayor yatra tena prāyo 'śucir janaḥ |
pūrvāpadānair dṛṣṭo vā saṃsṛṣṭo vā durātmabhiḥ || 24 ||
rātrisañcāriṇo ye ca bahiḥ kuryur bahiścarāḥ || 25 ||
steneṣv alabhyamāneṣu rājā dadyāt svakād dhanāt |
upekṣamāṇo hy enasvī dharmād arthāc ca hīyate || 26 ||
yad vacaḥ pratikūlārthaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ tad ucyate || 1 ||
gauravānukramād asya daṇḍo 'py atra kramād guruḥ || 2 ||
trīṇy eva sāhasāny āhus tatra kaṇṭakaśodhanam || 6 ||
vidhiḥ pañcavidhas tūkta etayor ubhayor api |

viśuddhir daṇḍabhāktvaṃ ca tatra sambadhyate yathā || 7
                            ||
pāruṣye sati saṃrambhād utpanne kṣubdhayor dvayoḥ |
sa manyate yaḥ kṣamate daṇḍabhāg yo 'tivartate || 8 ||
viśeṣaś cen na dṛśyeta vinayaḥ syāt samas tayoḥ || 9 ||
pūrvam ākṣārayed yas tu niyataṃ syāt sa doṣabhāk |

paścād yaḥ so 'py asatkārī pūrve tu vinayo guruḥ || 10
                            ||
dvayor āpannayos tulyam anubadhnāti yaḥ punaḥ |
sa tayor daṇḍam āpnoti pūrvo vā yadi vetaraḥ || 11 ||
na ca taddaṇḍapāruṣye doṣam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ || 13 ||
yam eva hy ativarterann ete santaṃ janaṃ nṛṣu |
sa eva vinayaṃ kuryān na tadvinayabhāṅ nṛpaḥ || 14 ||
malā hy ete manuṣyeṣu dhanam eṣāṃ malātmakam |
api tān ghātayed rājā nārthadaṇḍena daṇḍayet || 15 ||
śataṃ brāhmaṇam ākruśya kṣatriyo daṇḍam arhati |

vaiśyo 'dhyardhaṃ śataṃ dve vā śūdras tu vadham arhati || 16
                            ||

vaiśye syād ardhapañcāśac chūdre dvādaśako damaḥ || 17
                            ||
vādeṣv avacanīyeṣu tad eva dviguṇaṃ bhavet || 18 ||
kāṇam apy athavā khañjam anyaṃ vāpi tathāvidham |

na rājñā dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ ca daṇḍabhāk tadvyatikramāt || 20
                            ||
loke 'smin dvāv avaktavyāv adaṇḍyau ca prakīrtitau |
brāhmaṇaś caiva rājā ca tau hīdaṃ bibhṛto jagat || 21 ||
patitaṃ patitety uktvā cauraṃ caureti vā punaḥ |

vacanāt tulyadoṣaḥ syān mithyā dvir doṣatāṃ vrajet || 22
                            ||

taptam āsecayet tailaṃ vaktre śrotre ca pārthivaḥ || 24
                            ||

tad aṅgaṃ tasya chettavyam evaṃ śuddhim avāpnuyāt || 25
                            ||

kaṭyāṃ kṛṭāṅko nirvāsyaḥ sphigdeśaṃ vāsya kartayet || 26
                            ||
avaniṣṭhīvato darpād dvāv oṣṭhau chedayen nṛpaḥ |
pādayor nāsikāyāṃ ca grīvāyāṃ vṛṣaṇeṣu ca || 28 ||
upakruśya tu rājānaṃ vartmani sve vyavasthitam |
rājani prahared yas tu kṛtāgasy api durmatiḥ |
putrāparādhe na pitā na śvavāñ śuni daṇḍabhāk |
na markaṭe ca tatsvāmī tair eva prahito na cet || 31 ||
sabhikaḥ kārayed dyūtaṃ deyaṃ dadyāc ca tatkṛtam |
daśakaṃ tu śataṃ vṛddhis tasya syād dyūtakāritā || 2 ||
kitaveṣv eva tiṣṭheyuḥ kitavāḥ saṃśayaṃ prati |
ta eva tasya draṣṭāraḥ syus ta eva ca sākṣiṇaḥ || 4 ||
pratihanyān na sabhikaṃ dāpayet tat svam iṣṭataḥ || 5 ||
kaṇṭhe 'kṣamālām āsajya sa hy eṣāṃ vinayaḥ smṛtaḥ || 6 ||
na dṛṣṭaṃ yac ca pūrveṣu tat sarvaṃ syāt prakīrṇake || 4 ||
rājā tv avahitaḥ sarvān āśramān paripālayet |
yo yo varṇo 'vahīyeta yo vodrekam anuvrajet |

taṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā svato mārgāt pracyutaṃ sthāpayet pathi || 6
                            ||
śrutismṛtiviruddhaṃ ca janānām ahitaṃ ca yat |
na tat pravartayed rājā pravṛttaṃ ca nivartayet || 8 ||
nyāyāpetaṃ yad anyena rājñājñānakṛtaṃ ca yat |
tad apy anyāyavihitaṃ punar nyāye niveśayet || 9 ||
daṇḍyaḥ sa pāpo vadhyaś ca lopayan rājaśāsanam || 10 ||
yac ca yasyopakaraṇaṃ yena jīvanti kārukāḥ |
sarvasvaharaṇe 'py etān na rājā hartum arhati || 12 ||
anādiś cāpy anantaś ca dvipadāṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ |

dīptimatvāc chucitvāc ca yadi na syāt pathaś cyutaḥ || 13
                            ||
yadi rājā na sarveṣāṃ varṇānāṃ daṇḍadhāraṇam |
kuryāt patho vyapetānāṃ vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ || 14 ||
brāhmaṇyaṃ brāhmaṇo jahyāt kṣatriyaḥ kṣātram utsṛjet |
svakarma jahyād vaiśyas tu śūdraḥ sarvān viśeṣayet || 15 ||
satām anugraho nityam asatāṃ nigrahas tathā |
eṣa dharmaḥ smṛto rājñām arthaś cāmitrapīḍanāt || 17 ||
na lipyate yathā vahnir dahañ chaśvad imāḥ prajāḥ |
na lipyate tathā rājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayan || 18 ||
ājñā tejaḥ pārthivānāṃ sā ca vāci pratiṣṭhitā |
te yad brūyur asat sad vā sa dharmo vyavahāriṇām || 19 ||
rājā nāma caraty eṣa bhūmau sākṣāt sahasradṛk |
na tasyājñām atikramya santiṣṭheran prajāḥ kvacit || 20 ||
yad eva rājā kurute tat pramāṇam iti sthitiḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever the king decrees, that is the authoritative standard. || 21 ||

children.text: nirguṇo 'pi yathā strīṇāṃ pūjya eva patiḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Just as a husband is always to be honored by his wives, even if he is devoid of good qualities,

children.text: prajānāṃ viguṇo 'py evaṃ pūjya eva narādhipaḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: so too is a king to be honored by his subjects, even if he is deficient in virtues. || 22 ||

children.text: tapaḥkrītāḥ prajā rājñā prabhur āsāṃ tato nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: The subjects were acquired by the king through <s>tapas</s> (austerities); therefore the king is their lord.

children.text: tatas tadvacasi stheyaṃ vārtā cāsāṃ tadāśrayā || 23 ||
children.translated_text: Hence one should abide by his word, and their livelihood depends upon him. || 23 ||
Kings of immeasurable power bear five forms:

children.text: agner indrasya somasya yamasya dhanadasya ca || 24 ||
kāraṇād animittaṃ vā yadā krodhavaśaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: When, with or without cause, the king falls under the sway of anger
and burns his subjects, then he is called <s>Agni</s> (Fire). || 25 ||
When, displaying his splendor, desirous of conquest, with weapons raised,

children.text: abhiyāti parān rājā tadendraḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: the king marches against his enemies, then he is said to be <s>Indra</s>. || 26 ||
When the king, free from anger and sorrow, with a cheerful countenance,

children.text: prajānāṃ darśanaṃ yāti soma ity ucyate tadā || 27 ||
children.translated_text: goes forth to give audience to his subjects, then he is called <s>Soma</s>. || 27 ||

children.text: dharmāsanagataḥ śrīmān daṇḍaṃ dhatte yadā nṛpaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the glorious king, seated on the throne of justice, wields the rod of punishment,

children.text: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tadā vaivasvataḥ yamaḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: impartial toward all beings, then he is <s>Yama</s> <s>Vaivasvata</s> (son of the Sun). || 28 ||
When the lord of the earth favors the learned, elders, wise counselors, servants, and others

children.text: anugṛhṇāti dānena tadā sa dhanadaḥ smṛtaḥ || 29 ||
children.translated_text: with gifts, then he is known as <s>Dhanada</s> (the Giver of Wealth). || 29 ||

children.text: tasmāt taṃ nāvajānīyān nākrośen na viśeṣayet |
children.translated_text: Therefore one should not disregard him, nor revile him, nor oppose him;

children.text: ājñāyāṃ cāsya tiṣṭheta mṛtyuḥ syāt tadvyatikramāt || 30 ||
children.translated_text: one should abide by his command, for transgression thereof brings death. || 30 ||
His duty is the protection of subjects, attendance upon the aged and wise,
the examination of lawsuits, and the guarding of his own person. || 31 ||
The king should always attend upon <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with a focused mind;
the <s>Kṣatra</s> (royal power) united with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> is the foundation for the protection of the world. || 32 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> shall not be deprived of his property; the royal seat shall be placed foremost for him;
he shall have the first audience in the morning, and salutations from all. || 33 ||

children.text: agraṃ navebhyaḥ sasyebhyo mārgadānaṃ ca gacchataḥ |
children.translated_text: The first share of new crops, and the right of way when traveling;
for the purpose of begging alms, unhindered entry into another's house. || 34 ||
In the gathering of firewood, flowers, and water, there is no theft even from those who have possessions;

children.text: anākṣepaḥ parebhyaś ca sambhāṣaś ca parastriyā || 35 ||
children.translated_text: no accusation from others, and conversation with another man's wife is permitted. || 35 ||

children.text: nadīṣv avetanas tāraḥ pūrvam uttaraṇaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: At rivers, free passage without fee, and priority in crossing;

children.text: tareṣv aśulkadānaṃ ca na ced vāṇijyam asya tat || 36 ||
children.translated_text: at ferries, exemption from toll — provided he is not engaged in trade. || 36 ||
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> traveling on the road, being weary, taking but not dwelling himself,

children.text: brāhmaṇo nāparādhnoti dvāv ikṣū pañca mūlakān || 37 ||
children.translated_text: commits no offense in taking two sugarcanes or five radishes. || 37 ||

children.text: nābhiśastān na patitān na dviṣo na ca nāstikāt |
children.translated_text: One should not accept gifts from those who are accused, those who have fallen, enemies, or atheists,

children.text: na sopadhān nānimittaṃ na dātāraṃ prapīḍya ca || 38 ||
children.translated_text: nor from those employing fraud, nor without reason, nor by oppressing the giver. || 38 ||

children.text: arthānāṃ bhūribhāvāc ca deyatvāc ca mahātmanām |
children.translated_text: Because of the abundance of wealth and because of the great-souled being fit to give,

children.text: śreyān pratigraho rājñāṃ anyeṣāṃ brāhmaṇād ṛte || 39 ||
children.translated_text: accepting gifts from kings is better than from others, except from a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 39 ||

children.text: brāhmaṇaś caiva rājā ca dvāv apy etau dhṛtavratau |
children.translated_text: Both the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the king, when faithful to their vows,
there is no difference between these two, since both protect the <s>dharma</s> (law) of the subjects. || 40 ||
Of a king who knows <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), who is grateful, who punishes the wicked for the sake of protection,

children.text: medhyam eva dhanaṃ prāhus tīkṣṇasyāpi mahīpateḥ || 41 ||
children.translated_text: his wealth is declared pure, even if the king is severe. || 41 ||
Just as the waters of the pure and impure, when they meet,

children.text: samudre samatāṃ yāti tadvad rājño dhanāgamaḥ || 42 ||
children.translated_text: attain equality in the ocean, so too is the income of the king. || 42 ||

children.text: yathā cāgnau sthitaṃ dīpte śuddhim āyāti kāñcanam |
children.translated_text: And just as gold placed in blazing fire attains purity,

children.text: evam evāgamā sarve śuddhim āyānti rājasu || 43 ||
children.translated_text: even so all revenues attain purity in the hands of kings. || 43 ||

children.text: ya eva kaścit svadravyaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchati |
children.translated_text: Whoever gives his own property to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: tad rājñāpy anumantavyam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ || 44 ||
children.translated_text: that should be approved by the king also — this is the eternal <s>dharma</s> (law). || 44 ||
Apart from other customary dues, the one designated as the sixth part of the land's produce,
that tribute is ordained for him as wages for protecting the subjects. || 45 ||

children.text: śakyaṃ tat punar ādātuṃ yad abrāhmaṇasātkṛtam |
children.translated_text: That which has not been given to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> can be taken back;

children.text: brāhmaṇāya tu yad dattaṃ na tasya haraṇaṃ punaḥ || 46 ||
children.translated_text: but what has been given to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, there is no taking back of that. || 46 ||

children.text: dānam adhyayanaṃ yajñas tasya karma trilakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Giving, studying, and sacrifice — these are the three characteristic duties of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;
officiating at sacrifices, teaching — these are his livelihood, and the third is accepting gifts. || 47 ||

children.text: svakarmaṇi dvijas tiṣṭhed vṛttim āhārayet kṛtām |
children.translated_text: A twice-born should remain in his own occupation and earn his livelihood through prescribed means;
he should not accept gifts from unworthy persons or <s>varṇas</s> (castes), when there is no restraint. || 48 ||

children.text: aśucir vacanād yasya śucir bhavati puruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: An impure person becomes pure by the word of the king,

children.text: śuciś caivāśuciḥ sadyaḥ kathaṃ rājā na daivatam || 49 ||
children.translated_text: and a pure person at once becomes impure — how then is the king not a divinity? || 49 ||

children.text: vidur ya eva devatvaṃ rājño hy amitatejasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who know the divinity of the king of immeasurable splendor,

children.text: tasya te pratigṛhṇanto na lipyante dvijātayaḥ || 50 ||
children.translated_text: the twice-born who accept gifts from him are not tainted. || 50 ||

children.text: loke 'smin maṅgalāny aṣṭau brāhmaṇo gaur hutāśanaḥ |
children.translated_text: In this world, the eight auspicious things are: a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a cow, fire,

children.text: hiraṇyaṃ sarpir āditya āpo rājā tathāṣṭamaḥ || 51 ||
children.translated_text: gold, clarified butter, the sun, water, and the king as the eighth. || 51 ||

children.text: etāni satataṃ paśyen namasyed arcayec ca tān |
children.translated_text: One should always behold these, salute them, and worship them;

children.text: pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kurvīta tathā hy āyur na hīyate || 52 ||
children.translated_text: one should also circumambulate them, for thereby one's life is not diminished. || 52 ||
Thieves who steal the property of others are known to be of two kinds:

children.text: prakāśāś cāprakāśāś ca tān vidyād ātmavān nṛpaḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: open and secret — a wise king should know them. || 1 ||
Among the open deceivers are those who resort to false weights and measures,
extortioners, those who commit violence, gamblers, and prostitutes. || 2 ||
Counterfeiters, and those who make a living by pretending to perform auspicious rites —
these and others like them should be known as open deceivers of the world. || 3 ||
The secret ones should be known as those operating both outside and inside;

children.text: suptān pramattāṃś ca narā muṣṇanty ākramya caiva te || 4 ||
children.translated_text: they rob people who are asleep or careless, and also by force. || 4 ||
Those who destroy regions, villages, and houses, highway robbers, and pickpockets,

children.text: ity evamādayo jñeyā aprakāśāś ca taskarāḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: these and others like them should be known as secret thieves. || 5 ||
Having identified them through skilled spies who are experienced in such activities,
they should be tracked and apprehended by secretly deployed agents. || 6 ||
Assembly halls, rest houses, cook-shops, lodging houses, and liquor and food shops,
crossroads, sacred trees, festivals, and spectacles —
all these should be watched by spies zealous in apprehending thieves. || 8 ||
Likewise other deployed agents, trustworthy and eloquent,

children.text: carā hy utsāhayeyus tāṃs taskarān pūrvataskarāḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: should as secret agents incite those thieves — former thieves themselves. || 9 ||
Through offerings of food and drink, through showing festivals and gatherings,

children.text: tathā cauryāpadeśaiś ca kuryus teṣāṃ samāgamam || 10 ||
children.translated_text: and through pretexts of theft, they should arrange meetings with those thieves. || 10 ||

children.text: ye tatra nopasarpanti sṛtāḥ praṇihitā api |
children.translated_text: Those who do not approach even when sought out and deployed as agents,
they should be pursued and seized along with their sons, cattle, and kinsmen. || 11 ||

children.text: yāṃs tatra caurān gṛhṇīyāt tān vitāḍya viḍambya ca |
children.translated_text: The thieves captured there should be beaten and humiliated,

children.text: avaghuṣya ca sarvatra vadhyāś citravadhena te || 12 ||
children.translated_text: and after being publicly denounced everywhere, they should be executed by various modes of punishment. || 12 ||

children.text: na tv ahoḍhānvitāś caurā rājñā vadhyā hy anāgamāḥ |
children.translated_text: However, thieves caught without stolen goods should not be executed by the king, being without evidence;
but those caught with stolen goods and implements should be punished swiftly. || 13 ||
Those who are destroyers of their own country and highway robbers —

children.text: teṣāṃ sarvasvam ādāya bhūyo nindāṃ prakalpayet || 14 ||
children.translated_text: their entire property should be confiscated, and further public disgrace should be imposed. || 14 ||
Thieves apprehended on suspicion but without stolen goods should be examined;
through various threats and stratagems of fear, they should be made to confess as they actually did. || 15 ||

children.text: deśaṃ kālaṃ diśaṃ jātiṃ nāma vā sampratiśrayam |
children.translated_text: The place, time, direction, caste, name, or associates,

children.text: kṛtyaṃ karmakarā vā syuḥ praṣṭavyās te vinigrahe || 16 ||
children.translated_text: the deed, and the accomplices — these should be asked during interrogation. || 16 ||
From differences in voice, expression, and appearance, from suspicious statements,
from being seen at wrong places and times, and from failure to account for one's clothes,
from unexplained expenditure, from previous thefts, from association with wicked persons —

children.text: leśair apy avagantavyā na hoḍhenaiva kevalam || 18 ||
children.translated_text: guilt should be inferred even from slight indications, not solely from recovered stolen goods. || 18 ||

children.text: dasyuvṛtte yadi nare śaṅkā syāt taskare 'pi vā |
children.translated_text: If there is suspicion regarding a man engaged in brigandage or theft,

children.text: yadi spṛśyeta leśena kāryaḥ syāc chapathaḥ tataḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: if he is touched by even a slight indication, then an oath should be administered. || 19 ||
Those who provide food to thieves, as well as those who give fire and water,
those who give shelter, those who guide them, and likewise those who give testimony in their defense —

children.text: kretāraś caiva bhāṇḍānāṃ pratigrāhiṇa eva ca |
children.translated_text: those who buy their goods and those who receive stolen property —

children.text: samadaṇḍāḥ smṛtā hy ete ye ca pracchādayanti tān || 21 ||
children.translated_text: all these are declared to merit equal punishment, as also those who conceal them. || 21 ||
Provincial governors and feudal lords who are charged with authority in the provinces,

children.text: abhyāghāteṣu madhyasthā yathā caurās tathaiva te || 22 ||
children.translated_text: if they remain indifferent during attacks, they are to be treated like thieves themselves. || 22 ||

children.text: gocare yasya muṣyeta tena caurāḥ prayatnataḥ |
children.translated_text: In whose jurisdiction a robbery occurs, by him the thieves should be diligently

children.text: mṛgyā dāpyo 'nyathā moṣaṃ padaṃ yadi na nirgatam || 23 ||
children.translated_text: searched for; otherwise he should pay for the theft, if the trail has not left his territory. || 23 ||

children.text: nirgate tu pade tasmin naṣṭe 'nyatra nipātite |
children.translated_text: But when the trail has passed beyond his territory and the stolen goods are lost elsewhere,

children.text: sāmantān mārgapālāṃś ca dikpālāṃś caiva dāpayet || 24 ||
children.translated_text: the neighboring feudal lords, highway guards, and border officials should be made to pay. || 24 ||

children.text: gṛhe vai muṣite rājā cauragrāhāṃs tu dāpayet |
children.translated_text: When a house is robbed, the king should make the thief-catchers pay,

children.text: ārakṣakān rāṣṭrikāṃś ca yadi cauro na labhyate || 25 ||
children.translated_text: as well as the watchmen and provincial officers, if the thief is not found. || 25 ||

children.text: yadi vā dāpyamānānāṃ tasmin moṣe tu saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Or if there is doubt among those who are being made to pay regarding that theft,
the victim should be made to take an oath regarding the theft, for the purpose of verification. || 26 ||
When a non-thief is made to pay for a theft, for the purpose of verifying the crime,

children.text: caure labdhe labheyus te dviguṇaṃ pratipāditāḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: and the thief is later found, those who paid should receive double restitution. || 27 ||
The stolen property should be diligently restored in its original form;

children.text: tadabhāve tu mūlyaṃ syād daṇḍaṃ dāpyaś ca tatsamam || 28 ||
children.translated_text: in its absence, the monetary value should be paid, and a fine equal to that amount should be imposed. || 28 ||
For the theft of wood, stalks, grass, and similar items, of earthen articles,
of bamboo and wicker vessels, of cane, sinew, bone, and leather,
of vegetables, greens, and roots, of fruits and flowers,
of milk products and sugarcane derivatives, and of salt and oil —
of cooked food, prepared dishes, liquors, and meat,
for all items of small value, the fine is five times the value. || 31 ||
For items measured by weight, measure, and counting —
for those of higher value than the foregoing, the fine is ten times the value. || 32 ||
For one who steals more than ten <s>kumbhas</s> (pots) of grain, the punishment is death;

children.text: nyūnaṃ tv ekādaśaguṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dāpyo 'bravīn manuḥ || 33 ||
children.translated_text: for less, <s>Manu</s> has declared, a fine of eleven times the value should be imposed. || 33 ||
For gold, silver, and similar precious metals, and for the finest garments,

children.text: ratnānāṃ caiva mukhyānāṃ śatād abhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ || 34 ||
children.translated_text: and for the most valuable gems, theft exceeding a hundred in value is punishable by death. || 34 ||
For abducting a man, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) fine should be imposed;

children.text: sarvasvaṃ strīṃ tu harataḥ kanyāṃ tu harato vadhaḥ || 35 ||
children.translated_text: for abducting a woman, confiscation of all property; for abducting a maiden, death. || 35 ||
For stealing large animals, the highest <s>sāhasa</s> (violence) fine is imposed;
the middle fine for medium animals, and the lowest fine for stealing small animals. || 36 ||
The lowest fine begins at twenty-four, and the highest reaches ninety-six;

children.text: śatāni pañca tu paro madhyamo dviśatāvaraḥ || 37 ||
children.translated_text: five hundred is the highest, and two hundred is the middle fine. || 37 ||
The highest fine should be known as one thousand, beginning from five hundred;

children.text: trividhaḥ sāhaseṣv eva daṇḍaḥ proktaḥ svayambhuvā || 38 ||
children.translated_text: this threefold system of fines in cases of violence was declared by <s>Svayambhū</s> (Manu). || 38 ||
In the first degree of breaking joints, the punishment is cutting off the fingers and thumb;

children.text: dvitīye caiva taccheṣaṃ daṇḍaḥ pūrvaś ca sāhasaḥ || 39 ||
children.translated_text: in the second degree, the rest [of the hand is cut], and the fine is the first <s>sāhasa</s> (level of violence). || 39 ||
For [stealing] cows belonging to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, there should be cutting off of the foot;
but for one who habitually steals a female slave, half the foot should be cut off. || 40 ||
With whatever particular limb a thief commits the act,

children.text: tat tad evāsya chettavyaṃ tan manor anuśāsanam || 41 ||
children.translated_text: that very limb of his should be cut off — this is the instruction of <s>Manu</s>. || 41 ||
For a graver offense a heavier [punishment], and for a lighter one again [a lighter punishment];

children.text: stene nipātayed daṇḍaṃ na yathā prathame tathā || 42 ||
children.translated_text: the king should impose punishment on a thief, not in the same way as in the first [offense]. || 42 ||
<s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s> declared ten places of punishment

children.text: triṣu varṇeṣu yāni syur brāhmaṇo rakṣitaḥ sadā || 43 ||
children.translated_text: which apply to the three <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), while the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is always protected. || 43 ||

children.text: upastham udaraṃ jihvā hastau pādau ca pañcamam |
children.translated_text: The genitals, the belly, the tongue, the hands, and the feet as the fifth,

children.text: cakṣur nāsā ca karṇau ca dhanaṃ dehas tathaiva ca || 44 ||
children.translated_text: the eyes, the nose, and the ears, wealth, and also the body. || 44 ||
Having ascertained the offense, and the place and time in truth,
and having considered the motive and consequences, one should impose these punishments. || 45 ||

children.text: na mitrakāraṇād rājñā vipulād vā dhanāgamāt |
children.translated_text: The king should not, on account of friendship or great acquisition of wealth,
release a violent criminal who has abandoned [all moral restraint] — so declared <s>Manu</s>. || 46 ||

children.text: yāvān avadhyasya vadhe tāvān vadhyasya mokṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: As great is the sin in slaying one who should not be slain, so great is the sin in releasing one who should be slain;

children.text: bhavaty adharmo nṛpater dharmas tu viniyacchataḥ || 47 ||
children.translated_text: this is the <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) of the king, while <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) belongs to the one who restrains [criminals]. || 47 ||

children.text: na jātu brāhmaṇaṃ hanyāt sarvapāpeṣv api sthitam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should never be killed, even if he is engaged in all sins;

children.text: nirvāsaṃ kārayet kāmam iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ || 48 ||
children.translated_text: the king may at most banish him — this is the established <s>dharma</s> (law). || 48 ||

children.text: sarvasvaṃ vā hared rājā caturthaṃ vāvaśeṣayet |
children.translated_text: The king may confiscate all his property or leave him a fourth [of it],
mindful of the <s>dharma</s> (duty) toward dependents — this is the rule of <s>Prājāpatya</s> (relating to Prajāpati). || 49 ||
For the offense of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, branding is prescribed in four [cases]:,
for defiling the teacher's bed, drinking liquor, theft, and injuring a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. || 50 ||

children.text: gurutalpe bhagaḥ kāryaḥ surāpāne dhvajaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: For defiling the teacher's bed, [the brand of] a female organ should be made; for drinking liquor, a tavern sign is prescribed;

children.text: steye tu śvapadaṃ kṛtvā śikhipittena kūṭayet || 51 ||
children.translated_text: for theft, [the brand of] a dog's foot should be made, and it should be stamped with a peacock's feather. || 51 ||
A headless man [i.e., the figure of a man without a head] should be branded on the forehead of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-slayer,

children.text: asambhāṣyaś ca kartavyas tan manor anuśāsanam || 52 ||
children.translated_text: and he should be made an outcast — this is the instruction of <s>Manu</s>. || 52 ||
A thief should go to the king, running with hair unbound,

children.text: ācakṣāṇena tatsteyam evaṃ kartāsmi śādhi mām || 53 ||
children.translated_text: declaring his theft [saying]: 'I have done this; punish me.' || 53 ||
By this [confession], the thief becomes purified through the acknowledgment of his own deed;

children.text: rājānaṃ tat spṛśed ena utsṛjantaṃ sakilbiṣam || 54 ||
children.translated_text: the sin would touch the king who releases [the thief] while he is still guilty. || 54 ||

children.text: rājabhir dhṛtadaṇḍās tu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Men who have been punished by kings after committing sins,

children.text: nirmalāḥ svargam āyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā || 55 ||
children.translated_text: go to heaven purified, like the virtuous and meritorious. || 55 ||

children.text: śāsanād vā vimokṣād vā steno mucyate kilbiṣāt |
children.translated_text: Either by punishment or by release, a thief is freed from guilt;

children.text: aśāsanāt tu tad rājā stenasyāpnoti kilbiṣam || 56 ||
children.translated_text: but by not punishing, the king incurs the guilt of the thief. || 56 ||

children.text: gurur ātmavatāṃ śāstā śāstā rājā durātmanām |
children.translated_text: The preceptor is the discipliner of the self-controlled; the king is the discipliner of the wicked;
and <s>Yama Vaivasvata</s> is the discipliner of those whose sins are concealed. || 57 ||

children.text: aṣṭāpādyaṃ tu śūdrasya steye bhavati kilbiṣam |
children.translated_text: For a <s>Śūdra</s>, the guilt in theft is eight-fold;

children.text:
dvir aṣṭāpādyaṃ vaiśyasya dvātriṃśat kṣatriyasya tu || 58
                            ||
children.translated_text: for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, sixteen-fold; and for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, thirty-two-fold. || 58 ||
For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, sixty-four-fold — so declared <s>Manu Svāyambhuva</s>;

children.text: tatrāpi ca viśeṣeṇa vidvatsv abhyadhikaṃ bhavet || 59 ||
children.translated_text: and in particular, for the learned, it should be even greater. || 59 ||

children.text: śārīraś cārthadaṇḍaś ca daṇḍas tu dvividhaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Punishment is said to be of two kinds: corporal and pecuniary;

children.text: śārīrā daśadhā proktā arthadaṇḍās tv anekadhā || 60 ||
children.translated_text: corporal punishments are declared to be of ten kinds, and pecuniary fines of many kinds. || 60 ||

children.text: kākaṇyādis tv arthadaṇḍaḥ sarvasvāntas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The pecuniary fine begins with a <s>kākaṇī</s> (small copper coin) and extends up to confiscation of all property;

children.text: śārīras tv avarodhādir jīvitāntas tathaiva ca || 61 ||
children.translated_text: the corporal punishment begins with imprisonment and extends up to taking of life. || 61 ||

children.text: kākaṇyādis tu yo daṇḍaḥ sa tu māṣāparaḥ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The fine that begins with a <s>kākaṇī</s> has a <s>māṣa</s> (bean-weight) as its upper limit;

children.text: māṣāvarādyo yaḥ proktaḥ kārṣāpaṇaparas tu saḥ || 62 ||
children.translated_text: that which begins with a <s>māṣa</s> and below has a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> as its upper limit. || 62 ||
That which begins above the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> has four <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> as its upper limit;
another begins with two and has eight as its upper limit; another begins with three and has twelve as its upper limit. || 63 ||

children.text: kārṣāpaṇādyā ye proktāḥ sarve te syuś caturguṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those fines that are declared beginning with the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> are all to be quadrupled;

children.text: evam anye tu vijñeyāḥ prāk ca te pūrvasāhasāt || 64 ||
children.translated_text: the others are to be understood in the same way, and they are [all] below the first <s>sāhasa</s> (level of violence). || 64 ||
The <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> in the southern region is a silver [coin];

children.text: paṇair nibaddhaḥ pūrvasyāṃ ṣoḍaśaiva paṇāḥ sa tu || 65 ||
children.translated_text: in the eastern region, it is reckoned in <s>paṇas</s> — sixteen <s>paṇas</s> make one [kārṣāpaṇa]. || 65 ||

children.text: māṣo viṃśatibhāgas tu jñeyaḥ kārṣāpaṇasya tu |
children.translated_text: A <s>māṣa</s> should be known as one-twentieth of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>;

children.text: kākaṇī tu caturbhāgo māṣasya ca paṇasya ca || 66 ||
children.translated_text: a <s>kākaṇī</s> is one-fourth of a <s>māṣa</s> and also of a <s>paṇa</s>. || 66 ||

children.text: pāñcanadyāḥ pradeśe tu sañjñā yā vyāvahārikī |
children.translated_text: In the region of <s>Pāñcanada</s> (the Punjab), the commercial designation

children.text: kārṣāpaṇapramāṇaṃ tu nibaddham iha vai tayā || 67 ||
children.translated_text: of the standard of the <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> is established here by that [local convention]. || 67 ||

children.text: kārṣāpaṇo 'ṇḍikā jñeyāś catasras tās tu dhānakaḥ |
children.translated_text: A <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s> is [also called] an <s>aṇḍikā</s>; four of those make a <s>dhānaka</s>;
twelve of those [dhānakas] of gold make a <s>dīnāra</s>, [also] called <s>citraka</s>. || 68 ||
The king should constantly and attentively follow commerce, the Vedic learning, and also the science of punishment;
he should slay by skillful means those [criminals] who are caught,
and restrain the wicked both in the city and in the countryside. || 69 ||

children.text: yadā sākṣī na vidyate vivāde vadatāṃ nṛṇām |
children.translated_text: When there is no witness in a dispute between litigating men,

children.text: tadā divyaiḥ parīkṣeta śapathaiś ca pṛthagvidhaiḥ || 1 ||
children.translated_text: then one should test [them] by ordeals and by oaths of various kinds. || 1 ||
[Swearing by] truth, vehicles, weapons, cows, seeds, and silver,
and by deities, ancestors, and feet, and by gifts and meritorious deeds — || 2 ||
for great offenses, the sovereign should administer ordeals;

children.text: alpeṣu ca naraḥ śreṣṭhaḥ śapathaiḥ śāpayen naram || 3 ||
children.translated_text: and in minor [cases], the best of men should make the person swear by oaths. || 3 ||

children.text: ete hi śapathāḥ proktāḥ sukarās svalpasaṃśaye |
children.translated_text: These oaths are declared to be easy [to perform] in cases of slight doubt;

children.text: sāhaseṣv abhiśāpe ca vidhir divyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: in cases of violence and false accusation, the procedure of ordeal is prescribed. || 4 ||
In doubtful matters of those who are accused, especially in concealed [cases],

children.text: divyaḥ pañcavidho jñeya ity āha bhagavān manuḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the ordeal should be known as fivefold — so said the venerable <s>Manu</s>. || 5 ||

children.text: dhaṭo 'gnir udakaṃ caiva viṣaṃ kośaś ca pañcamaḥ |
children.translated_text: The balance, fire, water, poison, and the sacred water as the fifth —
these are declared as the ordeals for the purification of the accused. || 6 ||
For the purification of the accused in doubtful matters, the great-souled
<s>Nārada</s> further declared these means of discerning truth and falsehood;
a wise person should make [the accused undergo] this only with the consent of the plaintiff, and not otherwise. || 7 ||
The two posts of the balance are declared to be four <s>hastas</s> (cubits) in height;

children.text: ṣaḍḍhastaṃ tu tayor dṛṣṭaṃ pramāṇaṃ parimāṇataḥ || 8 ||
children.translated_text: the beam between them is prescribed as six <s>hastas</s> in measure. || 8 ||

children.text: pādayor antaraṃ hastaṃ bhaved adhyardham eva ca |
children.translated_text: The space between the two posts should be one and a half <s>hastas</s>;
two pans should be attached with firm hooks to the balance beam. || 9 ||

children.text: tulayitvā naraṃ pūrvaṃ cihnaṃ kuryād dhaṭasya tu |
children.translated_text: Having first weighed the man, one should make a mark on the balance beam;

children.text: kakṣāsthānena taṃ tulyam avatārya tato dhaṭāt || 10 ||
children.translated_text: having lowered him from the balance to the mark at the armpit level, || 10 ||
having bound him with agreements, one should place the man [on the balance] again;

children.text:
tasminn evaṃ kṛte sā cet kakṣe sthāpya suniścalā || 11
                                ||
children.translated_text: when this has been done, the [balance] should be kept perfectly still at the armpit [mark]. || 11 ||

children.text: tulito yadi vardheta śuddhaḥ syān nātre saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: If the one being weighed rises up, he is pure — there is no doubt about this;

children.text: samo vā hīyamāno vā na viśuddho bhaven naraḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: if he remains the same or sinks down, the man is not purified. || 12 ||
By the words of <s>dharma</s> (righteous procedure), you are called <s>dhaṭa</s> (balance);

children.text: tvaṃ vetsi sarvabhūtānāṃ pāpāni sukṛtāni ca |
children.translated_text: you know the sins and merits of all beings;

children.text: tvam eva dhaṭa jānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ || 13 ||
children.translated_text: you alone, O balance, know those things which mortals do not know. || 13 ||
This man is accused in a legal dispute and is thus being weighed;

children.text: tad eva saṃśayāpannaṃ dharmatas trātum arhasi || 14 ||
children.translated_text: him, who is beset with doubt, you should protect according to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). || 14 ||

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi lohasya vidhim uttamam |
children.translated_text: Henceforth I shall declare the excellent procedure of the [hot] iron;
the circles [on the ground] should be thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) apart from one circle to another. || 15 ||
With eight circles thus, [the total distance is] two hundred and twenty-four
<s>aṅgulas</s> — so it is declared by those who perceive the true meaning of numbers. || 16 ||

children.text: kalpitair maṇḍalair evam uṣitasya śucer api |
children.translated_text: When the circles have been arranged thus, [the accused] having fasted and being pure,
should have seven leaves of the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree wrapped around his hands with thread. || 17 ||
He should place in his hands a ball of heated iron weighing fifty <s>palas</s>,

children.text:
hastābhyāṃ piṇḍam ādāya śanaiḥ saptapadaṃ vrajet || 18
                                ||
children.translated_text: and taking the ball with both hands, should walk slowly seven steps. || 18 ||

children.text: na maṇḍalam atikrāmen nāpy arvāk pādayet padam |
children.translated_text: He should not overstep a circle, nor should he place his foot short [of it];
and he should not drop [the iron] before reaching the full extent of the prescribed ground. || 19 ||
Having traversed the circles in this prescribed manner with concentration,

children.text:
adagdhaḥ sarvato yas tu sa viśuddho bhaven naraḥ || 20
                                ||
children.translated_text: he who is entirely unburned — that man is purified. || 20 ||

children.text: bhayād vā pātayate yas tv adagdho yo vibhāvyate |
children.translated_text: If one drops [the iron] out of fear and is [found to be] unburned,

children.text: punas taṃ hārayel lohaṃ sthitir eṣā purātanī |
children.translated_text: he should be made to carry the iron again — this is the ancient rule;
the fire ordeal should be conducted according to this procedure, as prescribed. || 21 ||
O <s>Agni</s> (Fire), you dwell within all beings as a witness;
good deeds and evil deeds unknown to the world are known to you. || 22 ||
The hidden sins and merits of men

children.text: yathāvad eva jānīṣe na vidur yāni mānuṣāḥ || 23 ||
children.translated_text: you know exactly as they are — those things which mortals do not know. || 23 ||
This man, accused in a legal dispute, desires purification;

children.text: tad enaṃ saṃśayāpannaṃ dharmatas trātum arhasi || 24 ||
children.translated_text: him, who is beset with doubt, you should protect according to <s>dharma</s> (righteousness). || 24 ||

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi toyasya vidhim uttamam |
children.translated_text: Hereafter I shall declare the excellent procedure of water;
with a bow that is not too strong, three arrows should be shot. || 25 ||

children.text: madhyamas tu śaro grāhyaḥ puruṣeṇa yavīyasā |
children.translated_text: The middle arrow should be retrieved by the fastest man;

children.text:
pratyānītasya tasyātha sa viśuddho bhaven naraḥ || 26
                                ||
children.translated_text: if [the accused] is brought back [from the water] by the time [the arrow is retrieved], that man is purified. || 26 ||

children.text: anyathā na viśuddhaḥ syād ekāṅgam api darśayet |
children.translated_text: Otherwise he is not purified — even if he shows a single limb [above water];

children.text:
sthānād anyatra vā gacched yasmin pūrvaṃ niveṣitaḥ || 27
                                ||
children.translated_text: or if he moves from the place where he was originally stationed. || 27 ||

children.text: striyas tu na balāt kāryā na pumān api durbalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Women should not be forced [to undergo this], nor a weak man;

children.text: bhīrutvād yoṣito mṛtyuḥ kṛśasyāpi balāt kuryāt |
children.translated_text: death [may come] to women from fear, and also to one who is frail if forced;

children.text:
sahasā prāpnuyāt sarvāṃs tasmād etān na majjayet || 28
                                ||
children.translated_text: they might suddenly suffer all [consequences] — therefore these should not be submerged. || 28 ||
In the middle of the water, having firmly grasped the person's thighs, [the test is conducted]. || 29
For the determination of truth and falsehood, water and fire are the clearest [judges];

children.text: yataś cāgnir abhūd asmāt tatas toyaṃ viśiṣyate || 30 ||
children.translated_text: and since fire originated from water, water is considered superior. || 30 ||
The purification of the accused is performed by those who know the true principles of <s>dharma</s> (law);

children.text: tasmāt satyena bhagavañ jaleśa trātum arhasi || 31 ||
children.translated_text: therefore, O venerable lord of waters, you should protect [this person] through truth. || 31 ||

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi viṣasya vidhim uttamam |
children.translated_text: Hereafter I shall declare the excellent procedure of poison;

children.text: tulayitvā viṣaṃ pūrvaṃ deyam etad dhimāgame || 32 ||
children.translated_text: having weighed the poison beforehand, it should be administered in the cold season. || 32 ||

children.text: na pūrvāhṇe na madhyāhne na sandhyāyāṃ tu dharmavit |
children.translated_text: A knower of <s>dharma</s> (law) should not [administer it] in the forenoon, nor at midday, nor at twilight;
nor should he administer it in autumn, summer, spring, or the rainy season. || 33 ||

children.text: bhagnaṃ ca dāritaṃ caiva dhūpitaṃ miśritaṃ tathā |
kālakūṭam alambuṃ ca viṣaṃ yatnena varjayet || 34 ||
children.translated_text: <s>kālakūṭa</s> (a deadly poison) and <s>alambu</s> — these poisons should be carefully avoided. || 34 ||
That [poison] which comes from <s>Śṛṅga</s> and the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas), endowed with fragrance, color, and flavor, is recommended;
it should be given by the king to one accused of a great offense, with the desire to ascertain the truth. || 35 ||
It should not be [given] to children, the sick, or the aged, nor to those guilty of minor offenses;

children.text:
viṣasya tu yavān sapta dadyāc chodye ghṛtaplutān || 36
                                ||
children.translated_text: seven grains of poison should be given to the accused, soaked in clarified butter. || 36 ||

children.text: viṣasya palaṣaḍbhāgād bhāgo viṃśatimas tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of one-sixth of a <s>pala</s> (unit of weight) of poison, the twentieth part

children.text:
tam aṣṭabhāgahīnaṃ tu śodhye dadyād ghṛtaplutam || 37
                                ||
children.translated_text: diminished by an eighth — that [amount] should be given to the accused, soaked in clarified butter. || 37 ||
In the prescribed manner, having been approved after touching <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
and having fasted, he should eat [the poison] in the presence of the gods and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 38 ||
If the poison is digested easily, free from convulsions and exhaustion,

children.text:
viśuddham iti taṃ jñātvā rājā satkṛtya mokṣayet || 39
                                ||
children.translated_text: having ascertained him to be purified, the king should honor and release him. || 39 ||

children.text: tvaṃ viṣa brahmaṇaḥ putraḥ satyadharmaratau sthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: O poison, you are the son of <s>Brahman</s>, established in truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteousness);
purify this man from sin — through truth, become nectar for him. || 40 ||

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi kośasya vidhim uttamam || 41 ||
children.translated_text: Hereafter I shall declare the excellent procedure of the <s>kośa</s> (sacred water ordeal). || 41 ||
In the forenoon, for one who has fasted, bathed, and wears wet garments,
who has a <s>śūka</s> (sacred grass) and is free from vice, the drinking of the <s>kośa</s> (sacred water) is prescribed. || 42 ||

children.text: yadbhaktaḥ so 'bhiyuktaḥ syāt taddaivatyaṃ tu pāyayet |
children.translated_text: Whichever deity the accused is devoted to, he should be made to drink [water consecrated to] that deity;

children.text: saptāhād yasya dṛśyate dvisaptāhena vā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: if [a sign] appears within seven days, or else within fourteen days,

children.text:
pratyātmikaṃ tu yatkiñcit saiva tasya vibhāvanā || 43
                                ||
children.translated_text: whatever personal [affliction befalls him], that itself is the proof [of guilt]. || 43 ||

children.text: dvisaptāhāt paraṃ yasya mahad vā vaikṛtaṃ bhavet |
children.translated_text: If after fourteen days, [even] something great or an abnormality occurs,
the wise should not hold him liable, because the prescribed time has passed. || 44 ||
For a great offender, one devoid of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), an ungrateful person, a eunuch, or a despicable person,
for atheists, <s>vrātyas</s> (outcaste Āryans), and slaves, the <s>kośa</s> (sacred water) ordeal should be avoided. || 45 ||
A knower of <s>dharma</s> (law) should administer the five ordeals in the prescribed manner

children.text: dadyād rājābhiyuktānāṃ pretya ceha ca nandati || 46 ||
children.translated_text: to the accused — [such a king] rejoices both in this world and the next. || 46 ||

children.text: na viṣaṃ brāhmaṇe dadyān na lohaṃ kṣatriyo haret |
children.translated_text: Poison should not be given to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, nor should a <s>Kṣatriya</s> carry the [hot] iron;

children.text:
na nimajjyāpsu vaiśyaś ca śūdraḥ kośaṃ na pāyayet || 47
                                ||
children.translated_text: a <s>Vaiśya</s> should not be submerged in water, and a <s>Śūdra</s> should not be made to drink the <s>kośa</s> (sacred water). || 47 ||

children.text: varṣāsu na viṣaṃ dadyāt hemante nāpsu majjayet |
children.translated_text: One should not administer poison in the rainy season, nor submerge [anyone] in water in winter;

children.text: na lohaṃ hārayed grīṣme na kośaṃ pāyayen niśi || 48 ||
children.translated_text: one should not make [anyone] carry the [hot] iron in summer, nor make [anyone] drink the <s>kośa</s> (sacred water) at night. || 48 ||
